items.statement: Non-broking revenues now contribute 40% of gross revenue, up from previous periods
items.quote: Importantly, our revenue profile continues to become increasingly diversified, while our core trading platform remains our largest acquisition engine, contributing close to 60% of our gross revenues, the remaining 40% now comes from complementary businesses such as client funding, distribution, depository, wealth and other asset management businesses.

items.statement: Client funding book has limited risk with 83% exposure below ₹100,000 per client and 85% portfolio less than 30 days old
items.quote: Equally important is the quality of our assets. 83% of our client funding exposure is below ₹ 100,000 per client, while 85% of the portfolio is less than 30 years old (to be read as less than 30 days old), supported by fully collateralized client holdings and negligible delinquency.

items.statement: Board approved first interim dividend of ₹1 per share for FY27 with record date July 21, 2026
items.quote: I am also pleased to share that the Board has approved our first interim dividend for this financial year of ₹ 1 per share with the record date being July 21, 2026.

items.statement: Wealth and AMC businesses together caused a 4% operating margin decrement (400 bps) this quarter due to IPL spends and seasonality.
items.quote: Overall, as far as the operating margin decrement is concerned, it's about 4% for both the AMC and the wealth businesses put together from the overall.

items.statement: Full-year burn from Wealth and AMC expected to be 3-3.5% of operating margin.
items.quote: But overall, I think we will be in the range of about 3%, 3.5% as at the financial year.

items.statement: Wealth and AMC businesses expected to incrementally break even in 3-4 years.
items.quote: As of today, as I said, in the past also we mentioned that from the beginning, we are contemplating in about 3 to 4 years this business should incrementally breakeven.

items.statement: Active AP count is approximately 10,000; plans to expand AP channel into multi-product distribution including mutual funds and insurance.
items.quote: Approximately think of the number of APs as about 10,000 is what you should think of. And I think your next question was about mutual fund distribution?

items.statement: Personal loan distribution works with 7 lending partners across banks, large NBFCs, and fintechs; partners scaled or offloaded based on performance.
items.quote: On the PL side, we work with 7 lenders right now, and over time, some of the lenders come in and they scale with us and some of the lenders who don't scale with us, we sort of offload them.

items.statement: Loan Against Securities (LAS) via own NBFC is in COG pilot mode; expected to scale to full base in next 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: We are in COG mode right now. As and when we get more experience from the customers, we'll open up the entire base, and in next two or three quarters, you should see that business becoming big.

items.statement: Cash realization increased due to November pricing change, shift to higher ticket sizes (>₹20k), and uptake of new value-added assisted plan.
items.quote: If you look at it over a period of time, there was -- in November, we had made a small pricing change. That definitely has an impact. But recently, quarter-over-quarter, what we have seen is 2 major factors, one is the change in the ticket sizes, right, greater than 20,000 versus less than 20,000 orders.

items.statement: No further increase in cash realization baked in; can change quarter-to-quarter based on order mix.
items.quote: Look, it's very hard to predict, especially on the mix side. So I wouldn't bake in any further increase from here, and it can change quarter-to-quarter, depending on how the mix of orders come in.

items.statement: Client acquisition moderation reflects softer industry trends (CDSL data); spend adjusted based on client quality and LTV, not cost cutting.
items.quote: If you see what is sort of the CDSL number for client acquisition, that itself actually has been softer last few months. But the way we look at our client acquisition is that we are looking at what kind of client segments are available.

items.statement: Employee productivity expected to increase over next 2-3 years driven by AI and efficiency; no specific headcount guidance given.
items.quote: But overall, over the next 2-3 years, you're definitely going to see the world change. There is AI, other tools, all of that. And we'll continue to stay on that trajectory. And overall, I don't want to give a guidance on employee count, but you will see employee productivity increase for sure.

items.statement: Wealth management AUM split: UHNI (>₹50 Cr) and ₹1-50 Cr segment (~₹3,400-3,500 Cr); strategy focuses on tech-RM integration and product parity across segments.
items.quote: Now as far as the second business is concerned, where currently we are at close to about ₹ 3,400 crores, ₹ 3,500 crores of AUM, that's the business which is built more granularly.

items.statement: U.S. equities offering upgrade planned with GIFT City license; no pricing disclosed yet; LRS limit of $250,000 applies.
items.quote: We got a GIFT City license also on that front, as you would have seen. We can't talk about any pricing at this time because we haven't launched the product.

items.statement: Restricted basket (RSM) is an internal risk management policy beyond SEBI requirements; under continuous review.
items.quote: In terms of the risk, as you know, we have our own risk management on top of what SEBI would prescribe because brokers have their own requirement to do things.

items.statement: Mutual fund business seeing momentum in active SIPs; AI-driven query resolution, UX/UI improvements, and assisted distributor focus to drive further growth.
items.quote: We are seeing momentum, and there is more momentum coming on that front for sure.

items.statement: No plans for stock advisory; Ionic wealth platform offers full solution set.
items.quote: Look, not at this time. We do -- of course, we have RAs and we provide calls, as you know, those are different. But no plans on the stock advisory front.

items.statement: IPL costs classified as long-term branding, not client acquisition cost; acquisition cost creeps up during IPL but normalizes after.
items.quote: Look, the IPL costs are really not a acquisition cost. It's a branding cost, very, very long-term cost. So that has to be kept very much out of it.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at 25-30% YoY, maintaining Q1 run rate
items.quote: We see, yes, so 25%, 30% growth is what we forecasted, and that's what we stick to. So yes, in pure mathematics terms, we are saying that, yes, we should maintain this run rate.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 20-22% despite Q1 margin pressure
items.quote: As I always say, so unfortunately, we have lost 1 quarter with a little lesser margin, but I would still stick to 20%, 22% margins in guidance.

items.statement: Electrolyte Salts FY27 revenue guidance maintained at INR40-60 crores
items.quote: It will not be up to -- so between INR40 crores to INR60 crores revenue is what we still hold the guidance.

items.statement: New greenfield facility expected to generate INR300 crore revenue at peak (1.2-1.5x asset turnover)
items.quote: we would be looking at somewhere around 1.2x to 1.5x asset turnover ratio, which means we would end up having around INR300 crores of revenue at peak utilization.

items.statement: Pharma molecules to contribute INR70-80 crore in FY27, scaling to INR200 crore at full utilization
items.quote: It should contribute around INR70 crores to INR80 crores of revenue from all these pharma molecules. And in this current financial year. And gradually, it should uptick in next financial year, too.

items.statement: Semiconductor chemical first plant-scale batch qualified by customer; 5 products in pipeline, commercialization not before Q4 2028
items.quote: our first batch produced on commercial plant scale was delivered to the customer during this quarter, and this batch has been successfully qualified by the customer.

items.statement: SDA demand strengthening with Euro 7 implementation; geographical expansion beyond Europe expected over 3-5 years
items.quote: The implementation of Euro 7 standards has now begun translating into revenue and there is a very visible customer demand, validating the opportunity that we have been anticipating.

items.statement: Price pass-through initiated over last 40-50 days after raw material cost spikes; margins impacted by delayed pass-through
items.quote: Now we are pushing for price increase. So now we are translating that we are -- so since last, I would say, since last 40, 50 days now that price pass-on has started, customers have started accepting the higher price.

items.statement: No foreseen obstacles to FY27 guidance; customer demand visible across segments
items.quote: None of them. We don't foresee any obstacles to this year's guidance because all the demand from the customers and the segments are quite visible.

items.statement: 3-4 year CAGR revenue growth target of 20-25% from new Jolva facility commercialization
items.quote: So over the next 3 to 4 years, if you let us pick because Jolva was getting commercialized. So let us say about coming 4 years from today, we should envisage at least 20% to 25% compounded growth year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Hybrid battery customer commercialization starting Oct-Nov 2026; full scale-up expected late 2027
items.quote: Hybrid vehicle batteries customer is into the process of commercialization. So it's now just beginning to get into commercialization phase. So this should happen from October or November of this year, calendar year '26.

items.statement: Dahej site saturated; new greenfield at Jolva essential for growth beyond INR850 crore revenue
items.quote: Dahej, we are nearly saturated. We have consumed all the piece or parcel of land in Dahej. So now there is hardly anything. So very small production block is what is feasible to be made.

items.statement: Gold AUM growth guidance of 25-30% for FY27 if gold prices remain flat
items.quote: if there is no price drop, and if the price remains flat also over the year, that means, let's say, let's look at March to next March, the price would have remained flat, even then we would have given a gold AUM growth of about 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Entity-level AUM growth guidance of 20-22% for FY27
items.quote: And at an entity level, we are expecting to grow about 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Mortgage AUM growth guidance of 15-20% for FY27
items.quote: And the mortgage AUM will grow between 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance remains sub-1% for FY27
items.quote: Overall, Renish, the credit cost guidance remains same. At the start of the year itself, we said the credit cost guidance will be sub -1%.

items.statement: ROA expansion guidance of 20-30 bps over FY26 average ROA of 2.4%
items.quote: I had guided that we will expand the ROA by about 20 to 30 bps over the average ROA, that we had given last year. Last year, FY '26, we had given an average ROA of about 2.4%.

items.statement: Branch expansion guidance of 200 branches for FY27, with Q1 identification completed but openings deferred to Q2
items.quote: This year, we plan to add 200 branches. Our guidance remains, we have not changed our guidance. We will continue to add 200 branches Q1, we identified the premises. We did all the work, but we've not opened them.

items.statement: Gold loan disbursements grew 15% YoY to ₹6,087 Cr in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our Gold Loan business continued to lead this growth, with disbursements rising 15% YoY to ₹6,087 Cr and AUM increasing 77% YoY to ₹11,191 Cr.

items.statement: Mortgage disbursements grew 4% YoY to ₹673 Cr in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our Mortgage business continued to demonstrate steady growth, with disbursements increasing 4% YoY to ₹673 Cr and AUM rising 14% YoY to ₹9,777 Cr.

items.statement: Core NII grew 12.3% QoQ and 40.6% YoY; NII net of DA grew 6.6% QoQ and 38.7% YoY
items.quote: Our Core Net Interest income grew 12.3% sequentially QOQ and 40.6% YOY. We consciously de-grew our DA income. NII (net of DA income) increased 6.6% sequentially QOQ and 38.7% YOY.

items.statement: Yields (ex-DA) grew 10 bps QoQ to 15.7% on average loan book
items.quote: Yields (exc. DA) grew QOQ sequentially by 10 bps to 15.7% on Avg loan book and 15% on Avg total assets.

items.statement: Weighted average cost of borrowing reduced 3 bps QoQ despite incremental borrowing costs being 20-30 bps higher
items.quote: we were able to bring in our Weighted average COB marginally lower QOQ by 3 bps.

items.statement: Stage 2 increased from 2.2% to 2.7% due to regulatory transition to periodic interest-due structure; viewed as optical, not asset quality concern
items.quote: Our increase in Stage II from 2.2 % to 2.7% is entirely due to this re -adjustment. We do not see any asset quality concerns due to this rise with the collateral remaining highly realizable.

items.statement: GNPA reduced 30 bps to 1.6% from 1.9% in Q4; net NPA fell below 1% for first time; provision coverage increased to 38.36%
items.quote: On asset quality, our GNPAs reduced 30 bps to 1.6% in Q1 (from 1.9% in Q4 ) and net NPA also reduced 30 bps falling marginally below 1.0% for the first time.

items.statement: No stress observed in small ticket LAP (7-35 lakh) or medium ticket LAP (35 lakh-3 cr) segments; slippages similar to previous quarter
items.quote: The segment that we operate between 7 lakhs to 35 lakhs has not seen stress in this quarter. There is another segment, which is medium ticket LAP, we operate between 35 lakhs to 3 crores. That has also not seen stress.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM at 51.4% of total AUM; expected to increase 2-3 percentage points if gold grows 2-3% faster than mortgage
items.quote: See, we track it as a percentage of our AUM, it is about 51.4%. I will just have to do the arithmetic. If gold is growing at 2%, 3% higher than the other one, and that is 50% of the book. So maybe it will add another 2, 3 percentage point there.

items.statement: Gold tonnage grew 1% QoQ in Q1; expect tonnage growth of 10-12% for full year with pickup in Q3-Q4
items.quote: have shown in the past 5 years, our tonnage growth has been consistently about 10% to 12%. Last year also we gave a tonnage growth of 12%. The first quart er and second quarter are usually sluggish on tonnage growth, because there are festivities in the second quarter. There are withdrawals, which happened. But Q3 and Q4, we pick up the tonnage

items.statement: True North Fund LLP exited 6.86% stake via block deal; acquired by Nomura India Equity Fund
items.quote: True North Fund LLP, a long -standing shareholder in the Company, has exited its entire holding of approximately 25.7 million equity shares, representing 6.86% of the Company's paid-up equity share capital, through a block deal ex ecuted on the stock exchange. The shares have been acquired by Nomura India Equity Fund

items.statement: Expect strong double-digit organic revenue growth for FY27 with services as primary growth engine and margin expansion supported by scale, utilization, delivery productivity, AI-led efficiency and disciplined cost management
items.quote: Based on our current visibility, we continue to expect strong double -digit organic revenue growth for FY27 with services as the primary growth engine and margin expansion supported by scale, utilization, delivery productivity, AI -led efficiency and discipl ined cost management.

items.statement: Confidence in double-digit growth has grown; do not see tapering in H2, actually see growth accelerating through the fiscal year
items.quote: So, we do not see a tapering of growth in the second half of the year. We actually see growth accelerating as we move through the quarters of this fiscal.

items.statement: Expect growth to be much greater in second half of FY27 than first half, driven by ramp-up of closed deals
items.quote: I expect growth to be much greater in the second half of the year than in the first half of the year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 16.1%, up 10 bps QoQ; services gross margin improved 120 bps, Technology Solutions margin declined 250 bps due to mix
items.quote: Resultantly, EBITDA grew 6.1% sequentially to INR267 crores, while EBITDA margin improved 10 basis points Q-o-Q to 16.1%.

items.statement: Expect quarter-over-quarter margin expansion to continue in Q2 despite wage hikes; prioritizing growth without compromising margin ambition
items.quote: Given the strong demand and the healthy deal momentum, we would seek this opportunit y to accelerate growth without compromising on our ambition of quarter -over-quarter margin expansion.

items.statement: $100 million strategic engagement with Tenneco spanning engineering, digital technologies, AI-enabled processes and operational modernization over 5 years
items.quote: The most significant win was our $100 million strategic engagement with Tenneco , which expands our relationship beyond traditional engineering services into a multiyear transformation program spanning engineering, digital technologies, AI -enabled processes and operational modernization.

items.statement: Full vehicle development program with leading Japanese automotive OEM scaling up; represents complete vehicle development for a new strategic relationship
items.quote: We continue to make strong progress on the strategically significant full vehicle development program with a leading Japanese automotive OEM that we discussed during our previous earnings call.

items.statement: Seeing broad-based improvement in demand driven by outsourcing of full vehicles and turnkey responsibility; growth across engineering, embedded software and digital
items.quote: We are seeing a broad-based improvement in demand. It's certainly very much predicated upon the outsourcing of full vehicles.

items.statement: EV investment tapering, more balanced propulsion mix (ICE, hybrid, PHEV, BEV); clarity returning after tariff uncertainty, investments resuming
items.quote: We have, over the last couple of years, start to see the investments in EVs tapering and a much more balanced proposition as far as propulsion options that our customers are building and investing in.

items.statement: Automotive non-anchor revenue $43.9M, up 6.7% QoQ and 56.3% YoY; anchor contribution to services revenue reduced to 48.9%, down 150 bps QoQ
items.quote: Automotive non -anchor revenue reached $43.9 million, growing 6.7% quarter-on-quarter and 56.3% year -on-year, reflecting continued progress in reducing customer concentration and expanding our presence across global OEM.

items.statement: Aerospace revenue ~$10.2M, up 6.4% QoQ and 38.1% YoY; IHM revenue ~$15M; targeting $100M Aerospace revenue in next 3 years at ~40% CAGR
items.quote: Our Aerospace revenues grew to approximately $10.2 million. This was up 6.4% Q-o-Q and 38.1% Y -o-Y.

items.statement: Europe revenue ~$67.9M, up 10.1% QoQ; Germany strengthening; BMW TechWorks crossed 2,000 engineers milestone
items.quote: Q1 revenue from Europe reached approximately $67.9 million , representing growth of 10.1% quarter-on-quarter and reinforcing our belief that the region will remain a significant contributor to future expansion.

items.statement: Upfront investments in talent, ramp-up, capability development, transition activities and delivery readiness for large strategic engagements and full vehicle programs in mobilization phase
items.quote: Several large strategic engagements and full vehicle programs entered the mobilization phase during Q1, requiring upfront investments in talent, ramp -up, capability development, transition activities and delivery readiness ahead of revenues re aching steady state levels.

items.statement: Temporary headwinds in parts of Germany business as customers work through restructuring and cost optimization; annual wage increase in Q2
items.quote: We are also navigating some temporary headwinds within parts of our Germany business as certain customers work through restructuring and cost optimization initiatives.

items.statement: AI strategy built on 4 priorities: transforming service delivery, building differentiated offerings, strengthening AI partnerships, delivering AI-ready talent; chromosome.ai codifying engineering knowledge
items.quote: Our AI strategy is built around 4 priorities: transforming service delivery, building differentiated offerings, strengthening AI partnerships and delivering AI-ready talent.

items.statement: TechVarsity delivered over 9,000 learning hours across GenAI, software-defined vehicles and cybersecurity to 2,000+ employees in Q1
items.quote: Through TechVarsity, our internal university, we have delivered over 9,000 learning hours across GenAI, software -defined vehicles and cybersecurity this quarter, strengthening capabilities of over 2,000 employees.

items.statement: Reiterated FY27 guidance: gross loan growth 19-21%, deposit growth 23-25%, PAT growth 80%+
items.quote: Finally, I just want to finish with Page number 23 and reiterate our guidance of gross loan growth of 19% to 21%, a deposit growth of 23% to 25%, and a PAT of 80% plus for the year.

items.statement: NIM improved to 7.5% in Q1 FY27, driven by 50bps YoY cost of funds decline and lower unsecured slippages; expected to stay steady
items.quote: Our profit for the first quarter, which is PAT, is INR155 crore. I think importantly, we have seen that our NIM has backed up now to 7.5%.

items.statement: Cost of funds at 7.4% in Q1 FY27, down 60bps YoY; expected to plateau at 7.3-7.4% range for FY27
items.quote: If you see quarter 1, 2027, we are at 7.4%. This represents a drop-off 60 bps from Q1 FY26. I do expect that 7.4% will remain nearly 7.4%, plus or minus 5 bps at best, during this year.

items.statement: MFI portfolio targeting 10-12% YoY growth in FY27; book stabilizing after 5 quarters of declining slippages
items.quote: For FY27, we are targeting the portfolio not to be aggressively growing, to about 10% to 12%. That's really the targeted growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Secured book at 72.8%, expected to reach 80% over time; five secured product lines vs one unsecured (MFI) driving mix shift
items.quote: Since we have affordable housing, micro LAP, MSME, vehicle and Gold loans, we have five product lines in secured versus one unsecured product, which is basically MFI, nothing else, it is natural to expect that we'll always have more secured loan growth than unsecured loans every passing year.

items.statement: 79.8% of unsecured portfolio under guarantee program; INR196 cr of INR214 cr net NPA covered; CGMFU claims of INR65 cr expected in Q3
items.quote: I'm happy to report that 79.8%, which is nearly 80%, of unsecured is under guarantee program. I also want to highlight to you in the last two columns, our net NPA is at INR214 crore. This is our net NPA at 30th June for unsecured. Out of this INR214 crore net NPA, INR196 crore is under the guarantee program.

items.statement: Planning 78 branch actions in FY27: 8 new, 30 splits, 40 relocations; 7 executed so far; adding 50-75 gold loan branches in next 2 quarters
items.quote: We are planning to open 78 branches. Only 8 of them are new branches, 30 are split, which means a branch really has too many more customers and we really need to split the branch for better management.

items.statement: Credit cost flat at 0.45% in Q1 FY27 vs Q4 FY26; expected to maintain at minimum same levels for remaining quarters
items.quote: On your question on credit cost, it was at 0.45% for quarter 4. It remains at 0.45% in quarter 1. It gives us great confidence because typically first quarter is a bit more of a shocker than quarter 4, and quarter 4 is always the best quarter in terms of performance.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio at 66.7-67% in Q1; expected to reduce to 63-65% range in FY27; cost grew only INR10 cr QoQ
items.quote: Cost-to-income ratio will not go below 60%. However, it will reduce. It will go around 63% to 65% range during the year.

items.statement: INR103 cr received from capital raise; INR80 cr more pending RBI approval for TVS Group; balance 75% of INR728 cr over 18 months
items.quote: Folks who have been following us do know that we did raise some capital, out of which the first INR103 crore have been received by the bank. Once the TVS Group is approved by the Reserve Bank of India, we will certainly be receiving the next INR80-odd crore, and the balance, 75% of the total INR728 crore will come over

items.statement: Gold loan book grew 13.5% QoQ to INR2,678 cr (100%+ YoY); LTV at 64%; adding 50-75 branches and increasing headcount to drive growth
items.quote: The book grew about 13.5% quarter-on-quarter. So we are sitting at about INR2,678 crore, we grew over 100% year-on-year. While gold loan prices have witnessed some correction, I mean from a risk management standpoint, we are comfortable because, on an average, across the portfolio, our LTV is 64%.

items.statement: No material impact from Iran war or El Nino; portfolio well-diversified; monitoring MFI (27% of book) with early warning indicators
items.quote: At this stage, we're not really seeing any material impact on our portfolio, we are obviously closely monitoring it, neither due to the geopolitical situation, nor even due to El Nino weather-related developments.

items.statement: CASA grew 31% YoY and 7.1% QoQ in Q1; targeting CASA ratio of ~20% for FY27; government CASA deposits not yet returned but bank re-empaneled
items.quote: We want to have a CASA mix of close to around 20%, CASA ratio, for the year. That's the projection which we have.

items.statement: Volumes in FY27 likely to remain at same level as FY26 if situation remains same
items.quote: Given the current scenario, with still the [inaudible 00:18:46] that's going on, but we are working on multiple strategies beyond the MENA region. On the domestic front also, some strength in water sector from state-driven projects where we are seeing some uptake improvement in first quarter, and this is likely to co ntinue. So this is our estimate that if the situation remains same, volume-wise w

items.statement: Middle East monthly dispatches expected at 10,000-12,000 tons until sea route reopens
items.quote: In the Middle East, we -- the situation is a little bit different. On the domestic front, we have seen some improvement. But in the Middle East, the monthly dispatches should remain in the same range, like 10,000 to 12,000 ton per month.

items.statement: Peak term debt estimated at INR3,500 crores after Middle East projects completion
items.quote: Once the projects are over, we are estimating that term debt should remain in the range of INR3,500 crores approximately.

items.statement: Abu Dhabi subsidiary order book USD188 million, 177,000 tons, visibility 3-4 quarters
items.quote: as of 30th June '26, the subsidiary hold an order book of approximately USD 188 millio n. In terms of volume, it is 1,7 7,000 ton, which ensures operational visibility for next three to four

items.statement: Margins pressured in H1 FY27 due to lower utilization; improvement expected in H2 FY27
items.quote: We expect that this may get arrested, maybe in a couple of months when we find, let's say, options and solutions to cater to the domestic demand as well as the Middle East demand. So, our -- even if we are not able to, let's say, we don't -- normally, we don't give the forward-looking numbers. But in general, we expect that, what we have done in the first quarter, maybe second quarter may also be

items.statement: India prioritizing energy security with new pipeline tenders expected following March 2026 government mandate
items.quote: Currently, India is also prioritizing energy security with new pipeline tenders expected in coming quarters that follows a landmark March '26 government mandate designed to fast track nationwide pipe gas rolled out by eliminating bureaucratic delays, exces sive fees and local bottlenecks through time-bound central

items.statement: Nashik seamless pipe utilization expected 70,000-80,000 tons quarterly from October 2026 after API license reinstatement
items.quote: So it will be somewhere in 70,000 to 80,000 tons, yes, definitely, quarterly.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflict blocking Strait of Hormuz suspended all outward shipments to MENA since March 2026
items.quote: Geopolitical situation between U.S. and Iran brought MENA region trade to a standstill this quarter by blocking the Strait of Hormuz. A short-lived diplomatic breakthrough in mid-June offered some hope for recovery. However, the subsequent collapse of these peace talks has limited our short -term visibility.

items.statement: API license suspended Jan-Jun 2026, reinstated mid-June 2026, limited certified oil & gas order participation
items.quote: The company's seamless pipe business was additionally impacted because of its API license remains suspended from January 2026 until mid-June '26. This limited our ability to participate in certified oil and gas orders during the quarter.

items.statement: Long-term debt INR526 crores standalone (INR500 crores LIC NCD repayable FY28,29,30); consolidated long-term debt INR536 crores
items.quote: As of 30th June 2026, the standalone net debt narrowed to INR2,345 crores as that -- and -- versus INR2,453 crores as of 31st March 2026. This includes INR526 crores of long-term debt. This is primarily INR500 crores out of this is from LIC, NCD which is repayable in 3 equal installments in FY28, '29 and '30.

items.statement: Jindal Hunting JV revenue INR5 crores, loss INR5.3 crores in Q1 FY27 due to API license suspension; improvement expected
items.quote: Jindal Hunting, which is a joint venture between Hunting Energy Services, Singapore, and Jindal Saw, Jindal Saw holds 51% in this company. It generated a revenue of INR5 crores and a loss -- it is first time it incurred a loss of INR 5.3 crores in the Q1.

items.statement: Court case Jindal ITF vs NTPC arguments closed at Delhi High Court double bench; order expected within 2 months
items.quote: The arguments from both sides are closed at the double bench of Delhi High Court and the order has been reserved. We expect the order to be announced in next -- maximum two months' time.

items.statement: Expects to continue similar performance if conditions remain same; no formal guidance given
items.quote: Well, it will not be appropriate to give any guidance like that, but we are expecting that if all the things remain the same, we continue to -- we hope to continue to do in a similar way.

items.statement: 600 TPD expansion at existing location in full swing, commissioning expected Q4 FY27
items.quote: Work on our ongoing expansion of 600 ton per day at existing location is in full swing, and we expect the commissioning of the project in Q4 FY27.

items.statement: Construction completion targeted by December 2026, both furnaces SG4 and SG5 to be commissioned by March 2027
items.quote: So it is going on as per the plan, and we hope to complete the construction and everything by December '26 and commission the project within first quarter, that is January to March '27.

items.statement: EBITDA margin consistently above 33% for fourth quarter in a row; expects further operational efficiency improvements
items.quote: EBITDA margin has consistently stayed above 33% for the fourth quarter in a row. We continue to work on efficiency improvements and cost reductions and expect further enhancement in the operational efficiencies.

items.statement: Average ex-factory price increased to INR160.30 per mm per sqm including INR9.50 fuel surcharge; surcharge being reduced as fuel costs ease
items.quote: The major increase in sales value came from the selling prices as the average ex -factory price during the quarter increased to INR160.30 per millimeter, per square meter as compared to INR138.10 in the corresponding quarter and INR150.20 in the preceding quarter.

items.statement: Fuel surcharge of INR9.50 included in price; already started curtailing surcharge as fuel costs decline
items.quote: Yes, you're right that INR9.50 was the full fuel surcharge, which we had invoiced to our customers, and that is included in INR160. So which is why you see that the realization from INR150 has increased to INR160 in this quarter compared to the previous quarter.

items.statement: Domestic solar glass capacity 2,600 TPD vs 11,000 TPD requirement; demand robust with 75% supply gap even after expansion to 7,700 TPD by March 2027
items.quote: The 62 gigawatt module requirement translate s to solar glass capacity of about 11,000 ton per day against which local solar glass capacity stands at 2,600 ton per day, equivalent to 18 gigawatt, and the country depends on import s for the balance.

items.statement: Rooftop solar business launched with internal target of INR36 crore revenue in FY27; Q1 revenue INR1.3 crore; EBITDA margins in single digits

items.statement: Loan growth seen across mortgages, rural, personal loans, business banking, and corporate; no specific segment targets

items.statement: Net credit cost ~30-32 bps of average loans; seasonal agri NPLs in Q1/Q3 even out over year; no specific concern on asset quality based on current info
items.quote: Seasonally, in Q1 and Q3 of every year, we do see higher NP As from the agri -related lending and the credit costs are slightly higher. But they even out over the rest of the year. And even in this quarter, our net credit cost is just about 30, 32 basis points of average loans.

items.statement: Contingency provisions of ₹13,100 crore held at June 30, 2026

items.statement: ECL effective April 1, 2027; no material ongoing impact expected; adequate provisions for transition

items.statement: AI investment in early days; calibrated approach focusing on governance, long-term value; no material impact on headcount expected; continue investing in human and technology capital
items.quote: Because these are early days in AI. As I did mention, we have calibrated our approach. We look at cost, we look at the risk, and we look at the benefits. Our final objective is to make the journeys of our customers simpler. I think there are enough opportunities out there. items.statement: Invested in enterprise AI platform for development, hosting, deployment of AI and GenAI use cases across portfolio monitoring, onboarding, fraud detection, document extraction, customer servicing
items.quote: The Bank has invested in an enterprise AI platform, which serves as a secure environment f or development, hosting and deployment of AI and Generative AI use cases. The Bank continues to invest in AI and Generative AI use cases across areas such as portfolio monitoring, customer onboarding, fraud detection, document extraction and summarisation, and customer servicing among others.

items.statement: Corporate pipeline has adequate opportunities; Q1 opened fairly good number of opportunities; decisions based on 360-degree relationship and risk-reward
items.quote: As I mentioned, we have been engaging with our corporate customers over a long period of time and whenever we get opportunities which meet our risk and reward thresholds, we are happy to lend to them. So, there are adequate opportunities and this quarter did open up fairly good number of opportunities.

items.statement: Loan growth momentum continues to be pretty good; average year-on-year growth will be somewhat lower due to base effects but incremental momentum remains strong
items.quote: Average loan growth on a year-on-year basis will be somewhat lower, but as I mentioned earlier, higher loan growth this quarter is reflective of the increase in loan growth in the system and both the banks and the system is off the base of Q1 of last year. So, there could be some base effect, but incremental momentum continues to be pretty strong.

items.statement: NIM expected to remain range-bound assuming no policy rate changes; FCNR(B) mobilization may have some NIM impact over time but is earnings positive
items.quote: Based on current conditions and assuming no policy rate movements, I would say it should be range bound. As we go along, we'll also have to factor in sort of the impact of the FCNR deposit mobilization and the related leverage where there could be some impact on margins, but that is something that will happen over a period of time. In any case, the program itself has significant advantages. So tha

items.statement: FCNR(B) all-in cost after hedging estimated at 6.30-6.40%, competitive versus wholesale rates
items.quote: From a cost effectiveness perspective, 6%. If you look at kind of the all-in cost after hedging the coupon, etc., it will be somewhere maybe 6.30-6.40%, which is, of course, lower than wholesale rates and it will be competitive compared to the wholesale rates.

items.statement: Corporate loan growth driven by bond market shift, working capital utilization, and liquidity buffering; no meaningful increase in fresh capex proposals seen
items.quote: So, part of it is a shift from bond markets, part of it is working capital utilization, part of it may be corporates taking on some borrowings and just maintaining some liquidity buffers as they also want to be sort of have greater resilience in this uncertain environment. And to the extent that they are investing or were investing, that also continues, maybe the source of financing has shifted a

items.statement: Agri portfolio remediation and validation process ongoing; no timeline given for provision write-back
items.quote: We just want to make sure that whatever we have done is correct and signed off and validated before we discuss a write-back of the provision. So, we are in the process and will hopefully work it out over the next few months, but I don't want to give a timeline.

items.statement: Personal loans grew 12.9% year-on-year and 4.0% sequentially; credit card portfolio declined 1.9% year-on-year and 1.7% sequentially due to lower revolver rates
items.quote: PL has picked up quite a bit actually, 12% year-on-year and 4% sequential growth. I think it's after a long time that we are seeing those kinds of numbers. Cards, the revolver rates are lower. So that is impacting the book growth. But we'll see how to optimize that as we go along.

items.statement: Retail asset quality stable; unsecured NPA additions have come off year-on-year; savings inflows stable with no change seen in IT corridor
items.quote: In terms of inflows into the savings, etc., they are quite stable. We've not seen any change. And as you can see, the performance of the retail portfolio has only improved. In fact, additions have come off and in particular, if you look at it on a year-on-year basis, unsecured additions have come off.

items.statement: Normalised credit cost around 50 bps adjusting for chunky recoveries; reported credit cost 32 bps this quarter including NCLT recovery from asset previously sold to NARCL
items.quote: Most of you would all be aware that in one particular case, there was an NCLT judgment, where the company was taken over. So that recovery did come through this quarter. This is an asset that had been previously sold to NARCL. And then there are some other things in the regular course, but from a credit cost perspective, the reported of 32 basis points, and as we always say, a more normalised leve

items.statement: Branch count increased by 97 in Q1 FY27 to 7,608 branches; technology expenses 11.4% of operating expenses
items.quote: Our branch count has increased by 97 in the first quarter. We had 7,608 branches as of June 30, 2026. The technology expenses were about 11.4% of our operating expenses in this quarter.

items.statement: International branches loan book growing from trade finance and Indian corporate overseas borrowing; FCNR(B) deployment will further expand overseas book
items.quote: We have been seen both increase in the trade-related book as well as some borrowing by the overseas operations of Indian well-rated companies, and we have been participating in that. As we go forward, there will be some amount of loans against FCNR deposits that will also keep adding to the loan book overseas.

items.statement: FCNR(B) mobilization in early days; no target set; expects to play out over next 8-10 weeks; will involve mix of unleveraged deposits, self-leverage, and third-party leverage
items.quote: On the second question on FCNR {B), we don't really have any target or so on that we put out. I think it's a good scheme, and we will look to mobilize as much as we can, but it is very early days yet. This is something that will really play out over the next maybe 8 -10 weeks or so. So, nothing that can be said on that just now.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit volume growth for FY27
items.quote: Yes, we are targeting double-digit volume growth this year.

items.statement: Projects under execution backed by INR17,000 crores capex over next 2 to 2.5 years to take capacity beyond 242 million tons
items.quote: Projects under execution for capacity growth are backed by a capex of about INR17,000 crores in the next 2 to 2.5 years.

items.statement: Grey cement capacity to reach 212.7 million tons by end of FY27 and further balance to be completed next year
items.quote: We'll take our consolidated capacity beyond 242 million tons with grey cement capacity to reach 212.7 million tons by the end of fiscal '27 and further balance to be completed in the next year.

items.statement: India Cements EBITDA of INR1,000 per ton remains in sight with full capex benefit from Q4 FY28

items.quote: Industry expects prices to hold broadly steady through the monsoon quarter due to the impact of increase in costs, which, frankly, is a constructive outcome for this time of year.

items.statement: Industry volume growth estimated at 7% to 8% in Q1 FY27

items.quote: We reaffirm commissioning and product launch in Q3 fiscal '27, October - December '26 quarter, precisely as committed to you when we announced this investment.

items.quote: Cost improvement capex of about INR2,000 crores is being deployed into waste heat recovery, preheater upgr adation, cooler upgradation, et cetera, and a step change in the green power trajectory from around 3% of their power requirements to about 86% of their power requirements by the end of fiscal '28.

items.statement: Deposit growth guidance 11-12% and advances growth guidance 14-16% for FY27
items.quote: Bank had released guidance about composition of our advances, RAM and corporate , and our guidance to market towards the resources side, 11% to 12% in deposit growth and 14% to 16% in advances growth.

items.quote: We are sure that in coming year, Bank will reduce cost-to-income ratio by 1.5% to 1.6%.

items.quote: Under ECL, we have already made provisions of Stage 1 and Stage 2 for ₹1,525 crores out of approximately total requirement of ₹4,500 crores to ₹5,000 crores.

items.statement: Targeting recovery of Rs 2,200-2,500 crores from technically written-off accounts in FY27
items.quote: This year also, I'm expecting recovery of ₹2,200 crores to ₹2,500 crores out of technically written-off account.

items.statement: No capital raising plan as CRAR at 18.28% and CET1 at 16.24% sufficient for growth guidance
items.quote: We already have CRAR of 18.28% and CET1 of 16.24% In that way, we are having enough capital, and we don't need capital to support our growth guidance, which we have given to the market, we are having enough capital. So therefore, we don't have any plan for raising capital as of now.

items.statement: CFO indicates normalized SSSG improvement of 3-4% covers inflation and cost increases; store maturity and new store productivity also drive growth
items.quote: Normally, we consider an improvement of approximately 3% to 4% on SSSG, which will cover the inflation rate plus any kind of increase in cost.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 maintained at INR500-600 crores, may change if large managed office deals materialize
items.quote: we hol d good on the guidance of between INR500 crores to INR600 crores, and that is the visibility that we have today. There might be some change if large managed offices come through the year, and we have to deploy some large capex for delivering those, but that we will know pretty much by the next quarter if any of that's going to hit basically by the end of this year

items.statement: Expects 20%+ year-on-year EBITDA and revenue growth for FY27, with margins expanding from current 19-20% levels
items.quote: we will definitely meet the guidance of 20% plus EBITDA growth and sort of earnings sorry, revenue and EBITDA growth of, you know, over 20%. And like I mentioned earlier as well, with the new additions coming up, we don't see any, you know, major impact on the margin or the margin percentage. In fact, there will be, you know, really like an expansion in the margin from its current levels for sure.

items.statement: Total contracted capacity of 12 million sq ft (179,000 desks) including 2.9 million sq ft signed leases and LOIs; 32% capacity growth YoY
items.quote: We operate 9.1 million square foot today, add signed leases and LOIs of another 2.9 million, and total contracted capacity is about 12 million square foot, about 179,000 desks. That's a 32% capacity growth and nearly 44,000 desks that are already locked in.

items.statement: Expects to operate 10.3 million sq ft and 155,000 desks by March 2027; FY28-FY29 supply already in negotiation
items.quote: By March of 2027, we expect to be operating about 10.3 million square foot and around 155,000 desks. Beyond that, FY28 and FY29 supply is already in negotiation.

items.statement: Customization revenue treatment changed: large managed office customization now amortized over contract term; run-rate expected at INR10-15 crores/quarter
items.quote: what we are going to start doing is basically amortizing it over the complete term of the member's commitment itself. So, this will now from this year onwards actually smoothen out any type of lumpiness that we basically saw last year, and you'll have a more recurring base of customization revenue as the quarter’s kind of flow through. So typically, in the range of betwee n INR10 crores to INR15 c

items.statement: Q1 FY27 desk sales up 28% YoY to 12,700; April was record month at 7,500 desks; 52% sales to existing members; pricing multiples held steady without discounting
items.quote: We sold about 12,700 desks this quarter, which is up 28% year-over-year. April was our single biggest sales month with about 7,500 desks, and we did this without discounting, pricing multiples held steadily through the year. Worth repeating, 52% of what we sold went to members that are already with us, and that's not a one-quarter trend, that's been the base compounding.

items.statement: Locked-in contracted revenue INR3,363 crores (+60% YoY) vs locked-in rent obligations +30% YoY; contracted revenue growing 2x contracted cost; revenue-to-rent ratio 2.9-3x across markets
items.quote: The best place to start is what's already contracted, locked-in revenue, future revenue of our members that our members have already signed up for stands at about INR3,363 crores, which is up 60% from INR2,105 crores last year. Locked-in rent obligations only grew 30% in the same period. So contracted revenue is growing twice as fast as contracted cost. For every rupee of new rent that we committe

items.statement: VAS revenue expected at 11-12% of total revenue plus digital at 3-4%; Member Services platform launched July 15 with 6-16% take rates; Rivet at nascent stage with 10-15% margins flowing directly to PAT
items.quote: I think we've historically been at 13% to 15% VAS revenues. We think that we'll hold basically at those levels consistently. So, 11% to 12% on VAS plus about 3% to 4% on digital, which is what stacks up to that sort of 16%. And that's sort of the levels th at we continue to see. We're hoping obviously with the launch of Member Services over time there'll be some addition to the bottom line or the

items.statement: Promoter share pledge ~15% (INR570 crores debt stub from reduced IPO); aim to release/repay within FY27 via asset sales or block deal
items.quote: when we reduced INR4,000 crores to about INR3,000 crores, what happened was a stub of the debt that we would have loved to have paid off, you know, remained, which was about INR570-odd crores, you know, which continues to be what is pledged against the shares. And today, I think it's roughly about 15%, you know, or maybe, yeah, around 15% of our shares that are pledged. As the market cap has impro

items.statement: Net debt down 89% YoY to INR31.6 crores; cash INR371 crores; net debt/EBITDA 0.06x; borrowing cost down to 8.5% from 10.4%; rating upgraded to A+ from A-
items.quote: Net debt is INR31.6 crores, down 89% from INR297 crores a year ago, against INR371 crores of cash on hand. Net debt to EBITDA is 0.06x, cost of borrowing is down from 10.4% to 8.5%, and our rating moved from an A- to an A+ over the year.

items.statement: Flex space share of office leasing doubled to 27% in 5 quarters; 55% of occupiers use flex, on track for 2/3 by 2027; domestic companies 46% of leasing, >50% to flex operators
items.quote: Q2 calendar year '26 leasing hit 24.6 million square foot, a record quarter capping a record first half of 45.5 million square foot. Flex led that market for the third straight quarter, up 89% to 11.4 million square foot in the first half. Its share of all office leasing has more than doubled in five quarters into 27%. Roughly 55% of India's occupiers already use flex, and we're on track for about

items.statement: FY28 supply pipeline targeting ~12 million sq ft operational; 12-month 100% visibility, 18-month 90%, 24-month 80% on AUM growth
items.quote: Even for next year, we already have identified our pipeline. We're in the process of basically signing LOIs and leases which over the next quarter we'll see more -- we'll probably show you more of a solid amount for FY28. But you could consider that it would be in a similar range as the kind of growth that we've basically seen from last year to this year. So, 10.5 will be somewhere actually closer

items.statement: Cost of funds benefit of 40-50 bps expected but will not change in a hurry; depends on system liquidity stabilization and FCNR window
items.quote: the cost of funds is the biggest opportunity on the margin where compared to our historical norms as well as compared to what we have seen in the industry as such, there can be 40, 50 basis points change, but it is not going to change in a hurry.

items.statement: Borrowing mix at 11% expected to mature toward industry 5-6% over time; asset mix target 60% retail from current 52%
items.quote: The industry is more like a 5% or a 6%, right? So we do think that the maturity should take care of that to some extent and the overall growth should also take care of it to the balance of the extent because as the growth happens and you don't need to fund only through borrowing, so then the borrowing percentage will dwarf and come down.

items.statement: Healthy credit demand seen across corporate, MSME, and retail segments; ECLGS 5.0 and FCNR window are opportunities
items.quote: There is a very healthy credit demand that we are seeing in the system as we speak. We believe that the FCNR policy window that has been offered to the banking system is a great opportunity and we are focusing on that.

items.statement: Targeting retail asset mix of 60% from current 52% to mirror India's consumption GDP share
items.quote: Today we are at a 52% retail mix. At our kind of an experience that we have seen, we were at about 60% or so and we always have thought that India's consumption component of the GDP is at about 60% and that's where we want to be as far as the retail mix is concerned.

items.statement: Profit growth should be at or above balance sheet growth over longer term; Q1 adjusted profit growth 9.8% vs 5% reported
items.quote: We do think that in the longer term that the profit growth should be at or above the balance sheet growth. Yes, that's still in our plans and that's how we approach.

items.statement: Investment phase largely done; technology investments continue for security and AI; distribution investments slightly muted now
items.quote: Now, probably as you may have heard Srini in the past, there's always an investment phase and then a harnessing of the investment phase that will happen. So, we also want to enjoy some of the things that what we have invested is it sort of giving us a kind of returns as envisaged.

items.statement: ECLGS 5.0 disbursements of ~INR 14,000 crores as of June 30; corporate/wholesale growing ~18%, MSME business banking ~22.3%
items.quote: We've also in the MSME, as you would be aware, the scheme of ECLGS 5.0 was launched and we have participated in that scheme and we have already as of 30th of June had a disbursement in that scheme of close to INR14,000 crores under the ECLGS scheme.

items.statement: El Nino and West Asia geopolitics are risks but country and bank prepared to weather challenges
items.quote: Of course, there are risks in the horizon in terms of the weather-related disruptions like El Nino and also the geopolitical situation in West Asia. But I think the country has weathered these reasonably well.

items.statement: Maturing bonds offer 100-125 bps rate differential vs retail TD rates; INR 40,000-50,000 crores maturing over next couple of years
items.quote: It's a little more than 7%, if you get a retail, it could be 6%-odd. So you can pick up 100 basis points, 125 basis points depending on the source of the time deposit.

items.statement: CASA ratio target near pre-merger ~38%; focus on unit economics and customer acquisition quality over household deposit growth
items.quote: For a start, the endeavor and our vision is to reach to somewhere near the pre-merger levels or just around the time of the merger, which was around 38.

items.statement: PCR at 66% headline; excluding agri book it's 70% vs 71% in 2019; composition driven by secured/unsecured mix
items.quote: If you peel that and get to what is it, if you look at the coverage excluding the agricultural book, agriculture is a secured part of the book, at that time it was 71 was the total and today excluding agri it is 70.

items.statement: ECL transition April 1 2027 expected to have some credit cost impact from floors (1% unsecured, 5% secured stage 2) but nothing material
items.quote: I don't think there will be anything material, but there will be some because as exactly I described, standard assets today are approximately 40, there are some 25 basis points, some 100 basis points, but on an average 40 basis points standard assets.

items.statement: FCNR mobilization to ramp in July-September; targeting significant market share like 2014-15 but no public number committed
items.quote: you will see in the month of July, August, September, we have certain milestones. I'm sorry I can't sort of put a number to that in the public domain, but you will see a very handsome, or that's the endeavor to ensure that we are reasonably strong and significant market share in the market.

items.statement: Branch productivity at INR 330 crores per branch vs INR 266 crores in FY23; ~40% branches <5 years vintage
items.quote: If you look at the per branch metrics, we are about INR 330 crores per branch currently. And if you go back to the FY'23 time period, we were INR 266 crores per branch.

items.statement: GenAI lighthouse programs going into production during the year; AI also used for security defence mechanisms
items.quote: We are on the cusp of harnessing some of the GenAI technologies on our processes and we do have a fair amount of lighthouse programs that will go into production during the course of the year.

items.statement: CEO reappointment process underway with GNRC and Board; announcement to follow conclusion
items.quote: the GNRC and Board is fully seized of the matter and that is work in progress and as they arrive at a conclusion, we will certainly make the necessary announcements in that regard.

items.statement: Full-year AUM growth target maintained at 14%
items.quote: So we are still in line with the -- what we had projected at 14% AUM growth, just that we will have to now consistently do a little more disbursements every quarter to see that we offset whatever is the higher prepayment or rundown that is there.

items.statement: Full-year disbursement target maintained at INR 13,000 crores, may push higher to offset rundown
items.quote: If required, we may have to push the business, I think we should be able to do that. And already in Q1, we've overshot our -- whatever we had targeted for. Q2 also, we are targeting INR 3,000 crores.

items.statement: Q2 disbursement target set at INR 3,000 crores
items.quote: As of now, we are projecting for INR 3,000 crores only, but we will be pushing for seeing that we cover up for the higher rundown.

items.statement: NIM guidance maintained at 3.81% plus for the year
items.quote: So, we are confident that the NIM will be maintained at 3.81% plus and we should not have a problem in that.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 10 basis points
items.quote: So, basically, we are confident that, you know, we should be able to maintain our credit cost guidance of 10 basis points.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected around 19.5% for FY27, targeting 18% in three years
items.quote: 19% plus cost-to-income ratio. For the year, we expect it will be around 19.5%. And since, our project is already implemented and we've already worked out the cost, now going forward this, you know, the AMCs and this depreciation part and all will kind of remain stable, but as the book grows, this percentage will again start to come down a little bit. So, I guess, we would in another three years d

items.statement: Incremental bank borrowing costs risen to 7.25%-7.5% from 6.95% last year
items.quote: As against 6.95% which at which we were raising in last year from the banks, we are now, you know, the spread they have increased and while they can't increase on the existing loans, it's only for the new loans where the banks have been quoting anywhere between 7.25% to 7.5%.

items.statement: Special rate threshold increased from INR 20 lakh to INR 25 lakh to offset higher borrowing costs
items.quote: So, like now whatever special rates that we are offering, which we are offering for more than INR20 lakhs, we have increased it to more than INR25 lakhs.

items.statement: No slowdown in demand seen across geographies; 60 new APF projects added in Q1
items.quote: First is, you know, in terms of macros, I think as I indicated across geographies, we are at least not seeing any slowdown in the demand. And we are not seeing any major issues either in the project launches also. In fact, in this quarter, that is Q1, we've added another 60 APF projects also.

items.statement: SENP disbursements grew 44% YoY vs salaried 21%; HL grew 28%, NHL grew 32%
items.quote: But within that, the salaried segment has grown at 21% and the SENP has grown as 44%. Similarly, if you break up between the housing and the non-housing, the housing in Q1 FY '27 has grown at 28% compared to the Q1 of housing figure of last year. And whereas the non-housing that is NHL has grown at 32%.

items.statement: IT sector exposure only 6% of customers; no major delinquency impact seen; NACH bounce ratios declining for 6 quarters
items.quote: Our IT sector exposure is only about 6% in terms of the number of customers who are associated with the IT sector and have taken a loan from us, okay? And we have done so, a study, at least the top companies which are in IT, are definitely not -- the customers from those companies are not, like if you say, whether an Infosys customer, whether a Wipro customer, whether a Cognizant customer or someb

items.quote: As regards delinquency and NPA, the stage 2 and stage 3 delinquency has actually come down compared to March 26 in absolute value. So, while there is a little increase about close to INR17 crores, INR18 crores in NPA, it is more than compensated in the reduction in our SMA 2 and SMA 1.

items.statement: IT transformation (LOS/LMS) pilot done in 5 branches; full rollout to 245 branches targeted by September
items.quote: We plan to, in fact, implement it across our remaining 245 branches in this current quarter only. The only thing is we don't have a weekly upgradation or a weekly implementation process possible. It has to be only at the month end because only then we can take the data and compare it and be able to go ahead. So we have done it based on the 30th June data on 8th of July. Same way, we'll be doing it

items.statement: ROA 2.39% and ROE 18%+ achieved in Q1; confident of meeting FY27 targets of 2.4% ROA and 18% ROE
items.quote: I guess, this quarter, we have done 2.39% as the ROA and 18% plus in terms of ROE, at least for the quarter. And yes, you are right, in terms of our opex, we -- it has slightly inched up. But because it has inched up a little bit compared to last year, is the reason why, in fact, our ROA has dropped from around 2.53% last year to 2.39%.

items.statement: Tax rate for FY27 expected at 21% due to DTA benefits, stable with no surprises
items.quote: Yes, 21% because of some DTA benefits, and this will be stable rate. There are no major surprises coming in the next quarters.

items.statement: Approved APF projects increased from 271 to 331; max 10% exposure per project for risk management
items.quote: In fact, in this quarter, that is Q1, we've added another 60 APF projects also. So, the projects are also there, you know, w e are also increasing business from 271 approved projects, we now have 331 approved projects as at the end of the quarter

items.statement: Confident of maintaining growth momentum this year, barring Middle East global challenges.
items.quote: So we are confident that the same momentum can be maintained in this year as well, barring the impact that the global challenges in the Middle East that everybody is facing.

items.statement: FY27 capex budget of about INR80 crores for analytical capabilities and select services.
items.quote: We have slated a budget of approximately INR80 crores of capex spend for FY27 to primarily focus on strengthening our analytical capabilities and expanding select service offerings.

items.statement: INR10 crores of FY27 capex remaining for Biologics CRADS; rest INR70 crores routine.
items.quote: I think only a portion of it is remaining for the biologics CRADS that we have set up. So, that is around INR10 crores. The rest INR70 crores is for routine operations for the various business units that we have.

items.statement: Biologics project total budget INR35 crores; INR20 crores spent, may spend about INR10 crores this year.
items.quote: And on the Biologics, the plan is to spend INR35 crores. We have spent around INR20 crores. The plan is to see if there is a need to spend the remainder this year. We think we may spend about INR10 crores out of the total INR35 crores budget that we have put for this project.

items.statement: Margins expected not to decline further as business is expected to grow in coming quarters.
items.quote: We expect that the margins will not go down further, because we are expecting the business to grow in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Positive enquiry trend; upcoming quarters expected to be better.
items.quote: As I mentioned in my opening remarks, the enquiry trend is quite positive quarter-on-quarter. So with that positive enquiry trend, we are quite hopeful that the upcoming quarters will be better.

items.statement: Pharma demand strong with tailwinds in India and globally; food imports/exports impacted by war.
items.quote: Pharma, strong. Food, the import and exports have been impacted because of the war situation, because the cost of import and export has gone up for the businesses.

items.statement: Biologics to contribute significantly to top line and margin from third year onwards, not this year.
items.quote: Coming to your first question on when it will be a significant contributor to the top line and margin, not this year, but hopefully, from the third year onwards, we expect it to be contributing significantly to the top line and margin.

items.statement: First Biologics order secured from a domestic customer; commercialization began in Q1.
items.quote: The commercialization has begun already in Q1. The client is onboarded in Q1.

items.statement: Food business has 50% domestic exposure and 50% import/export samples; Middle East crisis caused some business loss.
items.quote: In our food business, we have 50% exposure to domestic testing and also on the other 50% is exposed to either import samples or export samples of food.

items.statement: No active acquisition or inorganic opportunity on the table currently, though open to evaluating.
items.quote: We are not involved actively in any acquisition or anything of that nature right now. But as we get into it, I'm sure I'll communicate that to the investor group. As of now, there is nothing active there.

items.statement: Infrastructure of about 200,000 sq ft built; approximately 60% occupied, good for next 4-5 years.
items.quote: Infrastructure, see, we have built about 200,000 square feet. In that, I think we have occupied at least 60%, I would say, you know, approximately.

items.statement: INR100 crores capex planned across FY27-28, INR27 crores executed in Q1 FY27, INR60 crores to be capitalized in FY27
items.quote: we are looking to spend around INR100 crores in FY27 and 2028 together. In my opening remarks, I mentioned we've already spent INR27 crores in Q1.

items.statement: Out of INR100 crores capex, INR60 crores to be capitalized in FY27
items.quote: Out of INR100 crores, we would be capitalizing around INR60 crores during FY27.

items.statement: Secured 15,000 tons rubberized bitumen processing order for FY27 execution
items.quote: The company also secured a 15,000 tons of rubberized bitumen processing order for execution in FY27.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 22% (exceeding 18-20% guidance), driven by gross margin expansion from efficient raw material costs and value-added product sales
items.quote: Our overall margin at EBITDA level has expanded by about 4%. So a very large contribution of this has come at the gross margin level because our -- and some on account of efficiencies because of scale.

items.statement: Management expects sustainable EBITDA margins of 18-20% despite Q1's 22%, citing front-ended costs from new projects
items.quote: overall margins of 18% to 20% is what we believe can be delivered in a business like ours, and that is what has played out well in Q1.

items.statement: TPO and rCB pyrolysis business expected to contribute 7-10% of FY27 revenue (INR50-60 crores)
items.quote: Approximately about 7% to 10% of total revenue will come from the pyrolysis TPO RCB business.

items.statement: Industrial segment revenue grew 58% YoY, exports up 46% YoY, driven by rising raw material costs and ESG focus in tire industry
items.quote: The Industrial segment achieved a strong 58% Y-o-Y growth in revenue. Exports volume delivered robust 46% Y-o-Y growth despite global economic headwinds, supported by a healthy order pipeline.

items.statement: Consumer segment volumes down 20% due to 3x binder/synthetic grass price increases from West Asia conflict; recovery expected when prices stabilize
items.quote: The significant rise in binder and synthetic grass prices nearly threefold in some of the cases led to delay in track and turfing project execution. This segment will bounce back once these scenarios stabilizes.

items.statement: Credit growth guidance of 13-14% minimum for FY27
items.quote: We intend to grow both sides assets and liabilities by 13% to 14% and as I said that is the minimum.

items.statement: ROA guidance of 1.4-1.5% for next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: ROA also around -- between 1.4% to 1.5%, we do expect in the foreseeable two to three quarters going forward.

items.statement: NIM guidance of 3.3-3.4% range maintained
items.quote: We are pretty confident that NIM will be able to maintain at around 3.3% to 3.40% because of our inherent strength and the type of efficiency we have brought into the system.

items.statement: Full year credit cost guidance of 0.35-0.40%
items.quote: Credit cost for June quarter is 0.14%. And we expect that for the full year, the credit cost should be around 0.35% to 0.40%.

items.statement: GIFT City branch targeting $500 million book by FY27 end
items.quote: we are loo king to build a book of around 500 million by the end of this financial year through this GIFT City branch. 500 million is the internal budget

items.statement: INR 5,000 crore equity raise approved, planned in multiple tranches in Q3/Q4 FY27
items.quote: We intend to go to the market in maybe more than one tranche in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Domestic NIM improved to 3.48% in Q1 FY27 from 3.35% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Net interest margin domestic stood at 3.48% for the quarter ended June 2026 as compared to 3.35% for t he quarter ended March 2026

items.statement: Cost of deposits reduced 10 bps Q-o-Q due to CASA focus and low bulk deposit reliance
items.quote: We have focused on CASA very aggressively. And we -- despite 13% or 14% growth in total deposit and 18% growth -- 17% growth in the retail term deposits, we have been able to maintain CASA of 41% on a consistent basis.

items.statement: Corporate loan pipeline of INR 14,000 crores sanctioned, expecting 12-13% corporate book growth by FY27 end
items.quote: The corporate book, I will say that, there is a pipeline of around INR 14,000 crores already sanctioned and in different stages of disbursement. And we expect that the corporate loan book also, by the end of this year will grow by 12% to 13%.

items.statement: ECL provisioning: INR 2,150 crores provided against INR 3,000 crores estimated requirement, balance to be provided by FY27 end
items.quote: against INR 3,000 crores of probable requiremen t, we have provided already INR 2,150 crores to meet this ECL provisioning requirement. And in coming quarters also, we will be equally making a provision going forward so that by the end of this financial year, the entire requirement of ECLGS can be taken care of in one shot

items.statement: SMA 2 increased by INR 500 crores Q-o-Q but mostly regularized, slippage ratio at 0.06%
items.quote: SMA 2 has increased by INR500 crores over March, that is correct. Total SMA, it has come down by INR2,200 crores.

items.statement: Yield on advances up 10 bps Q-o-Q due to better pricing across RAM and corporate segments
items.quote: Yield on advances has increased because of a pricing issue, of course. And about 54% of the credit portfolio is linked to MCLR and 37% to RLLR, and because of good quality lending at reasonable pricing, yield on advances has increased.

items.statement: RAM portfolio at 80% of credit book, intend to maintain this level
items.quote: Our rally is around 80%. We intend to maintain around that level.

items.statement: ECLGS disbursement: INR 2,600 crores done, INR 1,800 crores expected by Aug/Sep, targeting 95-100% completion
items.quote: ECLGS total universe from IOB side, whatever number of eligible accounts and amount is there, that is around INR 4,400 crores. And out of that, we h ave so far disbursed around INR 2,600 crores based on the requirement of the individual borrowers and in terms of ECLGS 5 requirement. So, INR 2,600 crores is already done. INR 1,800 crores is expected to be done over the next one, one and half months

items.statement: MD says bank is firmly on track to achieve FY27 guidance and strategic priorities
items.quote: We remain firmly on track to achieve the guidance and strategic priorities for financial year 26-27.

items.statement: Plans to open 250 new branches in FY27 with focus on southern and western regions
items.quote: During the year, we plan to open 250 new branches with a special focus on strengthening our presence in the southern and western region.

items.statement: Confident of healthy quarter-on-quarter NIM improvement and achieving FY27 margin guidance
items.quote: I am confident to witness healthy Q-o-Q improvement in margins in the coming quarters and achieving our guidance for the financial year '26-'27.

items.statement: Domestic NIM rose to 2.64% from 2.61% QoQ; global NIM rose to 2.50% from 2.47% QoQ
items.quote: Our domestic NIM, which was 2. 61% last quarter, it has gone to 2.64%. And the global NIM was 2.47% in the Q4, which has gone to 2.50%.

items.statement: Sanctioned over INR95,500 crore in Q1 FY27; INR1.38 lakh crore pending disbursement
items.quote: The bank sanctioned more than INR95,500 crores of credit facilities during first quarter of FY2026-27and total of INR1.38 lakh crores is pending for disbursement.

items.statement: Credit growth momentum expected to remain strong backed by robust sanction pipeline
items.quote: Credit growth momentum is expected to remain strong backed by a robust sanction pipeline.

items.statement: Core retail ex-IBPC grew 17.5%, MSME 19.8%, agri priority 16.4% YoY
items.quote: Our core RAM book has witnessed decent growth with retail book, excluding IBPC, growing at 17.5%. MSME is growing at 19.8% and agri priority sector at 16.4%.

items.statement: No material impact of geopolitical tensions on asset quality; slippages contained, SMA stable
items.quote: As of now, we have not seen any material impact of geopolitical tensions on the bank's asset quality. Our slippages remain contained, SMA accounts are stable, and the overall credit portfolio continues to perform well.

items.statement: Gross NPA guidance <2.5%, net NPA guidance <0.3% for FY27; already at 2.78% and 0.28%
items.quote: Gross NPA our guidance is less than 2.5% and net NPA it is less than 0.3%. And already our net NPA is below 0.3, we are 0.28%. Gross NPA also last year it was 3.78, we have brought it down to 2.78 in the first quarter itself.

items.statement: Slippage ratio guidance <0.9% for FY27; Q1 at 0.68%
items.quote: Our guidance for slippages ratio was to remain below 0.9% in FY 2027 and we are well within our guidance level as slippages ratio for this year is 0.68%.

items.statement: PCR guidance >96% for FY27; currently 97.23%
items.quote: Our PCR stands at 97.23% as on 30th J une 2026, which is well above our guidance of more than 96% for financial year 2027.

items.statement: Digital spend budget ~INR3,400 crore for FY27; utilized 82-84% of INR3,500 crore last year
items.quote: year also our total budget for the financial year is around INR3,400 crore s. And we are Punjab National Bank July 18, 2026 augmenting our data center

items.statement: Target cost-to-income ratio 47-48% by end of FY27 from 50.31% in Q1
items.quote: And we are setting a goal that we should be I think 47%-48% by end of this financial year.

items.statement: Total recovery guidance INR13,000 crore for FY27; INR4,000 crore from TWO route
items.quote: Total recovery guidance we have given for INR13,000 crores total recovery will happen through that route now. Within that INR13,000 crores, INR4,000 crores we are expecting that it will happen through the TWO route now.

items.statement: Aspiration to move NIM towards 3% plus over the next 2 years

items.statement: Guidance of INR 800-1,000 crores SR gains for FY27
items.quote: Despite tepid gains from the SR portfolio in Q1, we maintain our guidance of INR 800 crores to INR 1,000 crores of gains from this portfolio for this financial year '27.

items.statement: Target loan growth of 15-17% for FY27

items.statement: Aspiration to deliver full year ROA around 1% for FY27

items.statement: Expect 15-20 bps expansion in core ROA for FY27
items.quote: Our expectation is fiscal '27, we should see a 15 to 20 basis points expansion in the core ROA.

items.statement: NIM improved 20 bps YoY to 2.7%, held steady QoQ

items.statement: Confident of achieving NIM north of 3% in FY28
items.quote: Yes. I think north of 3% is something we would be able to achieve.

items.statement: Retail disbursements grew 27.5% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: It's also heartening to see Retail disbursements growing at 27.5% year-on-year for this quarter.

items.statement: Retail fresh business growing 25-30% depending on segment

items.statement: Retail slippages at lowest in past 10 quarters

items.statement: GNPA 1.3%, NNPA 0.2%, PCR 81.7%

items.quote: But at the moment, we have sufficient cushion to grow for the next maybe 3 or 4 quarters. But at the same time, we are keeping ourselves open, and this is a market where we keep looking at opportunities.

items.statement: Retail secured-unsecured mix maintained at 75-25 ratio
items.quote: So typically, let's say, it's a 75 -25 ratio, we will ensure a 75% secured versus 25% unsecured kind of Retail.

items.statement: Moody's upgraded issuer rating to Ba1; CARE, ICRA, S&P upgraded ratings
