items.statement: FCNR leverage maintained at 9x; strong demand seen
items.quote: As of now, we have decided that we'll keep it to 9% - I mean 9x. And going forward, we may change the leverage also if we feel that the market would look at us that way.

items.statement: ECL transition impact not expected to be material on core equity
items.quote: So when we kind of look at both these circulars together, which is the ECL transition impact and the new Capital Adequacy - credit risk weights, we do believe that the impact, if at all is not going to be material on our core equity.

items.statement: Management will provide full-year revenue growth guidance by end of September after assessing price increase impact and monsoon season
items.quote: we had mentioned in the last con call also that sometime for end of September, we would like to give a full year growth target with respect to our revenue. and we still maintain that.

items.statement: Management aims to maintain EBITDA margin around 15% for FY27
items.quote: Last year, on an operating EBITDA level, we did a little over 15% and that is our aim to be able to maintain and sustain.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR200-250 crores including INR130-140 crores for land acquisition and INR40-50 crores for defense facility
items.quote: for the whole year, I think our capex should be somewhere around INR200 crores to INR250 crores, in which the major chunk will go to take over that about INR130 crores, INR140 crores to take over the land

items.statement: Defense revenue expected to exceed INR200 crores in FY27 with repeat order of INR100+ crores expected in next 2-3 months
items.quote: Yes, I think we should be doing more than that. It could be another 10%, 15% more than maybe slightly more.

items.statement: Three price increases totaling ~10% implemented in Jan, Mar, Jun 2026; June increase still being realized
items.quote: we pushed 1%, 1.5% in January, then 3%, 4% across the range in March and in June, another 5%, 6%, depending on models and products. So the June price increase is still work in progress.

items.statement: Commodity cost inflation estimated at 11-12% for FY27; 5-6% impact in Q1, remainder flowing into Q2
items.quote: we feel that the overall inflation is going to be somewhere in the tune of the final effect, which hopefully should be finally settled in July or latest by August with respect to reflection in our costing would be anywhere between 11%, 12%.

items.statement: Gross margin contraction in Q1 FY27 attributed to commodity cost increases; steel up ~20%, all input costs rising
items.quote: Basically, it is commodity prices, impact of commodity prices because the steel -- as you are aware that the steel prices have gone up by nearly 20%. And not only steel, all other commodities like tire, belt, rubber, plastics, everything has gone up

items.statement: Demand strong till May-June, seasonal monsoon slowdown underway; supply chain issues with engine/casting suppliers largely resolved
items.quote: Demand had been very strong till May, June. And obviously, traditionally, it slows down a little in the rains. So that is what we are experiencing, but we experience this every year.

items.statement: Hydra crane mix expected to recover to 60% of volumes in FY27 from <60% in FY26; long-term stabilization at 50-50 Hydra/NG
items.quote: I feel that in this year, the Hydra to NG will again go back to 60 -40, where 60 is Hydra, 40 is NG. So this is one part of your question. The second part is that going forward, we feel that Hydra and NG share would eventually maybe in the next 1 or 2 years, maybe 3 years, land up at around 50 -50 and should stabilize there.

items.statement: Key risks: sustained commodity inflation (11-12%), potential GDP growth slowdown, monsoon deficiency impact (5-10% volume swing), anti-dumping duty not implemented
items.quote: I think the biggest challenge is inflation and competitive intensity remains same, and we have been doing a good job of it in the last so many years. So I'm sure that is not an issue at all.

items.statement: KATO JV functional by end-July 2026; meaningful revenue from FY28; targeting 50-60% localization for export models within 2-3 years
items.quote: More or less all the formalities are complete and the JV should become functional in end of July. So JV will start having some revenue from quarter 3 onwards. And quarter 3, quarter 4, a lot of time will be spent on upgrading our products. It's already in process. It will further be speeded up. So actual meaningful revenue fr om the joint venture will start to come only next year onwards, FY28 onw

items.statement: Defense facility (Plant 9) investment INR40-50 crores; targeted completion by end Q3 FY27; capacity INR500 crores turnover
items.quote: This particular facility, which we are currently already under construction. So this facility will be dedicated for defense manufacturing, the special machines. And apart from that, a couple of other products which we are currently designing

items.statement: Tower crane capacity expansion decision deferred to September 2026; current capacity raised to 1,000 units via rented facility
items.quote: We have already taken a plan for that and all our plans are ready. And as a matter of fact, we wanted to begin work from April onwards. But unfortunately, this war unfolded in March. So we are -- we will be waiting till September, and we'll finally take a call on the timing of the expansion in September.

items.statement: Export contribution 3% in Q1 FY27, targeting 6-7% for full year; defense 5% in Q1, targeting 5-6% for full year
items.quote: on a whole year basis, we are looking at, at least a 6%, 7% contribution from export, if not more, and about a 5%, 6% contribut ion from defense. So totally, it will go somewhere between 10% to 12

items.statement: Monsoon deficiency could cause 5-10% volume impact in H2 FY27, visible from Q3
items.quote: it can lead to a 5%, 7%, 10% up and down if the monsoons are not full or effectively.

items.statement: Inorganic growth and exports identified as top growth drivers for next 3 years alongside domestic infrastructure growth
items.quote: I think our biggest 2 growth drivers going forward would be inorganic growth and growth in exports. We feel these are going to be really big growth drivers for the company, inorganic growth as well as exports.

items.quote: In all our international projects, we continue to judiciously evaluate the risk and rewards and are mindful of not being exposed to the commodity prices and equipment price increase risk.

items.quote: We can say that the order book would be definitely more than INR10,000 crores in this financial year. To start with in the first quarter of next financial year at maybe slightly higher numbers than this financial years we had at the UOV.

items.quote: We have almost close to more than 10 months order bookings from our existing foil plant.

items.quote: Our major product, two-third is going to be 200 and 400, which is almost a nickel-free steel, and close to 35%, 40% is going to be 300 series.

items.quote: A few steelmaking -- iron-making facility is going to be commissioned by end of second year or early third quarter.

items.statement: Strong order intake from both existing customers (70%) and new customers (30%) added in last 4-6 quarters
items.quote: So, if you look at that one, probably close to around 70% of that is -- where it is from our existing customers and the balance 30% is from the new customers whom we added in the last 4 equipment, at least from the last four to six quarters.

items.statement: Expand phase (FY27-FY29) targets EBITDA margins of 11-13% by adding robotics and AI data centre sectors
items.quote: The second phase, expand, covers FY27 to FY29. The strategy here is elegantly simple: same stack with two new sectors. We take the capabilities we have already proven and extend them into two new industries: robotics and AI data cent re, taking us from four industries to six. Because we are leveraging the same core stack into higher value sectors, margins step up roughly to 11% to 13

items.statement: Transform phase (FY30+) targets EBITDA margins of 13-18% through B2S products and platforms
items.quote: The third phase, transform, is FY30 and beyond. This is where we build a product and platform moat. We stay across our six industries but layer in expanded B2S products and new platforms. This is the shift from being a service provider to owning product and intellectual property and that's what lifts margins to roughly 13% to 18%.

items.statement: B2S revenue expected to add 250-300 bps to consolidated EBITDA margin over next 12-18 months
items.quote: And in terms of margins, as you said, the overall when you just look at the combined one, you will be getting additional 250 bps to 300 bps additional margins when we have a consolidated EBITDA margin due to the B2S opportunities.

items.statement: Semiconductor capital equipment revenue growth expected over next 6-12 months
items.quote: No, I think we will be seeing some of the growth coming in in that area, so over the next 6 to 12 months we will be seeing more of the revenue growth which probably in turn will also give us some leverage in terms of the margins there.

items.statement: West Asia crisis causing logistics delays and cost increases, but mitigated by inventory planning for Q1 and Q2
items.quote: What we are seeing even now today is there is -- there are some delays in the logistics in terms of shipments and we are also seeing some of the costs going up due to these West Asia crisis at this point of time. But we are already well planned in terms of our execution, so we have not seen any of those challenges in Q1 and we also just put a plan together to ensure that those things won't impact

items.statement: Sequential revenue momentum expected to continue in Q2 and beyond
items.quote: Yes. I mean in terms of the Q2 and going forward, we will be seeing a similar momentum in the range, okay? So, we do not see any of the major concern on the momentum in terms of our revenues and order intakes.

items.quote: On capability and capacity, we completed the expansion of our build-to-specifications lab from 6,000 square feet to 15,000 square feet, more than doubling that footprint and giving us headroom for the product platform development that underpins the transform phase mentioned earlier as part of our strategy.

items.statement: MedTech sales pipeline at 17-20% of revenue mix, no structural concern despite flat YoY growth
items.quote: Med Tech is either way I mean around the same what we have today in terms of our revenue mix, maybe around the 17% to 20% range is where we have today our sale pipeline for the Med Tech too.

items.statement: Order pipeline substantially higher than INR4,000-5,000 crores estimate, but not disclosed
items.quote: No, I think we have more than that order pipeline, okay? So, the number, I do not know if we did you get that one, but we have a substantially higher pipeline at this point of time . Yes. Very, very high sales

items.statement: Reliance contract expected to contribute 35-40% of FY27 revenue (+/-5%)

items.quote: As we have been saying that in the 1st Phase, we shall be requiring around approximately INR 200 crores to start the project.

items.quote: Oman is, you know, it is outside the, I won't say outside the State of Hormuz, but it is on the outskirt of the State of Hormuz. So, the shipments have affected, but it has not affected that much that it's a matter of concern.

items.quote: To support our growing business requirements, we have placed orders for additional drilling rigs and other equipment, further strengthening our execution capabilities.

items.quote: So again, it's a good point. And we -- our intention is to reduce the minority shareholding on all our subsidiaries over the, say, medium 2 to 3 years' time.

items.statement: Project work has price variation contracts covering longer-term raw material cost changes.
items.quote: Yes. Most of our project work has got price variation contracts, so therefore, that takes care of it, which are longer term. And otherwise, not much of a concern on margins.

items.statement: Full-year AUM growth guidance of 18% maintained unless revised after Q2
items.quote: Our earlier guidance of 18% will hold good unless after second quarter, we revise it.

items.statement: Confident of growing more than 15% in Q2 FY27
items.quote: But we are confident that we'll be able to grow more than 15% at least for next quarter.

items.statement: Medium-term NIM target of around 8.5% as new vehicle mix increases
items.quote: I believe the -- as new vehicle portfolio keep increasing within the hours run, we will be able to manage the NIM at around 8.5% in the medium term.

items.statement: Current NIM of 9.04% expected to hold for next 2 quarters due to capital utilization
items.quote: See, immediate 2 quarters, I think the current NIM will hold good because we are utilizing the capital.

items.statement: Plan to add around 150 branches in FY27
items.quote: Tentatively around 150 branches.

items.statement: New vehicle disbursement share at 16%, targeting 20-25% in medium term
items.quote: Right now, on the disbursement basis, it is around 16% of the disbursement is new vehicle. And increasingly, it will go up next 2 to 3 years as we reach out to more number of our earlier customers.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio expected to double to 5% of book in 3 years from 2.5% currently
items.quote: So we expect the portfolio to grow double in the next 3 years from around 2.5% of the overall book to around 5% because we feel that there's a very big opportunity for us to grow in the gold.

items.statement: MSME book targeted to grow from 15% to 20% of portfolio
items.quote: So from around 15% of the portfolio, the MSME will become around 20% of the book.

items.statement: CV sales grew 14.1% YoY in Q1 FY27 with M&HCV up 18.3% and LCV up 20.8%
items.quote: Commercial vehicle sales increased by 14.1% in Q1 FY '27 and stands at 2.65 lakh units as against 2.24 lakh units in the Q1 '26.

items.statement: Construction equipment sales turned positive at 8.8% YoY growth in Q1 FY27 after negative growth last year
items.quote: Construction equipment recorded a growth of 8.8% with 25,176 units being sold against 23.147 units and showing a growth after negative growth in the last financial year.

items.statement: Monsoon deficit and El Nino create uncertainty for rural income and H2 growth
items.quote: But I would like to still wait till the second quarter for the actual impact of El Nino because we will see whether the agricultural output drops.

items.statement: No more liability repayment planned; excess liquidity to be used for growth with fresh borrowing by end of quarter
items.quote: So we'll be looking at business growth only utilization towards more of growth only. And we previously also used to maintain slightly higher liquidity, which will be close to around 3 months of our future liability repayment, which works out to close to around INR17,000 crores to INR18,000 crores.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost at 7.77%, lower than current 8.56% cost of liabilities
items.quote: The cost of liability has also come down from 8.59% to 8.56%, 3 basis point reduction. The incremental cost is at 7.77%.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at around 2% for near and medium term
items.quote: Yes, I think it will hold good, but our -- see, our guidance has been around 2%. So it will remain around that in the near term or even in the medium term.

items.statement: MSME disbursements expected to accelerate sequentially and grow faster than overall book
items.quote: MSME growth will be definitely higher than this because we are projecting CV at around 15%. So MSME book and gold will be faster.

items.statement: Management expects to meet or beat last year's revenue growth for FY27, but gives no specific guidance due to global headwinds.
items.quote: we will be at par or better than what we did last year from the growth perspective.

items.statement: Management declines to give multi-year guidance due to geopolitical and AI-driven uncertainty, reiterating meet-or-beat FY26 growth.
items.quote: At this point, right, if somebody gives you a guidance saying that, you know, three years, this is the number, you know, that's going to be tough to ask at this point.

items.statement: Company has order book visibility for nine months, providing predictable revenue for that period.
items.quote: We have order books for nine months. So, there is a predictable revenue for the next nine months.

items.statement: Second FCCB round delayed due to global headwinds and weak IT sector sentiment; will happen in time.
items.quote: The second round is delayed because of the global headwinds that we are facing, you know, you understand all the global headwinds that are going on, and also today, you know, IT industry is not, or IT companies are not seeing a good limelight.

items.statement: Customers signing contracts but delaying project starts due to their own cashflow concerns in the US.
items.quote: people are signing contracts and are delaying the start because the companies themselves are worried about their cashflow.

items.statement: AI-led inquiries increasing; every project now includes an AI component, though pure AI projects are smaller.
items.quote: A lot of AI-led inquiries are coming in. Yes, some of them are smaller, AI-related projects, pure AI-related projects are small, but whatever we are doing from a translation perspective, yes, there is a component of AI in every project that we are doing now, unlike before.

items.statement: Phoenix.ai modernization accelerator delivers projects 80% faster at half the cost, driving new customer wins.
items.quote: Phoenix.ai is a product or an accelerator that we have launched which helps modernize enterprise legacy systems at almost 80% faster at half the cost.

items.statement: Internal KAI platform delivers 30% efficiency gains in testing, business development, and BA/analysis areas.
items.quote: we have seen 30%, you know, efficiencies coming in in certain areas. Not all of them, but, you know, certain examples are like, you know, testing-related ones, you know, the business development side, also the BA side of it, analysis side of it.

items.statement: JV with Action Energy targets 5% of the billion-dollar digital oil field market within three years, starting in Kuwait.
items.quote: the CEO of Action Energy has already stated that our target is to achieve 5% of the billion market, right, that is out there in this space, especially that transformation of the oil field and the digital oil field platform.

items.statement: Kumori acquisition was for ServiceNow capability, not revenue; contributed about 4 crores last quarter.
items.quote: the last quarter, this quarter's revenue or the last quarter's revenue was about 4 crores. It's not much. That's the reason why I said we acquired that company more for capability and not for revenue.

items.statement: DSO is above 100 days due to Fortune 100 customers with 90-day payment terms and long government invoice cycles.
items.quote: if you look at our DSO days, we are at 100 plus days where we are.

items.statement: Receivables high because company lacks negotiating power with large Fortune 100 customers; take-it-or-leave-it terms.
items.quote: We are a small company. We are not like the large companies that have the muscle power to negotiate. For us, it's like, take it or leave it.

items.statement: Optima digital oil field platform deployment for Oil India completed in under six months across 46 sites and 80 wells.
items.quote: that project has been successfully completed in less than six months. This is done in the Northeast in very difficult terrain across 46 sites of claims as they call them, covering about 80-odd wells.

items.statement: Snowflake partnership upgraded to select tier to strengthen data and AI capabilities and go-to-market.
items.quote: we just strengthened our partnership and moved up to the select tier partner during this quarter.

items.statement: Confident to achieve 10% plywood volume growth and 25-30% MDF volume growth for full year.
items.quote: We are confident to achieve the target of 10% volume growth in plywood and 25% to 30% volume growth in MDF segment for the full year

items.statement: Confident on 10% plywood margin guidance; expects to achieve once quarterly revenue reaches 600+ crores.
items.quote: I think we still are very confident on the 10% margin guidance that we've given.

items.statement: MDF EBITDA margin sustainable at 16-17%; may increase by 1% with new capacity operating leverage.
items.quote: So see, as per the capacity right now we have, the EBITDA margin will be around the 16% to 17% on a sustainable basis. Once the other line will come up, where we are doing around 70% extra capacity we are adding, so there will get some operating leverage on that time, the EBITDA margin may increase by 1% further.

items.statement: Total capex for FY27 approximately 500 crores across entities.
items.quote: So for the current financial year, I think in the parent standalone GIL we would have about 47 crores of total capex including loss funding for SAMET. In GSPL we would have at around 100 crores and in GSPPL we would have around 300 crores of capex. So approximately 500 crores of total capex for this financial year.

items.statement: Effective price increase of 7-9% in MDF and 3-5% in plywood.
items.quote: Consequently, the effective price increase currently stands at approximately 7% to 9% in the MDF business and 3% to 5% in the Plywood business.

items.statement: Peak debt expected at 710-730 crores by March 2027, debt-equity 0.75x; then reducing.
items.quote: at the end of this fiscal year which is 31st March ‘27, we will hit peak debt around in absolute value anything between 710 to 725, 730 something like that. And if you talk about debt equity that day we'll be at 0.75x.

items.statement: New flooring line commercial production started 20 July 2026; potential peak revenue 75-80 crores.
items.quote: The potential peak revenue from this would be at about 75 crores, 80 crores, I think. Somewhere between 75 crores and 80 crores is a potential peak revenue.

items.statement: Plywood utilization target to max out at 98-100%; MDF practical max 80-82%.
items.quote: I think in plywood honestly, we've even gone up to 98, 99, or 100. So obviously the target will be to, you know, max out our, you know, available capacity. And in MDF I don't think it's practical to go above 80 %, 82%.

items.statement: May stop discounting in MDF or take small price increase in plywood if chemical prices continue rising.
items.quote: Maybe that maybe we stop discounting the way we are discounting in MDF, we pull back those schemes and in plywood if it continues this way maybe we take another small increase.

items.statement: Furniture JV targeting revenue of 120-150 crores for FY27 and FY28.
items.quote: I think we'll share that with you. I think should be around 120 crores to 150 crores, that range.

items.statement: New ContiRoll Tech in plywood to yield P&L gains from Q4 FY27.
items.quote: And quarter four onwards you should start seeing some gain on the P&L because of that as well.

items.statement: Furniture JV losses to become zero by mid next year.
items.quote: I think somewhere around next year mid is when we'll, you know, the losses will become zero and going forward from there I think it'll be positive.

items.statement: New laminate plant commercial production by early September; 30% capacity utilization in first year.
items.quote: Commercial production would be 1st of September, first week of September.

items.statement: Expects INR250-300 crore revenue from third plant in current financial year.
items.quote: I think based on the value of what you were saying, around INR250 crores to INR300 crores, it would be easily achieved from the third plant.

items.statement: Margins to remain similar at 19-20% plus even after new capex starts.
items.quote: I think the margins will remain the same, that is why even when the new capex will start end of August. So, we can expect the similar kind of margins 19%, 20% plus.

items.statement: New capex will be in products adjacent to laminates, focused on strengthening domestic market.
items.quote: In laminates there will be a saturation for every company. We do not actually want that. It would be product going along laminates.

items.statement: Domestic market restructuring to show results from Q3 FY27 onwards.
items.quote: And you will definitely see the results from Quarter 3. I won't even say Quarter 2, but you will see the results from Quarter 3 onwards.

items.statement: Phenol around USD1,400/ton; melamine USD1,000-1,100/ton; no further price hike currently planned.
items.value: USD1,400 per ton; USD1,000 to USD1,100
items.quote: Right now, the phenol prices are approximately around USD1,400 per ton. Melamine is around USD1,000 to USD1,100.

items.statement: US tariff remains at 10% as of now; situation uncertain.
items.quote: No, as of now it's 10%, but I think today morning it came a news that US is implementing because the 10% had to go 0% from 24th of July, which was today.

items.statement: Export growth to come from existing geographies plus new ones; Europe strong, APAC and Middle East next.
items.quote: We will generate growth on the existing geographies as well as adding more geographies to the point. And definitely Europe is our most Europe is doing good. Further ahead I think APAC region and Middle East.

items.statement: Logistics is a major challenge globally, including Middle East, but being managed.
items.quote: As of now, see, there are challenges in terms of logistics if we talk about right now for Middle East. In fact, for the entire world right now logistics is a very big problem, but that is a part of the business.

items.statement: Aica is a strategic partner; no daily involvement, only potential technology transfer.
items.quote: Secondly, no involvement from their side as they are themselves, they are a strategic partner. And as of now there is no discussions about export to them or anything of that sort.

items.statement: Domestic volume ramp-up slowly in Q2, significant ramp-up in Q3 FY27.
items.quote: So, you will slowly slowly see in Q2 also you in Q2 also you would see the ramp-up of the volume. Definitely Q3 you'll see a significant ramp-up.

items.statement: Confident growth will continue in FY27
items.quote: Nishita, we are quite excited and positive that the growth will continue. It's -- yes, we are confident it will continue.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR600 crores, INR89 crores spent in Q1
items.quote: We have guided earlier INR600 crores. We still remain INR600 crores, INR89 crores is already spent.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to continue in 22% to 23% range
items.quote: Yes, Nishita. We expect that to continue.

items.statement: Gross margin expansion driven by complex generics mix offsetting RM pressures
items.quote: You've got it right. Shashank, the RM pressures are quite high. There's a lot of challenges we are facing. But like you said, the mix is really helping us. Move towards more complex generics is helping us. And we have every reason to believe that it will continue.

items.statement: Pursuing calibrated pricing actions and cost pass-through to mitigate sustained cost inflation
items.quote: We continue to closely monitor the situation and where appropriate, pursuing calibrated pricing actions and cost pass-through mechanism with customers to mitigate the impact of sustained cost inflation for the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Europe and ROW growth driven by both API and finished dosage demand from past filings
items.quote: This is all planned growth in Europe. Like you said, ex of the CDMO business as well, this is increase in both the API business and the finished dosage business. There is a lot of demand coming in from the products that we've filed in the past in Eur ope. And this is only going to go in an upward trajectory going forward

items.statement: Complex generics now 50% of finished dosages, up from 39% a year ago
items.quote: Complex generics, which were around 39% of our finished dosages a year ago are now 50%.

items.statement: Peptide India investment estimated at INR100 crores for intermediates, INR200 crores for API side
items.quote: Our initial estimates suggest roughly about INR100 crores numbers on the intermediate side, and if you take it forward to the API side, we are starting with INR200 crores of investment plan.

items.statement: Peptide CDMO targeting PAT positive in FY27, USD 50M revenue with 30%+ EBITDA by mid of year 3
items.quote: So that's very clear, USD 50 million revenue with 30% plus EBITDA, somewhere in the third year from now, mid of third year from now, should be our run rate.

items.statement: 9 launches expected in FY27 pending FDA approval of Gagillapur, 18 total pending approvals
items.quote: This year, if -- pending the FDA approval, we are expecting about 9 launches. And overall, we have about 18 approvals that are still pending, 9 of which will be launched immediately after the FDA clear GGP and plus another 1 product from GPI and the remain ing are IP -based. So we have about 18 products that are pending approval

items.statement: Oncology pipeline of 9-13 products in oral solid dosage, first self-developed launch in FY28-29
items.quote: Going forward, though, starting in FY28, '29, we launched our first self-developed product, which is fully backward integrated, and it will have geographical presence -- geographical expansions. So we'll be launching it across many countries. And currently, to add to that, we have close to 9 to 13 products in different phases of development.

items.statement: R&D spend run rate expected at 5.5% to 6% of sales for rest of year
items.quote: This will be around 5.5% to 6% as we go ahead.

items.statement: Genome Valley facility utilization expected to cross 50% by year-end
items.quote: Currently, the utilization levels are very low. By the year-end, we are expecting it will cross 50%.

items.statement: Controlled substance quota sufficient to meet target market share and beyond
items.quote: Like I said, with whatever products we have, we have more than enough capacity and more to supply -- to get to our market share -- get to our target market share and also more.

items.statement: GPI facility at 70% utilization with room for growth, expansion planned by end of FY28
items.quote: We are currently at around 70% capacity utilization. And we have quite a large leeway to go ahead. We are also doing a little bit of expansion, which we think we will need by end of '28.

items.statement: AUM CAGR guidance of 16% to 18% over next 5 years
items.quote: I would stick to the 16% to 18% range because there is a very strong non -wheels assumption, not assumption, but a tuck -in ambition in that.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance of 1.3% to 1.7% for medium term across cycles
items.quote: I would still stay with that 1.3% to 1.7% for the business model from a medium term.

items.statement: Non-wheels business targeting 30% consol 4-year CAGR
items.quote: So consol 4 -year CAGR is the number that I talked about 30%.

items.statement: Continued investment in Udaan stack and channel relevance for market share gains
items.quote: We continue to invest. Hopefully, we'll keep our incremental market shares also at a formidable level.

items.statement: Opex to average assets target of 2.5% to 2.7% as business model requirement
items.quote: I've always said being in the 2.5% to 2.7% clip is a business model requirement for us.

items.statement: Loan income fell 25 bps QoQ due to INR 5,500 crore liquidity buffer
items.quote: it is the loan income, which has fallen by about 25 bps, right? Now there's a big contribution of that 25 bps completely to the liquidity buffer, enhanced liquidity buffer of INR5,500 crores that we are carrying

items.statement: Cost of funds increased 10 bps QoQ in Q1 FY27
items.quote: we have seen a 10 basis points of increase in the CoF compared to last quarter.

items.statement: Tractor demand resilient in Q1 aided by delayed monsoon and high rural cash flows from rabi arrivals
items.quote: We also saw a tailwind for tractor purchases in Q1 was a form factor of very high rural cash flows because of ra bi mandi arrivals and price discovery.

items.statement: Management overlays created in Q3/Q4 FY26 to buffer against possible compromised monsoon
items.quote: They were created one of the specific reasons was a possible compromised monsoon.

items.statement: No capital raise needed for next 6-8 quarters; Tier 1 at 16.5%, debt-to-equity at 5:1 with room to lever to 6:1
items.quote: I don't see us in the next at least 6 to 8 quarters requiring capital.

items.statement: PV unit growth lost due to sitting out low-IRR premium segments; gained share in entry-level cars post-GST
items.quote: We actively sit out of that very, very low IRR business, and that's the PV unit market share that we have lost.

items.statement: CV gained share in SCV/LCV, lost in HCV/fleet/CE as conscious call; tractor grew above industry
items.quote: In the CV business, we have gained market share in the SCV LCV business. We have lost market share in the HCV business, fleet business, C E business. Again, a conscious call.

items.statement: Housing business growing at 100%+ quarterly clip but will moderate; large headroom for growth
items.quote: if you just look at the quarterly growth on mortgages, it's growing at a much higher clip than let's 100-plus clip.

items.statement: Merger proposal for housing subsidiary to be taken to both Boards by Q2 FY27
items.quote: So we mentioned that the proposal will be taken to both the Boards by Q2 of this fiscal.

items.statement: Too early to call Q2 collection efficiency; monitoring vulnerability sectors like tractor for disruptions
items.quote: I think it's too early to call the second quarter. We are, as I said, we have an enhanced monitoring for making sure that the vulnerability sectors are over prioritized.

items.statement: Rural PV and rural CV growing at higher clip than urban per FADA data
items.quote: Even if you look at the FADA numbers for rural PV and rural CV, that's been growing at a higher clip than urban.

items.statement: Management aims to maintain growth in the 12% to 15% range going forward, close to weighted average market growth.
items.quote: Now moving forward, we are talking about a growth in the range of 12% to 15% is what has happened in these two quarters this year. I think going forward also, we are trying to maintain, as Ander was saying that we are proceeding in a measured way. And I think that is the range of growth we would like to maintain going forward.

items.statement: Management expects to outperform the market over the near term, targeting growth around or above market levels.
items.quote: Our aim is to, let's say, outperform the market. That's our aim, and that's our internal target too. Some quarters, we can be slightly below. Some quarters, we expect to be quite above that.

items.statement: H1 CY26 capex was INR2.1 billion; H2 CY26 capex expected to be significantly higher, focused on India growth projects.
items.quote: The capex during H1 C26 was INR2.1 billion as compared to INR3.8 billion in full year CY25. The growth capex is mainly concentrated in India. The capex in H2 C26 is expected to be significantly higher than in the first half of the year.

items.statement: New order book of INR5 billion per year secured in H1 CY26, well diversified across verticals.
items.quote: We have had a new order book around INR5 billion per year. That's the new order book that we have got till during the first half of the year. So we are in line with our internal targets.

items.statement: India EBITDA margin dropped 80 bps to 16.7% in Q2 CY26 due to cost inflation from West Asia conflict; expected to recover in next two quarters.
items.quote: Margins in the quarter have been affected by price inflation generated by the conflict in West Asia affecting mainly energy, consumables and als o part of raw materials. We are taking countervailing measures against these increases, which will show up in the next two quarters

items.statement: Europe EBITDA margin improved to 15.9% in Q2 CY26 from 12.5% a year ago due to restructuring.
items.quote: The EBITDA margin in our European operations in Q2 C26 was 15.9% versus 12.5% in Q2 C25 and 15.7% in Q1 C26. Margin recovery is because of last year's restructuring activities.

items.statement: India market demand robust in Q2 but gradual slowing expected as GST cut effects taper and below-normal monsoon impacts rural incomes.
items.quote: Market demand was robust in Q2 C26, though we expect a gradual slowing down of growth over the next few quarters as the effect of GST cuts tapers down and the negative impact of an expected below normal monsoon season starts impacting rural incomes.

items.statement: India growth impacted by aluminum portfolio restructuring (letting go loss-making products) and second consecutive quarter of export underperformance.
items.quote: One, the restructuring of our business portfolio at our aluminum vertical, wherein we have let go of some loss-making products. So that we are below market growth rate as far as two -wheelers is concerned. Exports ha s been a dampener for the second successive quarter

items.statement: Iron foundry export project ramp-up started; revenue recognition from next quarter; targeting INR2 billion annual turnover.
items.quote: We are now ramping up one big program for our American customers. So this will give us around INR2,000 million per year of new turnover that will fulfill our capacities in the country.

items.statement: Chinese OEMs gaining share in Europe (10-12% of registrations) threatens European supplier base; CIE engaging with Chinese OEMs for future localization.
items.quote: As of now, the Chinese OEMs don't have a supply chain in Europe. And as we see it for the next 2 years, the more market share Chinese gain, European automotive suppliers, auto component suppliers are at a disadvantage.

items.statement: Consolidated net financial debt negative INR14.2 billion (net cash) at end of H1 CY26; actively evaluating organic and inorganic growth opportunities.
items.quote: The consolidated net financial debt at the end of H1 C26 was negative INR14.2 billion, which means we have healthy liquid cash available, and we are actively evaluating organic and inorganic growth opportunities.

items.statement: Greenfield expansions under evaluation in two verticals driven by customer location requests; brownfield and pure expansions preferred for speed.
items.quote: The greenfields we are looking at in two different verticals, and that is because our customers are asking us to move to a new location. We have enough land in our existing plant. So wherever possible, we are looking at brownfields and pure expansions beca use as you know, that makes it faster

items.statement: Guided for at least 30% growth in presales for FY27, with potential to do slightly better if all launches happen on time
items.quote: The last quarter, I mean, like end of the financial year, so we have guided for at least 30% growth in the presales. That I think we should be able to continue to achieve. And if all the launches happen within time, probably we can do slightly better than that.

items.statement: Plan to complete 6 to 6.5 million square feet in FY27, about 20% higher than last year's 5.4 million square feet
items.quote: We plan to complete about 6 to 6.5 million square feet for FY '27 as against last year's completion of about 5.4 million square feet, which can be about 20% higher.

items.statement: Confident of launching 9 projects aggregating approximately 8.2 million square feet during remaining period of FY27
items.quote: Of this, we are confident of launching 9 projects, aggregating approximately 8.2 million square feet during the remaining period of FY '27.

items.statement: Envisage net debt to be at about zero level for FY27
items.quote: We envisage our net debt to be at about 0 level for this year.

items.statement: Expect operating cash flow to touch INR2,000 crores as the company grows
items.quote: But we should, as we grow, we should be able to do, we should be able to touch that number.

items.statement: Invested approximately INR370 crores in land and INR70 crores in capex during Q1 FY27
items.quote: During the quarter, we invested approximately INR370 crores in land and approximately INR70 crores in capex.

items.statement: Expect land payments for FY27 to be roughly similar to last year's INR1,160 crores, potentially reaching INR1,500-1,600 crores if new transactions complete
items.quote: And this year, we already did about INR370 crores. And we have identified a couple of opportunities where I think we can invest in Bangalore and in NCR. So, if we are able to complete those transactions, then we might look at closer towards INR1,500 crores to INR1,600 crores this year.

items.statement: Have INR20,553 crores of revenue yet to be recognized from sales already done as of end of Q1 FY27
items.quote: As end of this quarter, the company has INR20,553 crores of revenue yet to be recognized from the sales that have already been done.

items.statement: Expect margins to improve significantly in second half of FY27, targeting 17-20% EBITDA by Q4 from current 9.7%
items.quote: So, our expectation is that by Q4, as we currently, we are at about 9.7% EBITDA. So, as we leave the end of Q4, maybe hopefully, we should be able to do closer towards 17% to 20%.

items.statement: Overall demand scenario seems quite stable and steady based on launch response and post-launch sales
items.quote: Otherwise, the overall demand scenario seems to be quite stable from what we have seen in terms of the launches and also what we are witnessing post the launches also. It's been quite steady.

items.statement: Forthcoming project mix has greater proportion of joint development projects, reducing marginal cash flow compared to previous owned-land projects like Hoskote
items.quote: So, the main difference for the new forthcoming majority -- I mean, the mix of the projects, a greater mix is towards joint development. And hence, that's the marginal cash flow, you would have seen reduction.

items.statement: Karnataka's 60% minimum wage hike in May may have some impact on costs, but technician force is above minimum wage and impact should be absorbable within project budgets
items.quote: However, it would have a little bit of impact on our overall cost. That is yet to be assessed. But I think we are considering -- it should be -- we should be able to absorb it within the budget that we have allocated for the projects.

items.statement: Plan to issue approved INR1,000 crores NCDs in at least 2 tranches over next couple of quarters as acquisition opportunities firm up
items.quote: So, we would do it in tranches as and when we identify the acquisition opportunity or, let's say, firm up the acquisition opportunity, we would go ahead with the funding of NCD. So, it's not -- need not be at one shot, but as and when it's required. But at least I would think that we will break it into at least 2 tranches.

items.statement: Acquired 1.3 acre land in Mumbai for INR180 crores and invested in Greater Noida joint development project; combined GDV of INR2,700-3,000 crores
items.quote: The Mumbai project is about 1.3 acres and we bought the land for about INR180 crores. And the Greater Noida project is a joint development for which we have paid certain dues for the authority and for the landowners. So, both -- so each one -- both put together, the GDV for this would be about INR2,700 crores to INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: SOBHA Crescent Phase 2 launch planned for Q3 or early Q4 FY27
items.quote: Crescent Phase 2 will happen during this financial year, most likely in Q3, towards the end of Q3 or beginning of Q4.

items.statement: Evaluating option to develop Gurgaon commercial project for rental income rather than sales; removed from launch pipeline for now
items.quote: But currently, we are looking at an option -- evaluating an option of launching it, but not actually selling it, but retaining for our rental income. So that we are in an evaluation phase. And once that is -- and hence, we have removed it.

items.statement: Exports target to exceed 250,000 units per month from Q2 FY27 onwards
items.quote: we are looking at moving exports to beyond the 2,50,000 per month level this quarter and onwards

items.statement: Capacity expansion of ~25% from 7 million to 9 million units per annum across businesses
items.quote: we are undertaking an expansion of capacity by almost 25% from the current 7 million units per annum across different businesses to progressively go up to 9 million units per annum

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 20.9%, up 10 bps sequentially despite 4.5% commodity inflation
items.quote: EBITDA margins inched up to 20.9%, an improvement of 10 basis points sequentially despite the hyperinflationary commodity environment

items.statement: Pricing actions offset ~50% of 4.5% commodity inflation; balance absorbed via dollar realization and cost rationalization
items.quote: we responded with calibrated pricing very judiciously taken through April and June, enabling us to offset nearly about half of the inflation through pricing

items.statement: Domestic two-wheeler industry grew 14% YoY in Q1; EV scooters and 150cc+ motorcycles driving growth
items.quote: the two-wheeler industry turned in a resilient performance as registrations grew by 14% year-on-year in quarter 1

items.statement: EV portfolio (2W+3W) at 30% of domestic revenue with double-digit EBITDA margin; Chetak EBITDA positive
items.quote: Taken together, our electric two-wheeler and three-wheeler businesses delivered their largest ever quarter and are now at 30% of domestic revenues with double-digit EBITDA percentage

items.statement: Demand ahead of supply for Chetak; capacity expansion underway to 60,000 units/month immediately
items.quote: Demand, however, continued to remain ahead of our ability to supply. Capacity expansion has been undertaken, with an immediate and medium-term focus to enable us better serve the growing market

items.statement: Broader cost inflation spreading to proprietary components, electronics, labour, logistics and energy in Q2
items.quote: inflation is no longer confi ned to the base metals complex. The cost pressures have become more broader, with proprietary components, electronics, electrical parts, labour, logistics and energy and conversion now moving up simultaneously

items.statement: Cash surplus of INR21,000 crore at June end; INR10,000 crore paid out in July via dividend and buyback
items.quote: Cash on balance sheet was INR21,000 crores at the end of June. July is typically the month when we pay out the dividend. And last week, we've just concluded the buyback. Cumulatively, both those corporate actions put together would mean that INR10,000 crores in July would have been paid out to shareholders

items.statement: FY27 target of 3 GW capacity addition and ₹20,000 crore capex; 36% of capacity guidance achieved by Q1
items.quote: We remain firmly on track to deliver our FY27 annual target of 3 GW capacity addition and ₹20,000 crore capex — having already achieved close to 36% of the FY27 capacity guidance, and surpassed about 87% of the total capacity added in all of FY26.

items.statement: Pump storage projects Bhavali and Kandhaura expected to deliver significantly high-teen IRRs; capex not far from ₹5 crore per MW
items.quote: Not very far from this number, you can say that. Not very far from this number.

items.statement: Mahanadi 600 MW expansion capex at least 25-30% lower than greenfield Salboni project per MW
items.quote: As compared to that, Mahanadi, when we will be completing, I can say definitely that we will be at least 25% to 30% lower while doubling the capacity from 1,800 MW to 3,600 MW.

items.statement: Signed definitive agreement to acquire Maruti Clean Coal & Power 300 MW thermal plant with 195 MW PPA (14 years residual life)
items.quote: Accordingly, we signed a definitive agreement to acquire Maruti Clean Coal & Power Limited, which operates a 300 MW thermal plant in Chhattisgarh. The plant has a long-term PPA of 195 MW (net) with Rajasthan discoms, with a residual PPA life of 14 years.

items.statement: BESS assembly external order of ₹440 crore expected to yield ~₹150 crore annual EBITDA at $2.75-3 per kWh margin
items.quote: So I think here, in terms of the margin in dollar terms, it's in the range of about $2.75 to $3. If you look at the overall capacity running, it will be about $15 million in a year. So that's how we are saying you can get about close to ₹ 150-odd crores of EBITDA from this project.

items.statement: India Q1 FY27 power demand grew 8.5% YoY; July month-to-date growth ~12%; peak demand hit 271 GW in May, expected to reach 300 GW near term
items.quote: India's power sector delivered a strong start to FY27, with Q1 demand growing 8.5% year -on-year — a sharp turnaround from the muted 0.9% growth in FY26.

items.statement: DAM prices rose to ₹5.10/unit in Q1 FY27 from ₹4.40/unit in Q1 FY26 (~16% YoY increase)
items.quote: DAM prices, which averaged around ₹3.86 per unit through FY26 on muted demand, have firmed meaningfully in Q1 FY27 — rising to ₹5.10 per unit from about ₹4.40 in Q1 FY26, a near ly 16% YoY increase.

items.statement: API4 coal index increased ~25% YoY to $113 in Q1 FY27 from $90 in Q1 FY26; shift to domestic coal kept resilience
items.quote: Taking a specific index like API4 as a reference, it stood at $90 in Q1 FY26 compared to $113 in Q1 FY27 — an increase of about 25%. Our continued shift toward domestic coal has kept us resilient to this adver se fuel price movement.

items.statement: Total installed capacity ~14.6 GW with renewables at 61% and 5.7 GW thermal; vertical integration via wind blade facility (450 blades/year) and battery plant (5 GWh)
items.quote: With the sizeable capacity that we added, our total installed capacity now stands at about 14.6 GW, with renewables constituting around 61%, complemented by 5.7 G W of thermal capacity providing reliable, dispatchable

items.statement: Hydro generation declined 26% YoY due to weak hydrology (Sutlej basin -39%, Ravi basin -24%); July generation normalized with plants operating >100% PLF
items.quote: However, overall portfolio generation declined by almost 26% YoY, owing to weak hydrology across the entire basin — national hydro generation was down 7% YoY, Sutlej basin was down 39% YoY, and Ravi basin was down 24% YoY.

items.statement: Mahanadi thermal generation impacted by 17-day evacuation outage (184 MU loss, 7% YoY decline); categorized under Force Majeure
items.quote: On the thermal portfolio, Mahanadi generation was impacted by a one -off evacuation availability for about 17 days in the quarter, which is now fully normalized. The loss in MU's YoY was about 184 MUs, or 7% decline YoY. However, this will be categorized under the Force Majeure provision.

items.statement: Completed ₹10,150 crore capital raise (₹3,000 crore promoter preferential, ₹3,150 crore JSW Steel stake sale, ₹4,000 crore QIP); cash balance ~₹12,880 crore
items.quote: Another significant milestone in our journey was the deleveraging achieved through the successful execution of a ₹10,150 crore capital raise in the recent past — the largest growth capital raise in the Indian power sector.

items.statement: Net leverage target below 5x by 2030; current net operating leverage 4.95x (improved from 5.2x in FY26)
items.quote: By year 2030, we are committed to have our net leverage below 5 times.

items.statement: Acquired 10.7% stake in Toshiba JSW Power Systems JV (from 2.4%) and acquiring GE boiler business to de-risk thermal equipment supply chain
items.quote: On vertical integration — a priority we've spoken about consistently. On the thermal side, we increased our stake in Toshiba JSW Power Systems JV to 10.7% from 2.4% earlier – this is aimed at de -risking our equipment supply chain and building thermal capac ity at one of the lowest capital costs in the

items.statement: Wind PLF recovered 5-6% in July vs previous month; solar PLF seasonal pattern with H2 significantly higher (Q3 26%, Q4 28%)
items.quote: In July, if you see, as compared to previous month, the PLF is already higher by about 5% to 6%.

items.statement: Gross debt ₹74,000 crore, cash ~₹12,900 crore, net debt ~₹55,000 crore as of June 30; ₹1,875 crore promoter preferential capital still to come by June 2027
items.quote: Yes, it's about ₹ 74,000 crores is the gross debt. And we have about close to ₹ 12,900 crores of cash, yes.

items.statement: Housing.com to become profitable within four to six quarters; internal target three to four quarters.
items.quote: However, Aurum and Housing teams have developed an integration plan to make Housing LOOKUP in becoming profitable within four to six quarters.

items.statement: Company-level profitability possible in next two to three quarters, better guidance after Housing close.
items.quote: Yes, we do see the potential to be profitable at a company level because our existing businesses are already profitable, may it be in the distribution segment which always was profitable and now the rental segment is al so break-even at an adjusted EBITDA basis.

items.statement: INR 1,000 crores ARR target to be achieved faster and surpassed with Housing.com.
items.quote: Ishan, the INR 1,000 crores ARR target, you know, we feel that we're going to achieve that a lot faster with Housing.com transaction and surpass it a lot more.

items.statement: Revenue projections anticipated to be surpassed as flywheel adds consumers.
items.quote: But again, it's early days; we see a lot of ancillary revenue that is coming from Aurum PropTech into Housing and also Housing benefiting us at various subsidiary businesses, and as the flywheel keeps on getting us more consumers on the platform, we do, we do anticipate that our revenue projections will be surpassed.

items.statement: Tax rate and carry-forward losses guidance to be articulated in Q3 FY27.
items.quote: We will be able to articulate our clear positions in Q3, starting H2, when we are able to look at our long-term goals on the financial metrics of this business.

items.statement: PBT margins expanded 1,590 bps and adjusted EBITDA margins improved 1,320 bps, driven by fundamentals.
items.quote: PBT margins expanded by 1,590 basis points, while adjusted EBITDA margins improved by 1,320 basis points, reflecting the operating leverage beginning to emerge across the platform.

items.statement: Margins improved 1,000+ bps in Q1 FY27; unit economics to strengthen over coming years.
items.quote: Despite Q1 being the industry's softest quarter, our margins improved by 1,000+ basis points.

items.statement: Promoter subscribing to create INR 200+ crores war chest for Housing; not envisaged to be used.
items.quote: So yes, we'll have INR 200 odd crores of war chest for Housing, but I don't envisage to use this.

items.statement: REA Group now holds 24.9% after PropTiger and Housing share swaps; dilution to largest PropTech group.
items.quote: So, what we have effectively done, we have today on our cap table 24.9% shareholder which is probably the largest PropTech group in the world and one of the biggest media groups in the world.

items.statement: Housing.com annualized burn INR 200 crores; plan to streamline costs to break-even in 4-6 quarters.
items.quote: So as of right now, you know, the business as is, it's doing INR 200 crores of burn annualized basis. This of course, you know, once we close and we start our operations, the idea is to streamline the costs and bring it to a break-even point in four to six quarters.

items.statement: Housing FY25 revenue INR 343 crores, expenses INR 531 crores; FY26 numbers being audited.
items.quote: Having said that, if we look at the FY 2025 revenue from operations at Housing.com between the listing services and various other factors, INR 343 crores was the revenue as of FY '25.

items.statement: India has 2.5 crore property transactions yearly; 1.2 crore digitally addressable; only 7-10 lakh online intermediated.
items.quote: India witnesses approximately 2.5 crore s property transactions every year, of which nearly 1.2 crores transactions are expected to become digitally addressable. Today, however, only 7 to 10 lakh residential transactions are actively intermediated through online portals, highlighting how early digital penetration remai

items.statement: Housing.com has 24% online portal market share, 58 million monthly visits, 12 million app MAU.
items.quote: Housing.com already commands approximately 24% of India's online portal market, supported by one of the country's strongest consumer brands, attracting over 58 million average monthly visits and 12 million monthly active users on its app.

items.statement: Sell.do gross churn 7%, crossed 1,000 developers and 11,800+ active licenses.
items.quote: The churn at agross level was 7%, but Sell.do has been growing in terms of licenses as well as number of developers that are onboarded onto the platform. Sell.do has now crossed 1,000 developers onboarded onto the platform with 11,800+ active licenses that are there currently.

items.statement: Management maintains mid-to-high teens revenue growth guidance for FY27 despite strong Q1 performance
items.quote: I will still hold to the mid to high teens guidance at this point in time.

items.statement: Specialty diagnostics ambition to reach 15-20% of portfolio in 3-5 years
items.quote: our rough estimate is for most of our peer set, specialty forms between 15% to 20% of that portfolio. I think our ambition would be to reach the same levels in the three to five year timeline.

items.statement: Most specialty diagnostics capex already deployed in central labs; minimal incremental capex expected next year
items.quote: most of the investments are going into our Mumbai lab or our Delhi lab, which are our central processing labs. So that capex is already done. I mean, now it will be mostly expansion capex if the volumes increase far below -- beyond what we thought. But I don't anticipate the significant amount of capex going into this business at least next year.

items.statement: Franchisee network grew to 11,700 active franchisees with 900 net additions in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our franchisee base has reached its highest level ever at 11,700 active franchisees in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Franchisee additions expected at 500-700 per quarter for remaining FY27 with churn consideration
items.quote: you can consider 500 to 700 as an average addition every quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 32.2% in Q1 FY27, up from 23% in FY23
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for the quarter was 32.2%, with EBITDA growing 34% year -on-year.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 290 bps to 74.1% driven by better negotiations, 28% test volume growth, and operational efficiency
items.quote: our gross margins at 74.1%, reflecting an improvement of more than 290 basis points over the year. This was largely driven from better negotiations, strong 28% growth in task volume, and improved operation efficiency.

items.statement: Pathology business grew 26% YoY in Q1 FY27 with franchisee and partnership segments both growing over 25%
items.quote: our pathology business has grown even faster at 26%.

items.statement: Non-Aarogyam portfolio growing faster than Aarogyam; shift toward semi-specialized tests improving realization
items.quote: Aarogyam has grown slower than non-Aarogyam. And that is actually linked to the question that I just -- which was Aarogyam as a realization because there are so many tests and all of that typically tends to be dilutive to the revenue per while that we get from franchisees.

items.statement: Nuclear Healthcare divestment process expected to take at least 6 months; no definitive buyer yet
items.quote: I anticipate the process will take 6 months, right? But we don't have any definitive what you call buyer at this point in time.

items.statement: ESOP charge stabilized at ~INR 3.5 crores per quarter
items.quote: ESOPs charge -- so it would be around 3.5 crores in the P&L quarter. And now why we have stopped reporting is because now what we feel is this has stabilized now.

items.statement: Cumulative capex investment of INR 250+ crores over last 5 years while expanding EBITDA margins
items.quote: Importantly, we have achieved all this while continuing to invest in our business INR250 crores plus of capex investments and required opex investment to execute all the initiatives which we want to and so to ensure, strengthen reach, reliability, and Poverty.

items.statement: Radiology business PAT expected at INR 6 crores for FY27
items.quote: I think INR6 crores PAT is what we can expect for the year, not more.

items.statement: API Holdings debt reduced from INR 1,700 crores to INR 1,050 crores; IPO consideration only when profitable ex-Thyrocare and debt-free
items.quote: were at INR1,700 crores debt last year. We are now INR1,800 crores debt last year. We are now down to INR1,050 crores. And as you -- if you have been following, we have been, what you call, selling nonstrategic assets, seeing what all options are there to monetize to bring down the right? I think API will consider an IPO when it is profitable ex -Thyrocare, as well as debt free

items.statement: Thyrocare branded consumables strategy to be announced by September
items.quote: It will be in the direction of Thyrocare branded consumables, not backward integration. But this is a matter of internal strategy. So, I would request please be patient. By September, you will see an announcement from us

items.statement: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 10% to 15%, with similar growth expected in profits.
items.quote: So we can -- the growth rate is around 10% to 15% for the next this quarter, this year 2027.

items.statement: Management expects revenue to reach INR900-1,000 crores in the next two to three years.
items.quote: Down the next two to three years, you can expect anything around INR900 crores to INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Management plans annual capex of INR40-50 crores every year going forward.
items.quote: So the capex will be every year we are allocating around INR40 crores to INR50 crores for next every year, it will be like INR40 crores to INR50 crores capital expenditure.

items.statement: Peptide plant at full utilization expected to generate INR200-300 crores revenue at 18-20% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: Once we are to a peak and full utilization of plant, we can expect anything around INR200 crores to INR300 crores of revenue.

items.statement: Cenobamate launch expected to contribute INR10-12 crores revenue in FY27.
items.quote: So the launching quantity and put together this year, it will be around INR10 crores to INR12 crores.

items.statement: Peptide facility with 250 kg per annum capacity targeted for commissioning by Q4 2027, first producing Semaglutide.
items.quote: To commercialize this pipeline, we are getting up a dedicated peptide manufacturing facility with an installed capacity of approximately 250 kg per annum, targeted for commissioning by Q4 2027.

items.statement: Oncology API dedicated manufacturing facility targeted for commercialization by Q4 2028.
items.quote: Another key focus area is oncology API where we are building a dedicated manufacturing facility which will commercialize and the target date by Q4 2028.

items.statement: Export share expected to grow from current 18-20% to 30-35% of revenue in near future.
items.quote: So in near future, you can see exports growing to around 30% to 35% and rest will be domestic and formulation.

items.statement: Magnesium L-Threonate business expected to grow 15-20% in FY27.
items.quote: There's a growth of around 15% to 20%.

items.statement: API prices remained stable this quarter; future direction depends on geopolitical situation and oil prices.
items.quote: The API price has been more or less stable during this last quarter as compared to last quarter.

items.statement: Receivable days improved from 145 to 131 days; management anticipates further reduction to 110-120 days.
items.quote: We have come down from 145 days to 131 days as of quarter one of this year. We continue to work with our customers to improve this much further, but we anticipate it to be around 110 to 120 days going forward.

items.statement: Backward integration on 8-10 molecules covering 20-25% of revenue expected to improve margins by 1-2%.
items.quote: You can put together around 20% to 25% will come from that 8 to 10 products and there will be a marginal increase from 1% to 2%.

items.statement: Medium-term objective to scale AUM to INR500-550 crores by end of this fiscal year.
items.quote: Our medium-term objective is very clear, that is to scale AUM towards INR500 to INR550 crores by the end of this fiscal year while maintaining strong asset quality, capital adequacy and governance standards.

items.statement: Expects total revenue upwards of INR75 crores for full FY27.
items.quote: we should be able to deliver upwards of Northwards of INR75 crores on our total revenue in the end of the -- in the entire 12 months period

items.statement: Expects PAT of INR25-30 crores for full FY27.
items.quote: from a bottom line point of view, we should look at anything from a INR25 to INR30 crores kind of a PAT numbers that we can deliver.

items.statement: Expects cost of funds at 12.75%-12.95% by end of next quarter and 11.75%-12.5% by year end.
items.quote: We are hoping by end of the next financial quarter we should be a t around closer to 12.75% to 12.95% and that out by the end of the year we should be at 12.5% between 11.75% to 12.5%.

items.statement: Targets NIM of ~3-3.5% quarterly (10-12% annualized) on MSME portfolio.
items.quote: Our NIMs what it was projected or we want to be at on an MSME portfolio is about close to 3%, 3.5% on a quarterly basis, it is about 10%, 12% in a annualized basis if I have to give that number, okay?

items.statement: Targets gross NPA not exceeding 1.25% and credit cost below 1%.
items.quote: We want to work our GNPA not more than 1.25% and we want to keep our credit cost below 1%.

items.statement: Plans 80% MSME secured and 20% digital lending portfolio mix.
items.quote: Our major portfolio will contribute 80% toward MSME secured portfolio and 20% is in our digital lending platform.

items.statement: Digital lending market for salaried borrowers is over INR50,000-60,000 crores.
items.quote: the organized borrower salaried borrowing our m ethod states that it is more than -- currently it is more than INR50,000 to INR60,000 crores okay.

items.statement: Plans to expand digital lending pin code coverage from 11,000 to 18,000.
items.quote: Today we have just opened pin codes 11,000 pin codes only, right. In the coming year we will touch this to 18,000 pin codes.

items.statement: Applied for PPI license, expects to receive it in 3-5 months.
items.quote: we have applied for a PPI license in Regency Fincorp Limited, we have got the approval, we have already applied for it in next three to four months or five months time we should get the PPI license.

items.statement: Aims to keep leverage at 3.5x-4x, may raise equity via preferential shares.
items.quote: we are very, very comfortable at 3.5x to 4x kind of a debt race, okay? We will not go beyond 3.5x to 4x of our leverage first of all, okay?

items.statement: Digital lending opex plus acquisition cost is 4% of APR.
items.quote: 4% is my opex plus my digital expense cost towards acquisition of a customer.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA breakeven in Express business this financial year.
items.quote: we are working very hard towards an EBITDA break-even in this financial year, and we are very confident that target should be achieved by us.

items.statement: Aims to reduce white space by 95% by September 2026 from 1.6 million sq ft.
items.quote: we are firmly on our track to achieve our glide path on reducing our white space by 95% by September '26 to the point where we started in quarter 1 of last year.

items.statement: Expects 150-200 bps gross margin expansion in medium term.
items.quote: We have said that 150 to 200 bps is kind of the expansion that we are looking at in the gross margin from a medium-term perspective, and we will continue to maintain that view overall.

items.statement: Plans to continue PAT positivity and improve operating performance.
items.quote: we will work towards continuing our trajectory of PAT positivity and improvement in operating performance.

items.statement: Sees strong tailwind from Mahindra's auto and tractor business growth.
items.quote: when Mahindra's auto and tractor business does so well, obviously, that has a very big tailwind for us. So, we will benefit from that. And hopefully, that will continue through the year.

items.statement: Winning new customers in e-commerce, manufacturing, and telecom verticals.
items.quote: we are winning a lot of business from e-commerce customers. So, we don't share that business wise, but I can broadly tell you that we have done very good work on e-commerce.

items.statement: Passed on fuel cost increase to 80% of B2B Express customers.
items.quote: Broadly, we have got the fuel escalation passed on for 80% of our customer even in B2B.

items.statement: Faced manpower shortages, site ramp-up, and wage revisions causing margin compression.
items.quote: the business has faced some headwinds driven by manpower shortages, site ramp-up and minimum wage revisions resulting in some margin compression.

items.statement: Last Mile Delivery revenue declined 16% Y-o-Y due to strategic exit from low-margin business.
items.quote: In our Last Mile Delivery business, LMD, as we call it, revenue moderation, we had a degrowth of 16% Y-o-Y was a conscious strategic choice

items.statement: Mahindra & Mahindra contributes close to 60% of business.
items.quote: We have close to 60% business from Mahindra.

items.statement: Withdrawing from Mumbai Airport taxi service as it didn't meet internal thresholds.
items.quote: we are withdrawing from Mumbai Airport. if you would have noticed, if you were transiting through Mumbai Airport, we had a Alyte service available. As I speak to you, we are withdrawing from that airport.

items.statement: ROA guidance revised to 1.2%-1.4% by exit Q4 FY27 from earlier 1.6%-1.8% due to external factors
items.quote: Based on this visibility available, we believe an ROA in the range of 1.2% to 1.4% of the exit of Q4FY27 would be probable.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 1.6%-1.8% for FY27
items.quote: And therefore, our credit cost guidance of 1.6% to 1.8%, that continues to remain. So we are not changing that.

items.statement: Advances growth guidance for FY27 at 14% with EEB 5-10% and non-EEB 20%+
items.quote: On the credit growth, what we had guided was for the full year FY 27, we were looking at a 14% growth rate, within which EEB, we were looking at between a 5% to 10% growth and non-EEB would be 20% plus.

items.statement: NIM stable at 6.2% in Q1 FY27 but may face moderate pressure from rising cost of funds
items.quote: This quarter also, despite challenges, we could maintain the NIM at 6.20%. But as I have told you that going forward, there may be some increase in the cost of the funds & cost of the deposits. So that may moderately affect our NIM.

items.statement: NIM improvement trajectory to 6.5% by Q4 FY27 challenged by external factors
items.quote: We had a line of sight towards -- we wanted to go towards a 6.5% by the end of Q4FY27. But given the fact that the cost of funds in the industry has gone up due to these particular external factors, that's where our revised guidance is to see how exactly we can maintain.

items.statement: Cost of funds rising despite no repo rate hike; savings bank cost up 20-25 bps QoQ
items.quote: I can also see that the effect of the reduced cost of funds on account of the reduction in repo rate that has happened and the benefit of which we have got till Q1 may not be available Q2 onwards because already the savings bank costs, the cost of funds have increased by around 20 - 25 basis points.

items.statement: IT costs up 65% YoY due to supply chain constraints from Middle East war
items.quote: We all know that the availability of chips, etc all these are impacting the Indian economy for that matter. And as you have seen that my tech cost has gone, I would say, high by 65% YoY.

items.statement: IT investment to continue; IT cost at 9.5% of total opex including depreciation, targeting 10% near-term
items.quote: Right now, and including the depreciation, it is around 9.5%. Management: Total opex: Partha Pratim Sengupta: Total opex. The industry benchmark for the mature banks, they remain in the range of 10%. Given that we still have a lot of IT investment to make, we will try and remain within the range of 10

items.statement: Target portfolio mix: EEB 33-35%, non-EEB 65-67%; secured 60%, unsecured 40%
items.quote: The portfolio mix, the strategy remains the same. We'll go to one -third that is 33% to 35% of EEB book and 65% non-EEB book. In this quarter also, you have seen that in the non-EEB segment, we have grown by 27% YoY. Our EEB has marginally come down, but the moderation has been much, much lower compared to the previous quarters. So, the strategy remains the same - 40% unsecured and 60% secured.

items.statement: EEB growth cautious at 5-10% YoY for FY27 due to macro uncertainty; non-EEB growing 27% YoY
items.quote: The challenge that we see right now is EEB, which for first quarter has remained flat compared to the last year. And this is where we will try and see how exactly we can step up the growth as the external environment improves further and our growth, which continues to happen in a calibrated manner.

items.statement: External risks: Middle East war driving energy crisis, higher funding costs, tech cost inflation, unpredictable monsoon
items.quote: Ongoing geopolitical developments, particularly in the Middle East, a less predictable monsoon pattern, elevated funding costs and rising technology-related costs are factors that warrant close monitoring. These developments have the potential to influence customer sentiment, operating costs and overall profitability across the sector.

items.statement: Gross advances INR 1.56 lakh crore, up 16% YoY, 1% QoQ; deposits INR 1.65 lakh crore, up 7% YoY
items.quote: Gross advances stood at INR 1.56 lakh crores, registering a healthy 16% YoY growth, while deposits reached INR 1.65 lakh crores.

items.statement: Opex-to-assets at 4.3% in Q1 FY27 vs guided 4.2%; expected to taper after FY28 as tech investments yield returns
items.quote: Our guidance was that our opex to asset ratio would be around 4.2%, but we've already seen that it's hovering around 4.3%. So I think those are the two key factors which are leading to this reduction. But as we said, there are absolutely no efforts that we are putting of efforts that we are putting in terms of making sure that we continue to work towards the part that we need to focus on.

items.statement: CASA ratio improved sequentially to 29.4%; retail deposits 74% of total deposits
items.quote: CASA ratio improved sequentially to 29.4%, taking the share of retail deposits, including the CASA and retail term deposits to 74% of the overall deposits, further enhancing the stability of our funding profile.

items.statement: Gross NPA 3.1%, Net NPA 0.9%, PCR 86% including technical write-offs
items.quote: Gross NPA at 3.1%, net NPA at 0.9% and provision coverage at 86%, including the technical write-offs.

items.statement: Collection efficiency ex-NPA at 98.9% bank-level; EEB June collection 98.5% vs 98.6% in March
items.quote: At an overall bank level, the collection efficiency, excluding NPAs, remained healthy at 98.9% in June 2026. Within the EEB portfolio, collection performance was impacted by the usual seasonality associated with the first quarter, including a concentration of holidays during the month of April. items.quote: Our business currently operates with an inventory turnover ratio of around 4.7x to 5.0x annually, which, in our view, is among the best in the industry.
