items.quote: The company continues to leverage exchange led procurement of gold, gold metal loan, and hedging mechanisms on the commodity exchange platform to mitigate gold price volatility, support margin stability, and improve working capital efficiency.

items.statement: Targeting 20% volume growth for remainder of FY27 with EBITDA also growing at least 20%
items.quote: So, looking ahead, we are still working towards achieving a growth of 20% for the rest of the year.

items.statement: EBITDA per kg back to INR 7-8 range from mid-May, supporting full-year margin recovery
items.quote: From almost May 15th, we are already back to INR 7-INR 8 per kg margin.

items.statement: Annual capex capped at INR 200-250 crore to support 20-25% volume growth
items.quote: We will cap our CAPEX at about INR 200 crore-INR 250 crore every year to give us runway for each year. So, this year also will be INR 200 crore-INR 250 crore in total.

items.statement: Q1 blended EBITDA margin hit INR 2/kg due to absorbing gas cost spike on committed orders; new orders at INR 7-8/kg
items.quote: We took a hit from INR 7 a kg blended and we came down to INR 2 a kg, wherein we absorbed all that cost.

items.statement: Cost-plus model with 30-40 day order book hedge; sudden gas cost spike absorbed on committed orders, new orders repriced immediately
items.quote: We operate at a cost-plus model wherein any increase and decrease that we take in our raw material or even consumable is passed on to the customer.

items.statement: B2C contributed ~10% of sales in Q1; target 25% of total sales from B2C (50% of low-carbon volume) with 20-30% higher EBITDA/kg vs B2B
items.quote: Customer response has been encouraging with these products contributing approximately 10% of our sales already during the last quarter.

items.statement: IHT/OHT combined capacity 9,000t (rising to 15,000t with OHT commissioning); targeting 50% IHT utilization next month, 60-80% by year-end; EBITDA INR 10-20/kg at optimum utilization
items.quote: IHT and OHT combined, right now we have 9,000 tonnes of capacity, which will reach to 15,000 tonnes with OHT commissioning.

items.statement: Gas costs remain elevated (1.5x average increase) but fully passed through in new orders; no inventory loss risk due to 70-80% order hedge
items.quote: Even today, our gas prices are escalated. We do not see any decrease in our gas prices today. All of that is still there. Our costs are still escalated but the only change is that all of that has been passed on.

items.statement: Operating capacity 680,000 tonnes; running at ~85-90% utilization sweet spot; 60,000t additional capacity available on demand; backward integrated equipment manufacturing enables 6-month capex lead time
items.quote: Our operating capacity as of today stands at around 680,000 tonnes, and we are pleased to say that we are back to the normal level of operations with steady and comfortable margins.

items.statement: Reiterated FY2027 guidance of low double-digit organic growth in constant currency and 24-25% adjusted EBITDA margin despite 120 bps minimum wage impact
items.value: low double-digit organic growth in constant currency; 24% to 25%
items.quote: we remain confident in our revenue outlook and reiterate our FY 2027 guidance of Page | 9 low double -digit organic growth in constant currency. On margins, we are maintaining our 24% to 25% guidance despite absorbing 120 basis points incremental impact from minimum wage increases in Karnataka and Telangana

items.statement: Q1 adjusted EBITDA margin at 24% after absorbing annual salary increases and minimum wage hikes; full 120 bps FY2027 impact expected
items.quote: adjusted EBITDA margin for Q1 FY 2027 was 24%, again reflecting Page | 7 the resilience of our operating model despite absorbing both annual compensation increases and initial impact of the minimum wage revisions

items.statement: Minimum wage revisions in Karnataka and Telangana estimated at 120 bps impact on FY2027 adjusted EBITDA; Q1 impact was INR 70 million
items.quote: Based on the current notification, we estimate an impact of approximately 120 basis points for FY 2027 on adjusted EBITDA.

items.statement: Q1 free cash flow INR 2,416 million after fixed asset additions of INR 745 million
items.quote: We generated INR 3,161 million of operating cash flow during the quarter, and our free cash flow was INR 2,416 million after fixed asset additions of INR 745 million.

items.statement: Signed $35.3 million steady state ACV in Q1 across 18 existing clients and 1 new logo
items.quote: Turning to new wins, our commercial momentum remained healthy with $35.3 million of steady state ACV signed during the quarter across 18 existing clients and 1 new logo.

items.statement: Demand favors partners with healthcare domain expertise, technology, analytics, AI and ability to deliver measurable outcomes; traction in managed service deals
items.quote: Against this backdrop, demand continues to favour partners that combine deep healthcare domain expertise with operational scale, technology, analytics, AI and a demonstrated ability to deliver measurable outcomes.

items.statement: Minimum wage impact could change if notifications revised; deal timing for managed services unpredictable; pricing pressure from clients continues
items.quote: These estimates are based on the minimum wages notification currently in effect, and any revisions to the same could result in a change to the estimated impact.

items.statement: On track to fully repay outstanding debt during FY2027; net debt INR 1,110 million, net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA 0.06x
items.quote: We remain on track to fully repay our outstanding debt during FY 2027. This will further strengthen our balance sheet and reduce finance costs.

items.statement: CareSeed acquisition closed June 2026; adds HEDIS reporting platforms Forecast and Harvest, 26 mid/small payer clients, strengthens Medicare Advantage quality capabilities
items.quote: We closed this acquisition in June this year. This is a company founded in 2012, headquartered in Kansas City. CareSeed delivers on HEDIS reporting and has two platforms, Forecast which provides HEDIS reporting and quality analytics, and Harvest which delivers cloud -based medical record review and chart abstraction.

items.statement: No pricing levers exercised; pricing pressure from clients continues; revenue growth driven by volume and new services not price increases
items.quote: There were no pricing levers that we exercised, right? I've continued to say this in the past. Given the situation of our clients, the movement in prices is in the opposite direction, right? So there's more pricing pr essure than any price increases that we would get

items.statement: Broad-based growth across existing clients and FY2026 client additions; high-value areas like clinical driving growth; 5.1% sequential organic constant currency growth ex-seasonality
items.quote: After normalising for open enrolment revenues in Q4 FY 2026, our sequential organic growth in constant currency terms was 5.1%.

items.statement: AI implementation by payers showing only marginal improvements; 70% adopted AI but only 10% report measurable improvement; workflow redesign needed before agentic AI
items.quote: 70% of them claim to have adopted AI, but only 10% of them reported measurable improvement. What that really means is people who are doing AI implementation on a piecemeal basis aren't seeing the returns that they expected.

items.statement: Employee strength 47,307; voluntary attrition improved to 28.6% from 38.1% in Q4 FY2026; 65-70% headcount in Bangalore and Hyderabad affected by minimum wage revisions
items.quote: Our employee strength was 47,307 at the end of Q1, while quarterly voluntary attrition improved significantly to 28.6% from 38.1% in Q4 FY 2026, but was marginally higher than Q1 of FY 2026.

items.statement: ESOP pool of 3% equity over multi-year period; grants not yet made; impact to be reported in subsequent earnings calls
items.quote: The 3% is obviously not for one year. It's over a period of time for which the grants will be applicable. It will be in -line with what the rest of the market also sees.

items.statement: AI-led deflation historically 100-150 bps, could increase to 200 bps; driven by onshore-to-offshore migration, automation, and AI; not tracked quarterly
items.quote: even before we had 100 to 150 bps and that could increase to 200 bps over the near future and maybe even go higher in the future. But specifically, we don't have a means to track that on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Expect inflation impact to taper down in subsequent quarters
items.quote: With elevated inflation weighing on demand environment in quarter 1, we expect the impact to taper down in the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Added 27 new stores in Q1 FY27, total store count 819
items.quote: Our total store opening momentum remains strong with the addition of 27 new stores in the quarter. This takes the total store count to 819 as of June '26 end and our presence in 559 cities.

items.statement: Small store format opportunity of almost 3,000 stores in the country
items.quote: We can see an opportunity of almost 3,000 small format stores in the country. And as we progress forward, you will see increased momentum on the small format.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin improved from 10.3% to 10.4% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Operating EBITDA was INR 387 crores, which was a growth of 19.3% over last year, and our operating margin (Operating EBITDA margin) improved from 10.3% last year to 10.4% this year.

items.statement: Gross margin improved from 28.4% to 28.7% due to lower promotional expenditure
items.quote: On the gross margin, the improvement that you've seen this quarter from 28.4% to 28.7% is largely because of the fact that our promotional expenditure has been lower than the previous year.

items.statement: Price increases only in higher price points, not in opening or mid-price points
items.quote: The price increase has not been affected in any of the opening price points or mid-price points. The price increases if any, have been affected only in the higher price points.

items.statement: Private brands will maintain or increase price discount to market leaders
items.quote: Our firm view is that our price discount to the market leaders has to be almost in every case, actually slightly higher than earlier or at the very least, the same.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth of 10% in Q1 FY27, driven by 8% new customer acquisition and 3% existing customer growth
items.quote: Our total number of customer acquisitions in the quarter has gone up by 8%. So we have served 8% new customers in our store. And our existing customers have bought 3% more approximately in this quarter, and that's how we have achieved approximately 10% same-store sales growth.

items.statement: Private brands contribute 75.2% of revenue in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our private brands continue to see strong customer traction, contributing 75.2% to revenue growth or rather our revenue in quarter 1 FY27.

items.statement: Quick commerce expanded to 767 stores across 520 cities, 1.4 crore registered consumers
items.quote: Our quick commerce expanded to 767 stores across 520 cities in the country. The total number of registered consumers on quick commerce crossed 1.4 crores people.

items.statement: Quick commerce contributes 2% to 9% of store revenue, majority at least 5%
items.quote: They are currently contributing to anywhere from 2% to 9% to the store revenue. But in majority of the places, the contribution is at least 5% to our store revenue now.

items.statement: RFID rollout across entire network will take slightly over 1 year
items.quote: I think the entire rollout will slightly exceed 1-year time frame.

items.statement: Employee cost per square foot up 13% YoY due to minimum wage increases across multiple states
items.quote: This quarter, we have seen a significant increase in minimum wages across multiple states like Haryana, UP, Telangana, Karnataka and so on and so forth. Obviously, the base has gone up, but we will continue to look for opportunities and try and optimize as much as possible.

items.statement: New format pilot stores launch imminent, will evaluate response before rollout
items.quote: we are very close to the launch of our first pilot store, which wil l be followed by either 1 or 2 other pilot stores. And then we will read the response and decide on the further course of action

items.statement: Closing inventory for Q1 FY27 is INR 1,900 crores
items.quote: So our closing inventory for quarter 1 is INR 1,900 crores.

items.statement: Foreign ownership cap of 49.99% to ensure Indian owned and controlled status
items.quote: We want to make sure that we remain as Indian owned and controlled entity. That is the reason why we are proactively putting this cap to 49.99%.

items.statement: Targets ~30% SSSG over next four years and revenue of INR 12,000 crores in next four years
items.quote: We believe that is the most conducive environment for us to be able to deliver the targets that we have set off for ourselves, which is essentially almost 30% or so SS S G over the next four years and along with distribution growth taking the overall revenue to around INR 12,000 crores number in the next four years

items.statement: Guides 20% CAGR in store count over next four years
items.quote: So, I think we've guided to about 20% CAGR over the next four years in terms of distribution growth.

items.statement: Expects marketing spend as percentage of revenue to decline from 6.6% to 4.5-4.6% over next five years
items.quote: So, we believe that over the next five years, this 6.6% will go down to around 4.5%, 4.6% odd percent.

items.statement: Expects blended inventory turn to improve to 1.7-1.8x over next four years
items.quote: And as we are growing distribution or adding stores on a larger base, the dilution of new stores is going to be significantly lower. So, we've already communicated that our Q1FY27 | Earnings Call Transcript blended inventory turn should continue to improve and over the next four years should go to the 1.7 mix kind of

items.statement: Sees massive headroom to expand operating EBITDA margin from 7.5% to 15% handle over next four years
items.quote: So, there is massive headroom to expand the operating EBITDA margin from 7.5% to the 15% handle.

items.statement: Contribution margin has been largely stable
items.quote: I think what is important is to look broadly the gross margin and contribution margin, which is a more relevant metric, has been largely stable.

items.statement: Demand softened in May after customs duty hike but normalized through June and continued into July
items.quote: And we continue to see that the same trend continuing into July also. So, no major difference compared to what we observed in June.

items.statement: Stable gold prices are most conducive for consumer demand and business targets
items.quote: We believe that is the most conducive environment for us to be able to deliver the targets that we have set off for ourselves.

items.statement: Has not tried 9 karat; experimented with 14 karat in lower price points and redesigning entry price points
items.quote: we have not tried 9 k arat so far. And at some point - in - time we might, but right now we have not. We have seen, we have done some experimentation with 14 karatage

items.statement: Hedging policy unchanged at 50% of gold inventory; not designed to predict gold prices
items.quote: So, we are consistent with our policy, there is no change.

items.statement: 95% of products manufactured in-house; provides 300-400 bps margin delta but primarily strategic for design control
items.quote: Broadly all of it is in-house, about 95% of the products that we sell is manufactured in-house.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth of 39% in Q1 FY27, broad-based with older cohorts in line with portfolio
items.quote: One thing worth highlighting this quarter is our same - store sales growth of 39%, which was broad - based with older cohorts posting SS S Gs in line with the overall

items.statement: Repeat revenue contribution increased to ~60%, up 9 percentage points YoY; new customer additions declined to ~40k from 50k due to merchandise dislocation now improving
items.quote: So essentially, a lot of growth that we are seeing right now is being ably supported by very strong repeat in our business.

items.statement: Repeat AOV typically 20-30% higher than new; frequency stabilizes from second-third year; no material deviation across tiers
items.quote: I think repeat AOVs would generally be 20% to 30% higher than new.

items.statement: Long-term NMV growth guidance of 25% CAGR over next five years, higher in initial years and lower later
items.quote: So, I think we have a long -term growth guidance that we have kind of mentioned of the next five years of 25% CAGR, which is kind of obviously higher in the initial years and maybe lower in kind of the later years.

items.statement: Contribution margin to improve by restoring logistics pricing vs cost gap and growing ad revenue; efficiency gains passed to customers via lower pricing
items.quote: Initially or during the course of last year, some of our margin in relation to what we charge for our logistics services versus our cost had sort of come down, which we are now in the process of restoring. And beyond a certain kind of stage, we would largely kind of keep it constant and pass on any efficiencies that we gain in terms of logistics cost back to our sellers and hence customers.

items.statement: Logistics cost per delivered order fell ~INR 1 QoQ in Q1 FY27 despite fuel and minimum wage hikes; expect continued efficiency gains
items.quote: you would be able to see that our cost per delivered order actually came down even during this quar ter by about a rupee versus kind of the previous

items.statement: AOV baseline decline ~5% YoY; Q1 FY27 AOV declined ~2% YoY due to raw material and fuel cost pass-through
items.quote: During the course of a year as we kind of keep passing on efficiencies, the baseline AOV decline should be about 5% year-on-year. I think if I look at the last quarter, AOV declined by about 2% year-on-year.

items.statement: New initiatives (Horizon 2) annual EBITDA burn capped at ~INR 200 cr
items.quote: roughly about INR200 crores is kind of the annual budget cap that we have around new initiatives in terms of EBITDA.

items.statement: Valmo share of volumes ~50% in Q1 FY27, similar to prior quarters; no specific guidance on future share
items.quote: In terms of quantification, I think again last quarter was about 50%, similar to kind of the previous quarter before that.

items.statement: Annual frequency grew ~9% YoY with 29% ADU growth; both older and newer cohorts trending positively
items.quote: if you look at overall the annual frequency with a 29% ADU growth still continued to go up by about 9% year -on-year.

items.statement: Meesho Mall growing much faster than overall platform; substantial part of business and expected to be large growth driver for 3-5+ years
items.quote: Overall, if you see, Meesho Mall continues to grow at much faster pace as compared to the overall platform. It's substantial part of our business, so it's not insignificant, and we anticipate that this should be a large part of our growth story over the next three, five, maybe even longer years.

items.statement: Karnataka Gig Workers Act welfare fee: stay by court, provisions made, amounts not material
items.quote: the court has kind of put a stay on any actions there. From a conservative standpoint, we continue to make provisions and provide for any of those costs into our P&L. So, there shouldn't be any adverse impact if we are required to pay that. That being said, those amounts are not material in nature.

items.statement: GST/GTA model for Valmo: no regulatory query received; legal/accounting opinions obtained; believe no risk exposure
items.quote: Just to clarify, there has been no question asked by any regulatory authority or tax authority to us on this matter. So we continue to kind of see how this kind of progresses, but we have good reason to believe that there i

items.statement: Kirana Club acquisition: early product-market fit, P&L contribution long-term; strong capability overlap with Valmo and tech stack
items.quote: So, on Kirana Club, I think first of all, contribution to P&L will happen over the long term. The business is really, really small. I think I would say like early product-market fit. So, we have to do a lot before it starts to contribute to the P&L of the company.

items.statement: Low-cost local logistics network for perishables/grocery: pre-product-market fit, experimenting with sub-INR 20-30 items, distinct from national Valmo network
items.quote: I would say potentially fruits and vegetables at some point in time, staples, a lot of very small average order val ue products, like sub INR20, sub INR30 products that we do not believe can become viable on our core platform

items.statement: ~2/3 of GMV-contributing sellers advertise; ad adoption rising QoQ; ROAS similar to prior quarter
items.quote: I think close to about two -thirds of our GMV contributing sellers do ads. I think there is scope for increasing this even further.

items.statement: For >50% of GMV-contributing sellers, Meesho is a primary source of income
items.quote: So more than for more than 50% of our sellers, let's say, we would be a primary source of income.

items.statement: Competitive intensity remains high and unchanged; focus on own mission, value prop improving across pricing, selection, logistics
items.quote: I would not say that the competitive intensity has changed in either direction. We continue to kind of move forward on our own mission and vision. We will continue to kind of scale up aggressively. Our value proposition continues to get better.

items.statement: Management does not provide MRR guidance; advises looking at past quarterly exit MRR trends instead
items.quote: See, we don't provide guidance on MRR. We always, advise everyone to look at what we have done in the past rather than, predict the future.

items.statement: Expecting next lot of 1,024 B200 GPUs in next couple of months; plans to add more Blackwell and Vera Rubin capacity
items.quote: We obviously plan to deploy the B200 as soon as a new lot becomes available to us. And we are expecting that to happen soon over the next couple of months.

items.statement: B200 cluster at maximal utilization; customers increasingly preferring 1-3 year contracts for capacity lock-in
items.quote: Yes, it's quite a maximal utilization of capacity that we have.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 75.2% in Q1 FY27, up 1,450 bps QoQ; management believes margins sustainable medium to long term
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR1,179 million with margins expanding up to 75.2%. EBITDA margin expanded by 1,450 basis points compared to Q4 2026.

items.statement: Price hike announced in July for GPU and CPU; driven by both demand-supply and input cost increases (memory cost up more on CPU side)
items.quote: So, to accommodate that, we had to, in fact, increase the price of both the GPUs and CPUs. And it's not just about the higher demand scenario that's associated with the price increase.

items.statement: Very robust demand scenario; major growth expected from capacity additions rather than price hikes
items.quote: Now that being said, the major growth will come from capacity additions as opposed to majorly on the price hike side is what we believe.

items.statement: Revenue mix: India AI ~20-21%, International ~37%, rest domestic; training dominant but inference growing on same infrastructure
items.quote: I think India AI revenue was about 20%, 21%. And international was closer to 37% or so. And rest is like all domestic revenue.

items.statement: AI at day zero of decadal super cycle; not worried about commoditization news or China model competition
items.quote: We believe that some of those things which are equally important are completely lower. So it is still day zero of AI.

items.statement: Current loan ~INR 450 cr for first B200 lot; will increase with next lot; no quantification of peak debt; future equity raise possible but not announced
items.quote: So, the loan, which stands as of now is broadly INR 450 crores, which with the other lot coming in picture, it would be increasing across in the near term.

items.statement: SovCloud subsidiary for large-scale CPU clusters; Delaware entity for international sales and alliances; L&T partnership at arm's length for data center capacity
items.quote: SovCloud is essentially an infrastructure subsidiary, very focused on build-out of the infrastructure. And the U.S. entity, the Delaware entity, obviously is focused on selling in the international market.

items.statement: Expect a year of revenue and earnings growth driven by consumer preference and expanding new destinations
items.quote: We expect a year of revenue and earnings growth driven by consumer preference for our cruise brand and expanding our new destinations.

items.statement: Cordelia Sky handover on September 25, 2026; maiden voyage October 23, 2026; Cordelia Sun to follow
items.quote: The handover of the vessel will be on September 25, 2026. Thereafter, the rebranding will be happening and implementing our entertainment programs, our guest offerings for India. The ship name will change to Cordelia Sky and will be arriving in Mumbai on October 15, 2026 and our first maiden voyage will be October 23, 2026.

items.statement: Rs.65 Crores advance bookings for new ships translating to Rs.110-115 Crores revenue for shorter sailings
items.quote: Right now, I can share with you Rs.65 Crores in advance booking, which is resulting to approximately Rs.110 Crores to Rs.115 Crores revenue for the shorter sailings.

items.statement: Net profit margin around 12% for Q1 FY27; EBITDA impacted by Rs.14 Crores higher fuel cost
items.quote: With the higher fuel costs, we report a net profit of Rs.22.77 Crores on a consolidated basis and a net profit margin of around 12% for the quarter ended June 2026.

items.statement: Average ticket price increased 4.3% vs Q1 2025; fuel surcharges on new bookings to recover extra cost from Q2/Q3
items.quote: The first quarter was shaped by the geopolitical situation in the Middle East that created huge headwinds for the entire global cruise sector and the entire transportation industry driven by extremely high fuel costs. Despite these industry wide impacts and headwinds, we report a load factor of 105% for Q1 with an increase of 4.3% of average ticket price versus Q1 2025.

items.statement: Served 55,700 guests and 24,245 staterooms in Q1, up ~10% YoY; load factor 105%
items.quote: While the revenue environment saw moderation increase over last year, demand for cruising in India remained strong, as we served more than 55,700 guests and 24,245 staterooms booked during the quarter reflecting a growth of around 10% over last year Q1.

items.statement: New ships offer 245 suites vs 69 on Empress; 9 restaurants vs 3; potential revenue per ship nearly 100% higher
items.quote: Before we sold 69 rooms every vacation and every cruise for a premium price now we are going to be selling 250 rooms for premium price, on top of it the new ship has 200 rooms more. So really, it is the possibility of revenue generating for each ship because of the different cabins and layout is almost 100% increase on potential revenue versus our current vessel.

items.statement: Fuel cost spiked to $1,228/tonne from $580 average; now ~$800; extra impact secured in Q3, recovery expected by year-end
items.quote: The average price for a metric tonne for entire last year was $580. The highest price when the tension started was $1228 per metric tonne that is why the impact of 65% is secured in the Q3. Now when I purchase fuel I am getting the actual price but I am putting the fuel on only two to three weeks later because it is preordered so the price is paid on the preorder and then even if the delivery date

items.quote: We are expanding our presence in Lakshadweep with two new islands and successfully testing new ports and destinations on the West Coast for our continuous growth as we speak by the upcoming delivery of Cordelia Sky in September, and then followed by Cordelia Sun. Of a particular note are the steps we are taking to enhance our loyalty ecosystem, including the rollout of our loyalty program called C

items.statement: International sailings to Sri Lanka, Maldives, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand; four new monsoon sailings from West Coast in 2027; Maldives and Columbus sailings from East Coast starting October 2026
items.quote: However, our international cruises are focused on easy entry for Indians, which is covering mostly Sri Lanka, Maldives, Singapore, Indonesia, and Thailand. That will start, as you know, we already started our international sailing during the monsoon season from the West Coast. All these itineraries have been successfully tested this year and from next year onwards 2027 we are introducing four more

items.statement: Fixed costs to be shared across three ships reducing per-unit cost; purchasing power to improve with fleet scale
items.quote: Now with Sky coming in September, our total operating cost is split between two ships and then further down in three ships. So especially our fixed costs in shore side marketing, our management fees, everything is going to be shared by three ships. So naturally the cost will reduce because of the shared cost between three vessels and the purchasing power will also increase in our favor.

items.statement: Empress revenue growth expected 10-12% going forward; Q1 load factor 105% vs 99.9% last year
items.quote: I think with the given situation, I am of the belief that it should go into two digit, the growth of Empress. This is the given situation which is going on. You can say it is almost 8% or 9%, but yes, going forward, it will be 10% to 11% to 12%.

items.statement: Finance cost doubled to Rs.4 Crores due to IDFC First Bank loan for rating upgrade; backed by FDs; intend to prepay despite 1% penalty
items.quote: So Swapna, we have taken a loan from IDFC First Bank and that is the only reason though it is backed by FDs but then because I think I have already appraised earlier also that in order to have the ratings in place this was a challenge, which we have been facing and the FDOD facilities were not being considered so we have taken loan from IDFC Bank.

items.statement: First retail store in Jaipur (~30,000 sq ft) targeting operational start by November end 2026
items.quote: It's around 30,000 square feet. So, we are trying to bring it more faster than usually what construction and interior time takes. But I think most probably by the end of the year, we will be shifting into that and we will be starting our operations from there.

items.statement: New orders expected from August 2026; artisans ready to work hard on incoming demand
items.quote: So, it will go well. Touchwood I just feel it will be great and Jaipur is a potential with the coloured stone, Polkis, jewellery side. It is it has a potential we can -- we get everything, raw material and labour.

items.statement: EBITDA margin maintained at ~29.5% in FY26; luxury positioning and artwork justify premium margins
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 29.48% while diluted EPS improved to INR10.74, reflecting the strength of our business model and disciplined execution.

items.statement: Fixed margin policy maintained across product categories; raw material cost changes passed through via design-led pricing
items.quote: It will be compared because we are just keeping the fixed margins. Whatever the cost comes, we just keep the margins fixed on. Yeah, we are not changing our margins on things.

items.quote: Now, I am adding men's jewellery into this. As I just explained in my last answer, we are coming up with cufflinks of Polki, we are coming up buckle belt uh in Polki, brooches in Polki, we are coming up kilangi, even there are special rings we are making for men.

items.statement: Franchise partner Francorp committed to 30 stores in 3 years; company targeting minimum 3 owned stores in FY27 to gain experience before scaling
items.quote: It's a Francorp named franchise company which has committed to us to bring up 30 stores in next three years. That I told him. Yes, we are working on it.

items.statement: Export journey initiated with first US sale via Instagram; prioritizing UK (FTA effective July 15) and Middle East; hallmarking and IGI certifications in place
items.quote: UK is opened. UK on 15th of July if you see, UK has opened with the free trade. So, UK has a fabulous market of handmade jewelry. Even Middle East, we are working on we are planning on some shows in Middle East.

items.statement: Raised FY27 revenue growth aspiration to 40% and above from previous 20%

items.statement: Tax refund of higher advance tax due to ambiguous expense allowability; non-structural, may occur occasionally
items.quote: The tax refund was on account of a refund because there were certain expenses which were ambiguous on whether they'll be allowable. We had deposited higher advance tax and there's a refund towards that. That's normal course of business and such things may come up once in a while going forward as well, but nothing structural.

items.statement: Nugget is enterprise AI product business in stealth mode; good traction but evolving market; will share more in coming quarters; expenses largely manpower
items.quote: It's an enterprise AI product business and we are seeing good traction in that but it's an evolving market, as you know, the entire AI space. We want to take a couple of more quarters and build our thesis more strongly around this, and then we'll share more about this business going forward.

items.statement: No near-term margin pressures anticipated; directionally margins should continue to improve if growth continues as expected
items.quote: At this point, we can say that.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 results in line with full-year targets; strong OEM schedules indicate volume growth from September through March
items.quote: In general, if you see, our Q1 results are in line of our targets for this coming financial year.

items.statement: High-pressure mold line for foundry to start in Q3 FY27, doubling foundry capacity; axle shaft forging facility on track for September 2026 commissioning
items.quote: A high-pressure mold line for our foundry is expected to start in Q3. This will double our foundry capacity. Axle shaft production facility using material gathering and press forging technology is on track for commissioning by September 2026.

items.statement: Trailer axle prices increased 3-5% from April 1; further 1-2% hike planned for conversion cost increases; steel pass-through of INR4,700/tonne retrospective from mid-July
items.quote: It is approximately between 3% to 5%.

items.statement: OEMs indicating strong volumes from September through March across tractor-trailer and tipper segments; fabricators giving repeated and new orders driving 30% YoY axle/suspension volume growth
items.quote: We have been indicated very good projections from September onwards right up to March. And it's just that these kind of schedule lines or projections usually don't come into manufacturers as early as June and July.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue mix: trailer/axle/suspension/tipping 41%, component business 59%; axle volumes ~9,500 units, suspension volumes ~3,200-3,300 units in Q1
items.quote: If we look into our segment-wise revenue contribution, our trailers, axles, suspensions, and our tipping segment has contributed to 41%, while the component business stands at 59%.

items.statement: No additional debt planned for existing business beyond seamless tube facility; term debt ~INR54 cr end Q4 FY26, may rise INR10-15 cr; IPO funds fully utilized as planned
items.quote: For our existing business, there is no plan on any debt in the immediate timeline.

items.statement: Extrusion line commissioned and productionized; tipping jack capacity 800/month, targeting 65-70% utilization by Q4 FY27; sold 226 kits in Q1 FY27
items.quote: We have a capacity to manufacture 800 numbers a month. The lines have already been set for that and we expect by quarter four to be at around 65% to 70% of that capacity utilization.

name: CG Power and Industrial Solutions Ltd

items.statement: FY27 volume target of ~7 million tonnes excluding clinker sales
items.quote: We remain confident of achieving volumes of approximately 7 million tons in FY 2027, supported by our expanding market presence and ongoing operational initiatives.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA per tonne guidance of ₹500-550
items.quote: What we have indicated and what we remain committed is around ₹500 to ₹550 EBITDA per tonne.

items.statement: Expect double-digit volume growth in FY28 similar to FY27
items.quote: I think even this year it's a double-digit growth. And for next year also, we are expecting something similar in terms of a percentage.

items.statement: No major capex plans for next couple of years except ₹30-40 crore annual maintenance; ₹240 crore ongoing capex to spread over FY27-28
items.quote: We are not having any CapEx plans for next couple of years. So, except for the operational maintenance, which is roughly around ₹30 crore to ₹40 crore per year, we do not have any CapEx plan up to end of 2028, for sure.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA/tonne at ₹451; moderated due to elevated input costs from geopolitical tensions
items.quote: From an operational standpoint, the EBITDA per tonne for the quarter stood at ₹451. As anticipated, profitability and margins moderated during Q1 due to elevated input prices across the energy, fuel, and packaging amid the geopolitical tensions in West Asia.

items.statement: Expect full-year cost inflation of ~₹100/tonne (₹50 fuel, ₹50 other) to be offset by efficiency gains; Q2 costs higher due to maintenance shutdowns and inventory
items.quote: For the full-year, we are expecting fuel plus raw material, plus other miscellaneous expenditure by ₹100 a tonne. We expect a matching kind of a saving, so net-net, we might remain very similar.

items.statement: Prices flat from March to July; realised ₹50-60/tonne sequential improvement from mix/regional hikes but largely stable
items.quote: See I think in the markets from March exit to July, it has been flat. From June to July also it has been flat. So of course, there were certain price increases that have happened in between, but more or less everything got moderated.

items.statement: South demand grew ~6% YoY in Q1 (AP/Telangana 11%, Karnataka flat, TN 4%, Kerala 12%); expect 8-10% for full year; MP 9-10%, Odisha strong
items.quote: We believe that South demand should be anywhere between 8% to 10% for the year. So far, it is close to 6%, 6.5%. In spite of a few challenging months in the region, primarily on account of elections that have happened.

items.statement: Vizag land sale awaiting generic GO from Andhra government; expect ₹150 crore realisation in FY27 and ₹200 crore in FY28
items.quote: We are only waiting for the final Government approval. Earlier, we were expecting a GO specific to our case. However, our understanding now is that the Government intends to issue a more generic GO instead.

items.statement: West Asia crisis driving fuel cost inflation; have inventory till mid-October; further escalation beyond ₹100/tonne not factored
items.quote: We do have inventory all the way up to middle of October. So, we know we can go all the way up to middle of October. What we have pencilled in is an ₹100 price hike. On account of fuel, it is ₹50, and all the other things.

items.statement: WHRS at Gudipadu to save ~₹25/tonne consolidated (₹100-125 at Jeerabad); Andhra WHRS targeted in next couple of years
items.quote: Overall, on a consolidated volume, we expect a ₹25 per ton, saving on that account, though at Jeerabad volume it could be ₹100, ₹125. The only asset which doesn't have a waste heat recovery is Andhra. So next couple of years, the target is to go for a waste heat recovery at Andhra.

items.statement: Andhra Cements utilisation at ~50%, targeting 60-70% by year-end despite high competitive intensity
items.quote: I think by end of this year, we should reach close to 60% capacity utilisation. So, from that perspective, we believe that Andhra might operate anywhere between 60% to 70% for the coming years, despite very high competitive intensity in the neighbourhood.

items.statement: Expect IMFL proprietary revenue to grow ~30% YoY over next 2-3 years
items.quote: So, in our guidance also, we have earlier also mentioned that we expect the revenue of the IMFL business to grow at the rate of 30% year-on-year. That's what we are focusing on.

items.statement: SDF Kerala plant upgrade on track; one unit moving by Dec 2026, full operation from Apr 2027
items.quote: So, by December, we will start moving one of the units to SDF. And from April onwards, we are planning to do a full-fledged operation from SDF. It will be done in December. First, we'll start and then we'll full-fledged move the operation from 1st of April.

items.statement: Target SDF capacity of 3.5-4 lakh cases/month
items.quote: However, we are working for a capacity buildup of at least around 3.5 lakh to 4 lakh cases per month.

items.statement: IMFL proprietary share of revenue rose to 23% in Q1 FY27 from 17% in FY26
items.quote: In Q1 FY 2026-27, IMFL proprietary contributed 23% of our overall revenue, compared to 17% in FY 2026-27, reflecting in the growth contribution of our higher-margin proprietary portfolio.

items.statement: IMFL proprietary EBITDA margin at 20% in Q1 FY27 despite brand investments
items.quote: Despite continued investments in brand building and market expansions, we maintain a healthy IMFL proprietary EBITDA margin of 20%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 11% in Q1 FY27 due to ethanol segment losses
items.quote: It is mainly because of ethanol business.

items.statement: CP series volume surged 260% YoY to 73,000 cases in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The CP series delivered an impressive 260% year-on-year volume growth in Q1 FY27 with the sales increase from 20,300 cases to 73,000 cases, reflecting strong brand equity and reinforcing its leadership position within the segment.

items.statement: Single malt whiskey (2 variants) maturing 8-9 months; revenue expected from Q3 FY28
items.quote: We have started maturing the liquid. It's been almost 8 to 9 months since we've matured the liquid and the result is coming out fairly well. So, we expect the revenue of this to start being shown in the balance sheet in, I think, Q3 next year onwards.

items.statement: Pyrova Energy to scale to 45,000 tons capacity in FY27, add 30,000 tons in FY28; margins to build from single-digit during ramp-up to 18-20% once rCB facility is commissioned and mature
items.quote: For Pyrova Energy, we expect to steadily scale capacity to 45,000 tons as we stabilize the technology, followed by a further 30,000 tons capacity addition in FY 2028. items.statement: Plastic recycling verticals (nylon and polyolefin) expect over 20% growth in FY27, mid-teen growth through FY30, with stable EBITDA margin of 10-15% supported by EPR regulation and value-added focus
items.quote: In our plastic recycling business, our nylon and polyolefin recycling verticals, we expect over a 20% growth this fiscal, followed by a mid-teen growth through FY 2030, while maintaining a stable EBITDA margin of between 10% to 15%, supported by tightening EPR regulation and our continued focus on value-added products.

items.quote: So, because of the first two months, we were earlier predicting around 15%. Because of the loss of volume in the first two months, we are looking at slightly lower than 15%.

items.statement: Export contribution targeted at 12-15% of revenue for FY27
items.quote: It will be a minimum of 10%, but we are targeting more towards 15%, so we are looking at somewhere between 12% and 15% this year.

items.quote: All our customers are looking to increase their volumes and everybody is talking about doubling their capacity in the next 3 years.

items.quote: We have had our highest EBITDA margin of recent times at 5.43%, our highest PAT margin of 2.87%.

items.statement: Average copper price assumption raised above initial Rs 1,300/kg projection for FY27
items.quote: Initially, we were taking around 1,300 rupees as the average price for the year, which should be exceeded.

items.statement: Recycled copper market in India growing at 12-13% CAGR; company growing at 2-2.5x market rate, gaining share
items.quote: The recycled copper market, by some estimates, should be growing in India at a CAGR of about 12-13%.

items.statement: Highest value addition in auto/switchgear (double-digit margins); highest growth in transformer/motor winding and bus bars
items.quote: Auto and switchgear will have double digits; the rest of it will all be in single digits.

items.statement: Fundraise of Rs 52 cr finalized (money expected August); second tranche ~March FY28 post-demerger in standalone copper unit

items.quote: We are going to form a new company called Tieramet Limited, which will be a wholly owned subsidiary of Bhagyanagar India. All the copper business will move from Bhagyanagar Copper to Tieramet.

items.statement: Long-term revenue target Rs 5,000 cr by FY30 (conservative); projected debt Rs 300-350 cr by FY30; plastic recycling adds <1% revenue but high margins
items.quote: We are very confident of 5,000 crores by FY30, whatever the copper price.

items.statement: Management stands by 15% volume growth guidance for FY27 and is not upgrading despite 20% Q1 growth
items.quote: We stand by the guidance of 15% volume growth. In the first quarter, we have achieved 20%. We're very confident that we'll be able to stick to this guidance of 15% volume growth.

items.statement: EBITDA per kg expected to sustain at current levels around INR135-140 for FY27
items.quote: No, no. I think this will be sacrosanct throughout the year. The EBITDA per kilo will remain same throughout the year.

items.statement: Capex plan for FY27 is INR25-50 crores for upgrades and small additions, no expansion capex for next 2-3 years
items.quote: It will be anything between INR25 crores to INR50 crores. These are generally a little bit of an upgradation, some additions in the current listing only. So these are very small numbers.

items.statement: Capacity utilization at 65-70% aggregate, freeze-dried utilization higher than spray-dried
items.quote: Capacity utilization stands at around between 65% to 70%. That is at an aggregate level, yes. There is a higher utilization for the freeze-dried because we are seeing a higher demand for freeze-dried.

items.statement: Freeze-dried earns 30-40% higher EBITDA per kg than spray-dried as a thumb rule
items.quote: But what we can tell you is that generally, a freeze-dried would earn you anywhere between 30% to 40% more EBITDA than spray-dried as a thumb rule.

items.statement: Domestic branded business targeting INR550-600 crores revenue in FY27 with 25-30% volume growth
items.quote: We did INR125 crores, INR130 crores. I multiply it by 4, it is INR500 crores. In India, a season does play an impact. We are looking at anything between INR550 crores, INR600 crores of only branded play.

items.statement: Freeze-dried proportion increased vs previous year, but EBITDA per kg not expected to improve further from mix shift
items.quote: FDC already -- last year, if you see the last 3 quarters, the FDC demand or the FDC sales had increased proportionately higher. So what happened is that it's already building the base. Therefore, we don't see any further improvement in EBITDA because of any proportion change towards FDC.

items.statement: Green coffee prices volatile at INR3,300-3,800 range due to Brazil supply and El Nino impact on Vietnam crop
items.quote: As far as the green coffee prices are concerned, they are right now range about between INR3,300 to INR3,800, but there is a certain amount of volatility that still exists owing to simultaneously bearish and bullish factors claimed.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR963 crores as of June 2026, targeting gross debt reduction to INR1,000 crores and net debt to INR800 crores
items.quote: The net debt as at 30th June has further come down to INR963 crores. This is sub-1,000 levels. So a reduction of close to INR100 crores from the last quarter.

items.statement: Term loan repayment schedule: INR140 crores in next 3 quarters, INR200 crores in FY28, balance INR160 crores thereafter
items.quote: We have around INR517 crores of term loan outstanding as of now. Out of that, INR140 crores will get paid in the next 3 quarters, which means we are left with close to INR360 crores of debt, which will be -- out of INR360 crores, INR200 crores will be paid in FY28.

items.statement: B2C consumer business targeting 25-30% growth in FY27
items.quote: B2C will be around 25% growth that we are looking at 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Domestic branded business maintaining 5-6% EBITDA margins, reinvesting for growth rather than milking profits
items.quote: What we said is that the 5%, 6% EBITDA margins that we are running on this business, we will keep it at those levels instead of focusing on milking it right now because we foresee that there is still a lot of growth that can be achieved.

items.statement: Logistics costs remain volatile with no clear trend, facing cost impacts from shipping and packaging price fluctuations
items.quote: So there -- again, just like coffee prices, even the logistics has been a little wibbly-wobbly. There has been phases of a week where things started to settle down. For example, when the ceasefire got announced, then we saw some stability coming. Again, in the last week, 10 days, there has been again certain instabilities.

items.statement: Malgudi snacks rollout expanded with new products, targeting a couple of crores revenue in FY27
items.quote: Maybe a couple of crores is what we are looking to right now build this year, considering we are still keeping it focused into some areas.

items.statement: Percol UK turned around at INR26-27 crores revenue, expanding to US and Middle East markets
items.quote: Percol U.K. has turned around. We -- last year, we closed at around INR26 crores, INR27 crores of top line. We are likely to kind of keep growing on that front.

items.statement: Long-term volume growth target of 15% for next 3-5 years, capacity not a constraint with brownfield expansion capability
items.quote: We believe that, yes, next 2 years, it may not be required. But if at all, we feel that the growths are going ahead or things like that, we will definitely make sure that we end up either putting the capacity ourselves or doing some strategic tie-ups, which helps us to augment our capacity.

items.statement: Credit growth guidance maintained at 12-14% for FY27
items.quote: On the credit growth, continue to have the same guidance of 12 to 14% growth.

items.statement: Deposit growth guidance maintained at 10-12% for FY27
items.quote: The deposit growth, continue to have the same guidance of 10 to 12% growth.

items.statement: CD ratio guidance maintained at 84-86% for FY27
items.quote: The CD ratio will be happy to operate within 84 to 86%.

items.statement: Net interest margin guidance maintained at 2.75-2.95% for FY27
items.quote: The net interest margin would be again at the same band of 2.75 to 2.95 %.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained below 0.6% for FY27
items.quote: Credit cost below 0.6 %.

items.statement: Slippage ratio guidance maintained at 1-1.25% for FY27
items.quote: The slippages again would be the same guidance of 1 to 1.25%.

items.statement: Global NIM at 2.77% and domestic NIM at 2.93% for Q1 FY27, within guidance band
items.quote: The margin for the bank is global at 2.77% and the domestic at 2.93%, which is in line with our guidance of 2.75 to 2.95%.

items.statement: Plan to raise INR 6,000 crore Tier 2 bonds in FY27
items.quote: we intend to raise roughly 6,000 crores of Tier 2 in this year.

items.statement: Plan to raise INR 8,500 crore equity by March 2028
items.quote: One is a raising 8,500 crore of equity in a medium term, that is March 2028.

items.statement: Target to raise USD 4-5 billion via FCNR, MTN, and OFCB by December 2026
items.quote: we anticipated that we'll be raising something around 4 to 5 billion in terms of all the three instruments, FCNR, MT N, and also on the

items.statement: Raised USD 700 million via FCNR so far, expect to cross USD 1 billion by July end
items.quote: as of today on FCNR, we have raised almost close to 700 million now and possibly by month end, we'll be crossing 1 billion now.

items.statement: Plan to raise up to USD 1 billion via dollar bonds, board approved mandate to exceed if pricing favorable
items.quote: Out of that, through the bond route, actually we are expecting 1 billion as of today. But depending upon the opportunity and the pricing, we can upsize that.

items.statement: NMC settlement of USD 600 million paid July 1, 2026, fully absorbed in Q1 FY27 P&L
items.quote: The liability of the Bank in these proceedings is limited to the sum of USD 600 million, which was paid on 1st July 2026. The settlement amount has been debited to the profit and loss account for the quarter ended 30th June 2026.

items.statement: ECL migration may add 15-20 bps to credit cost, within current guidance of below 0.6%
items.quote: the impact on the credit cost can be in the range of around 15 to 20 bps on the credit cost. My credit cost as on June is 0.29 %. And my guidance is always below 0.6%.

items.statement: Hiring plan of 7,000 employees in FY27, added 260 branches in FY26
items.quote: this year also there is a plan to almost hire 7,000 headcounts.

items.statement: FY27 global advances growth guidance 15-16% and global deposits growth 13-14%
items.quote: Against this backdrop, our guidance for FY27 stays unchanged – global advances to grow by 15-16%, and global deposits by 13-14%.

items.statement: FY27 ROA guidance 1% and above on consistent QoQ basis
items.quote: Our guidance continues to remain the same that we would want to have a 1% and above ROA in FY27 on a consistent basis QoQ basis.

items.statement: FY27 global NIM guidance 2.55% to 2.60%
items.quote: But our guidance for the global NIM is somewhere around 2.55 % to 2.60% for FY27.

items.statement: FY27 cost to income ratio guidance 48-49% on consistent basis
items.quote: But , during FY27 we should be somewhere around 48 % - 49% on a consistent basis.

items.statement: ATM rationalization reduced count by 300 as part of cost optimization
items.quote: Yes, we have rationalized some of the ATMs. Our ATMs are both in the OPEX and the CAPEX model. So, in some of the Cap ex models, where we've thought that these A TMs were running into losses, much hits were not there. So, there we have clearly moved out of those ATMs.

items.quote: If I tell you the corporate and the international book, the pipeline is somewhere around 70,000 crores. items.quote: Global NIM stood at 2.52% in Jun'26 against 2.55% in Jun'25.

items.quote: RAM advances increased by 19.75% YoY from Rs. 3.28 lakh crore in Jun'25 to Rs. 3.93 lakh crore in Jun'26 constituting 58.30% of Advances in Jun'26.

items.quote: As regards the gold loans are concerned, we have a book of somewhere around Rs. 57,000 crores as on the 30th of June and the yield in that is more than 9% somewhere around 9.10%.

items.quote: So as far as the SMA numbers are there, if you see our 5 crore and above SMA numbers, our SMA has now come down to 409 0 odd crores which is only 0.52% of our standard book which was around 4700 crores as on 31st March 2026 and more than 7000 crores as on 30th June 2025.

items.quote: So put together , we will be somewhere around 4.2 billion by the end of the 31st of December with FCNR, OFCB, MTN and the ECB which is there.

items.quote: The target which we have set is to have a credit card base of 3 lakh by end of the FY27.

items.quote: So as far as that scheme is concerned, we have already sanctioned somewhere around 6,000 crores under the ECLGS scheme out of which 4,600 crores has already been disbursed and we expect that by the time the scheme comes to an end, we feel that around 8,000 crore of sanctions and disbursal will be able to do.

items.statement: International business crossed Rs 2.56 lakh crore; 32% trade finance, shifting to higher-margin corporate lending

items.statement: EBIT target of 15% now expected a couple of quarters into FY28, delayed from original Q4 FY27 aim due to slower revenue ramp

items.statement: Semiconductor business breakeven expected in FY28, with high voltage product development consuming cash for next 4-5 quarters
items.quote: Now, in terms of breakeven, it looks like breakeven will happen only in FY28 and if you look at a gross level it has a very healthy gross margin.

items.statement: DLM closed Q1 FY27 at highest ever order book with book-to-bill ratio in excess of 1.5
items.quote: Our order book momentum there continues to be a strong anchor for our confidence, with the quarter closing at the highest ever order book, supported by a strong order inflow and a book-to-bill ratio of in excess of 1.5.

items.statement: DET order intake up 5.3% YoY in Q1 FY27; new business EN and NN grew 64% YoY and 49% QoQ; five large deals won in last two quarters; pipeline over $300M

items.statement: DET capex higher in Q1 FY27 due to cyclical IT system refresh and project ramp-up
items.quote: Also, you will notice that the capex spending this quarter is a little bit higher, which is reflective of the cyclical IT system refresh and a project ramp-up.

items.statement: Semiconductor financing closed with EAAA at $500M post-money valuation; $30M fresh capital raised via debt and equity

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 21.7%; operating margin at 17.5% impacted by forex loss and receivables provision

items.statement: Target to increase capacity utilization by 10-20 percentage points by end of FY27, aiming to exit at 70-75% from current ~60%

items.statement: Plan to grow sales volumes by 5-7% per quarter, targeting 15-20% cumulative volume growth by end of FY27
items.quote: So, every quarter we intend to grow by 5% to 7%. So, at the end of the last quarter, we would have grown by 15% to 20%.

items.statement: New 40,000 MT oleochemical plant to start trial runs in Q2 FY27; margins expected to be better than current levels
items.quote: We are going to start the trial run. So, once that is stabilized, then we will ramp up the capacity.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 10.14% in Q1 FY27; management expects current margin levels to sustain and sees operating leverage benefits from higher utilization
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 18 crores with EBITDA margin of 10.14%.

items.statement: Realizations increased ~25% from Q4 FY26 and ~30% from Q1 FY26 due to reduced Chinese dumping, supply chain constraints, and rupee depreciation; cost pass-through successful
items.quote: Realization from Q4 has gone up by around 25% and from Q1 it has gone up by 30%.

items.statement: Seeing strong export enquiries from 7-8 large global customers seeking supply chain diversification; export revenue currently 7-8% of total
items.quote: Around 7 to 8 big customers.

items.statement: Isostearic acid (4% of revenue) ramping slowly due to stringent cosmetic industry qualifications; expect commercial breakthroughs by end of FY27 at a couple of customers
items.quote: At a couple of companies, we have finished all five steps. At a couple of companies, we are at the fourth step.

items.statement: New oleochemical product (non-EV battery) to launch next quarter from in-house R&D; will improve dimer acid plant utilization
items.quote: Next quarter, we will be introducing one new raw material. Again, for the first time, we will be manufacturing that particular product.

items.statement: Management refuses long-term volume contracts without price commitment; geopolitical situation (Middle East) significantly impacts competitive dynamics

items.statement: R&D spend ~Rs 50 lakh revenue expense (1-1.5% of sales); capex on need basis; focus on difficult-to-manufacture niche oleochemicals
items.quote: It's around 50 lakhs is only spent on the revenue side. The salary and the capital expenditure is on need-based basis.

items.statement: Target to achieve 25% blended EBITDA margin over next few years

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 468 bps YoY to 23.04%; PAT margin near 13%
items.quote: Our EBITDA stood at INR33.5 crores, which is up by 116% on a year-on-year basis with margins expanding by 468 basis points as compared to the same quarter in last year to 23.04%.

items.statement: Flexible hose margins 16-20%, assemblies 22-26%; blended around 22-23% this quarter
items.quote: So, when we sell the flexible hose just in the hose form, margins range between 16% to 20%. And when we sell the assemblies, the margins range anywhere between 22% to 26% margins.

items.statement: Fire hose assembly margins range 23-26%
items.quote: The fire hose assemblies has margins ranging between 23% to 26%.

items.statement: Expect international skid assembly business this financial year; international potential multifold vs India
items.quote: Yes. So, we are definitely on track. And in this financial year, we'll definitely have business coming in from international market.

items.statement: Skid assemblies contributed INR32.4 crores (23% of revenue) in Q1 FY27; volume 1,040 units
items.quote: Revenue from SFN Skid Assemblies reached INR32.4 crores in this quarter, which is contributing to approximately 23% of the total revenue.

items.statement: Flexible hose assembly split: 63% assemblies/fittings, 37% plain hose in Q1 FY27
items.quote: In this quarter, approximately 66% of the business was through -- 63% of the business was selling of the fittings and assembly products and about 37% of the business was selling the flexible hose, so 63% and 37%, yes.

items.statement: Skid capacity expanded from 6,000 to 9,000 units/annum; target 15,000 by Q3 FY27

items.statement: Flexible hose capacity expansion from 17.5 to 20 million meters/annum to complete by Q3 FY27
items.quote: On the flexible hoses vertical, we have planned to increase the production from 17.5 million meters per annum currently to 20 million meters per annum and it should be completed by Q3 of this financial year.

items.statement: Flexible hose segment peak revenue potential INR650-675 crores at 70% assembly mix and peak utilization
items.quote: With the -- at the peak utilization and assuming that 70% of the sales comes in from the assemblies, we are looking at a top line of anywhere between INR650 crores to INR675 crores.

items.statement: Logistics costs increased significantly in Q1 due to West Asia crisis impacting margins sequentially
items.quote: Also to add to that, just because the -- barring the material cost in the last -- in the Q1, if you also would see that logistics cost also has increased because of the crisis that has happened in West Asia.

items.statement: About 40 skids per megawatt of liquid-cooled IT load on average
items.quote: About 40-odd skids go into 1 megawatt on an average.

items.statement: FY27 loan growth guidance of 22% and FY29 loan book target of INR 16,000 crores plus
items.quote: As we look forward, the momentum of the first quarter marks an important step towards Vision 2029 and making us well positioned to achieve the target FY29 loan book of INR16,000 crores plus and 22% growth in FY27.

items.statement: ROA target of 1.35-1.4% for FY27 and 1.6% plus by FY29; ROE target 15% plus by FY29
items.quote: We expect further ROTA expansion and targeting to make it towards 1.4% in FY27 and 1.6% plus by FY29 and ROE expansion to 15% plus by FY29.

items.statement: NIM improved to 4.21% in Q1 FY27 from 4.06% in Q4 FY26 driven by deposit repricing and higher CD ratio
items.quote: Net interest margin has improved to 4.21% against 4.06% in the previous quarter and 4.06% a year ago. The same is supported by a decline in the deposit cost on repricing, coupled with acceleration in the CD ratio.

items.statement: GNPA improved to 2.47% (down 28 bps YoY, 7 bps QoQ); NNPA improved to 1.14% (down from 1.24% QoQ, 1.39% YoY); PCR improved to 54.5%; SMA 1&2 at 4.78% (down from 5.47% YoY)
items.quote: Asset quality, showing consistent improvement during the quarter with gross NPA improved to 2.47%, improved by 28 basis points and by 7 basis points on year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter basis respectively. Net NPA has also improved significantly and now stood at 1.14%.

items.statement: Branch network expanded to 216 branches across 5 states and 2 UTs; focus on semi-urban and rural markets
items.quote: As of June '26, our branch network expanded to 216 branches across 5 states and 2 union territories, strengthening our presence in rural and semi-urban markets.

items.statement: Average CD ratio at 83% in Q1 FY27; targeting mid-to-high 80s over next 2-3 years to drive NIM expansion
items.quote: We are presently reporting an average CD ratio of 83%. And as we discussed over the last couple of calls, we intend to take it to the mid- to high 80s.

items.statement: Opex at 2.95-2.98% in Q1 FY27; expected to improve in FY27 as salary increments annualize and business scales; larger opex leverage expected in FY29
items.quote: Typically, current quarter, we're seeing at around 2.95% to 2.98% levels. That is the opex in the current quarter. I'm seeing an improvement in the coming period for this.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; capital adequacy at 21.6% provides ample headroom for growth
items.quote: Our balance sheet remained well capitalized and liquid. The capital adequacy ratio stood at 21.6%, providing sufficient headroom to support the future growth.

items.statement: Management does not provide guidance and will not change this approach.
items.quote: We do not chase growth. That does not pay for itself. And as some of you have noticed in the past, occasionally with some frustration, we do not give guidance. We would rather you judge us by terms of what we do rather than what we promise.

items.statement: Core profit after tax (with DAC, without discounting and mark-to-market) fell 5% YoY to INR190 crores.
items.quote: So when we look at it from that perspective, our profit after tax with DAC, but without discounting and mark-to-market is INR190 crores compared to INR200 crores a year ago. This is a drop of 5%.

items.statement: Combined ratio (NEP with DAC) worsened to 107.2% from 104.3% with discounting.
items.quote: Combined ratio is 107.2% with DAC and 104.3% with discounting. So you can actually see the difference between the 2 numbers also is roughly about 3%.

items.statement: Loss ratio increased to 73.3% from 70.3% YoY, driven by private car own damage.
items.quote: the essential increase is happening because loss ratio has increased from 70.3% in the first quarter to 73.3%.

items.statement: Motor market share fell to 5.6% from 6.25% due to corrective actions in private car and commercial vehicles.
items.quote: our motor market share is now 5.6%. This compared to Q1 last year or compared to the whole of '25-'26 against 6.25% for the whole year.

items.statement: New business in 2-wheeler grew 26% YoY with collected premium of INR546 crores.
items.quote: New business in 2-wheeler has grown by 26% in Q1, and our collected premium is INR546 crores against INR433 crores last year, an increase of INR113 crores in premium income.

items.statement: Fire business de-grew 37% vs industry de-growth of 27-28% to protect gross loss ratios for reinsurers.
items.quote: if you look at the fire business, industry has -- if I remember, industry has de-grown by minus 27%, 28%. We have de-grown by 37%.

items.statement: Third-party loss ratio stable at 66.6%; reserving includes legal inflation and wage hikes; no separate provision for Supreme Court ruling yet.
items.quote: On the TP, our loss ratio is 66.6%, similar to what it was, broadly stable. Third party, as we have always said, is a long-tail business, and we read it on a full year basis, not any single quarter.

items.statement: Aggressive claim settlement on homemaker claims underway; conservative reserving maintained; no bet on judicial outcomes.
items.quote: We will go out and aggressively settle homemakers compromises, particularly or specifically, we anyway settle, as I gave you a number, 83% of the claims on the TP side.

items.statement: Equity allocation increased to 9.5% of AUM with INR268 crores unrealized gains; fixed income duration raised to 4.9 years.
items.quote: Now we are sitting at 9.5% in this period, and on top of it, we are sitting at an unrealized gains of INR268 crores.

items.statement: Dividend possible on IGAAP basis given 242% solvency; decision pending RBC norms and board approval in Q4.
items.quote: Based on where we are on IGAAP profitability, we can easily pay dividend because our solvency justifies it. And it will go up hopefully every quarter. By how much, we don't know. So I think all we are doing is waiting for the RBC norms to come.

items.statement: Motor TP rates unchanged for 5 years; 90-95% of vehicles need a hike; management not waiting for hike to act.
items.quote: On a thumb rule, I would say 90%, 95% of the vehicles should see a hike in TP. But the question is, should we wait for it in the hope that it will increase this month, that month or you say right now, it increase hasn't happened and we'll go and run our business on that basis.

items.statement: Gross written premium down 8% YoY; excluding reinsurance inward in health and crop, de-growth is ~2% similar to industry.
items.quote: On the gross written premium, we are down by 8%. Now most of it is actually coming in because we -- the drop in the reinsurance inward business, essentially in health and crop, so group health and crop, where pricing was unattractive.

items.statement: Solvency strong at 2.43x (IGAAP); IFRS net worth INR8,200 crores vs INR7,600 crores at March 31.
items.quote: Solvency is very strong at 2.43 times and this obviously plays in terms of the optionality we have. But there is one number here, which is actually going the other way. And that number is net earned premium.

items.statement: Long-term advance premium stands at INR3,387 crores (Motor INR2,879 crores, Non-motor INR508 crores).
items.quote: Long-term advance premium now stands at INR3,387 crores. Motor is INR2,879 crores and non-motor is INR508 crores.

items.statement: Group health loss ratio elevated due to one large bank-driven personal accident policy with high intimations.
items.quote: what happened this quarter is that we have a fairly large bank-driven personal accident policy where claims get intimated. A lot of these claims get repudiated over a period of time. So this quarter, the group level PA is essentially looking elevated because of one single large PA policy.

items.statement: Management confident of delivering 35-40% AUM growth in FY27
items.quote: Based on the strong momentum we have built, we remain confident of delivering AUM growth of 35% to 40% growth during the current financial years.

items.statement: Targeting ROA of 3.5% for FY27 driven by higher-yield product mix
items.quote: Yes. So, we are targeting around 3.5% ROA for the FY27.

items.statement: Net interest margin expected to remain in 13-14% range for FY27
items.quote: So eventually net interest margin will remain in the range of 13% to 14%.

items.quote: And we are in a process of raising the capital. By September or latest by October, we will raise INR100 crores to for to manage our further growth and expansion.

items.quote: And we are expecting that by end of this year it should be reach around 77% to -- 75% to 77%.

items.quote: So that will -- whenever need is arising, company is spending. And as far as total percentage of the entire expense is concerned, so it will remain what we are spending today, morely in the similar range only.

items.quote: On the funding side, our average cost of borrowing currently stands at 10.86%.

items.quote: During the period, disbursement grew by 37% year-on-year to INR226 crores, reflecting a strong demand across the core vehicle finance portfolio and continued execution across existing market.

items.statement: Declared first interim dividend of INR0.25 per share (face value INR10) for FY27
items.quote: Further, the company declared first interim dividend of INR0.25 per equity shares on a face value of INR10 each for the financial year '26, '27, reflecting our continued commitment towards shareholders value creation.

items.statement: Battery replacement finance launched at INR60,000 ticket size for existing e-3W customers, with OEM tie-ups
items.quote: Yes. So, this is INR60,000 ticket size product. And basically after 15 months of utilization of three-wheeler, generally battery starts giving some issues and eventually the entire vehicle goes into that kind of situation where they generally, it becomes a non-performing asset.

items.statement: MSME LAP ticket size INR8-20 lakhs targeting shop-owning businessmen
items.quote: And the ticket size will be around will start from INR8 lakhs to INR20 lakhs. We are talking about the MSME LAP, right? So INR20 lakhs will be the highest loan which we are going to provide to the customers.

items.quote: we are estimating to get a turnover of around INR130 crores to INR150 crores somewhere in between for this financial

items.quote: I increased the MRP by another INR10 to INR12 and started giving this technology for free

items.quote: out of the INR100 crores more than 40% has been recovered by July and August. By October-November, 90% of the receivables will be recovered

items.quote: We are targeting an AUM growth, as we had said in the guidance, between 25% to 30% for this year.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 3.5-4% for FY27
items.quote: Our guidance on credit cost was, and at the beginning of the year we had given a guidance of 3.5% to 4%, and this appears well within our grasp now.

items.quote: From a NIM perspective, the guidance that we had given, we expect to stay on target.

items.quote: We did realize that quarter 1, quarter 2 we might be out of those bands and quarter 3, quarter 4 we will be very much in the band giving a result which for the entire year should be in that band.

items.quote: From an order book Stand point, would be around 25% composite and 75% metallics.

items.quote: Oh, the export order books are not very strong. We don't have long term export order book. Right. So, export order book is predominantly on ATC division which I said where of the order book of thousand crores it's 90%.

items.quote: We are going to have I think 150 crores worth of land building being built. Building basically land is of course our own. So, building being built up for ATC and this, the timeline for this is over at least 18 to 24 months.

Of last year
