items.quote: stay at around 5.75% to 6% for this year. But in a steady state, this number should drop somewhere close to about 5.25% to 5.5%. But that will happen more -- 5.25% to 5.5% in a steady -state scenario, but that will happen more from FY 28 onwards and not during this financial year

items.statement: Write-offs guided at INR 225-250 crores for FY27
items.quote: We should be seeing write-offs for the full year at somewhere around INR225 crores to INR 250 crores, which is largely the run rate that we did in the first quarter.

items.statement: Incremental cost of borrowings guided at ~8.5%
items.quote: please bake in an 8.5% incremental cost of funds going forward, not the current levels.

items.statement: Expense growth of 20-21% YoY expected for FY27
items.quote: On a year-on-year basis, Nischint, I think it will largely track what you saw in the first quarter. So we are expecting somewhere around 20% to 21% growth compared to last year's numbers.

items.statement: No dearth of demand in the segment; demand was never a problem
items.quote: The first point to keep in mind is there is no dearth of demand in this segment which is something that we have been consistently reiterating. The demand was always there.

items.statement: NIM flat; spread improved by 3 bps due to cost of funds dropping 15 bps vs yield drop of 12 bps
items.quote: Our yields continue to remain consistent in line with the drop in yields that we did about a couple of years back. You will see about 10-15 basis points of reduction in yields on a quarterly basis. So there was a 12 basis points drop in our yields. However, this was more than compensated by the drop in the average cost of funds, which dropped by about 15 basis points, resulting in a spread of 3 ba

items.statement: Yield on assets ~22.5% in Q1; expected to settle around 22.25% after 10-15 bps further compression
items.quote: In fact, for Q1, if you look at it, we are at less than 22.5%. And today, we are onboarding loans at close to 22.5%. And given some adjustments for the NPA interest reversals, th is number should largely settle around the 22.25% is our thought. So maybe you will see this contraction of another 10-15 basis points for the next couple of quarters, should settle somewhere around the 22.25

items.statement: Cost of funds on book reduced from 8.95% to 8.80% QoQ; all-inclusive cost at 8.33%
items.quote: On the borrowing front, our all -inclusive cost was at 8.33% despite not so favou rable liquidity conditions. This has also helped bring down our cost of fund on the book from 8.95% for Q4 to 8.80% for the Q1 this year.

items.statement: Quarterly disbursements at INR 1,496 crores, up 23% QoQ and 16% YoY; AUM at INR 13,722 crores, up 4% QoQ
items.quote: We clocked our historical best in disbursement with quarterly disbursements coming in at INR 1,496 crores, a growth of 23% over the previous quarter and 16% over the previous year. We ended the quarter with an AUM of INR 13,722 crores, which is a sequential growth of 4% for the quarter.

items.statement: Active loan customers crossed 500,000 as of June 30
items.quote: During this quarter, one other milestone that we crossed is to achieve 500,000 active loan customers as on 30th June, which is a very significant milestone in the journey of the company.

items.statement: Unique customer collection efficiency 97.9% vs 98.1% QoQ; x-bucket collection 99.2% vs 99.3% QoQ
items.quote: For the quarter ended June 30, 2026, we clocked a unique customer collection efficiency of 97.9% versus 98.1% last quarter, with our x-bucket collections coming in at 99.2% versus 99.3% in previous quarter.

items.statement: Current book improved to 83.30% from 82.69%; 30+ book reduced to 12.38% from 12.69% QoQ
items.quote: On the result of this, our current book continues to improve and stood at 83.30% as compared to 82.69% as of previous quarter. We also saw a good improvement in our 30-plus book, which reduced to 12.38% as compared to 12.69% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Slippages flat at 0.70% QoQ; credit cost dropped to 1.85% from 1.88% QoQ
items.quote: Our slippages remained flat at 0.70% compared to the previous quarter. And despite the seasonally soft nature of this quarter, our credit cost dropped sequentially to 1.85% for Q1 financial year '27 from 1.88% for the Q4 financial year '26.

items.statement: Stage 3 provision coverage >40%; overall provision coverage ~1.8% of AUM
items.quote: Our provision coverage on the Stage 3 book continues to remain healthy at over 40%. And on the overall AUM, we are close to about 1.8% of provision coverage.

items.statement: Rollback rates: 4-5% in 1-30 and 31-60 buckets; 2-3% in 61-90 bucket
items.quote: generally, we see at least about 4% to 5% of rollbacks happening in the softer buckets. By that, we mean about the 31 to 60 and the 1 to 30 bucket and about 2% to 3% happening on the 61 to 90-day bucket.

items.statement: MFI overlap in customer portfolio trended down from 20-21% to 16-17%
items.quote: I think the number -- while we have not done it for this quarter, but it trended down from about 20%-21% to about 16%-17%.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity of 2x expected in 6-8 quarters (medium term)
items.quote: I would probably think it's in the medium term, maybe another 6 to 8 quarters from here onwards because it depends on the growth that we are looking at in the current product and also the newer product diversification we're thinking about.

items.statement: Holding INR 1,850 crores liquidity on balance sheet; raised INR 450 crores in Q1
items.quote: We are still holding close to INR 1,850 crores on the balance sheet. So it's still a sizable number. But the focus of the company will clearly be to ensure appropriate cost of funds.

items.statement: Target ticket size mix: 25% at ~INR 3 lakh, 50% at ~INR 5 lakh, 25% at ~INR 10 lakh
items.quote: we definitely want to operate at 25-50-20, which will be 25% at around INR3 lakh ticket size and 50% around the INR5 lakh ticket size and the other 25% closer to the INR10 lakh ticket size. So that's the kind of mix that we would be comfortable with.

items.statement: Average ticket size ~INR 4.5-5 lakh; will largely stay there
items.quote: The average ticket size is somewhere close to around INR 5 lakh -- INR4.5 lakh to INR5. It will largely stay there.

items.statement: Plan to launch one new product in next 3-6 months (beyond existing micro LAP and housing)
items.quote: we are very clearly thinking 2-3 products, out of that one product which we wanted to go first, maybe in next 3 months or 6 months. We will definitely get into one of the products because one of the learnings that what we have learned in this crisis is not to be in a single product.

items.statement: Energy cost increases and regulatory liquidity/price hike decisions are key monitorables for collections
items.quote: But I want everyone to keep 2 things in mind. One is on the energy cost, which has gone up, which may even go up. Second is on the liquidity front, what the regulator is going to take a call on the price hike. So these 2 things have to be kept in mind. But at current circumstance, we see no issues from a collections perspective.

items.statement: Institution not dependent on few individuals; strength demonstrated across metrics despite challenges
items.quote: This clearly shows the strength of the institution that we have built and re -establishes the fact that we are not an institution that is dependent on few individuals. The individual s may come and go, but the institution will go on forever.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 18-20% CAGR maintained
items.quote: We continue to maintain that we have a robust pipeline of sales where revenue will continue to be in the range of 18% to 20% CAGR.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 40-45% maintained with 40% threshold including Ascent by year end
items.quote: EBITDA margins will be in the range of 40% to 45%. We will maintain 40% threshold including Ascent by the end of this year.

items.statement: EBITDA growth visibility of 17-20% and PAT growth of 12-15% for FY27
items.quote: have visibility for EBITDA growth closer to 20 %, anywhere between 17% to 20%, and our PAT numbers anywhere between 12% to 15

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 34.2% including Ascent, 39.4% excluding Ascent in Q1 FY27
items.quote: If you look at EBITDA margins, EBITDA has gone up overall at 7.1% year-on-year and 5.1% quarter-on-quarter. And this is something which we continue to work upon where the margins have come down because of Ascent integration. But without Ascent integration, they are good at 39.4%, while with Ascent, it is 34.2%.

items.statement: Ascent EBITDA margin at 8.4% in Q1 FY27, targeting double digits within 12 months
items.quote: In terms of the margin of the entity itself, it had already turned the corner into the previous quarter, as you heard from the Q4 of the previous year. This year, too, it continues to be around 8.4% in terms of the EBITDA margin, and we believe that in quarters to come, we would expand that.

items.statement: Cost optimization initiatives initiated in Q4 expected to show sizable margin expansion from Q2 onwards
items.quote: Having said that, we have several strategic initiatives in terms of cost optimizations which we have initiated. Given there is a quarter delay in terms of fruition of those initiatives to show into the P&L, we expect Q2 onwards there should be sizable expansion on the margins.

items.statement: Mutual fund industry AUM grew ~15% YoY, KFin grew ~16% YoY with 100bps outperformance
items.quote: For the Q1, the industry had grown a little around 15% on the overall AUM, even as KFin Tech has grown a little over 16%, so it is 100 basis points fast growth at the overall AUM level.

items.statement: International business organic growth >32% YoY excluding Ascent, ~200% YoY including Ascent
items.quote: In terms of international business, obviously with the Ascent's expansion, we have grown nearly 200% year-on-year. Even if you exclude Ascent, just the KFin's organic business has grown over 32%.

items.statement: Won 6 new fund managers with >$100M AUM each at Ascent
items.quote: As I called out, what is probably the most heartwarming performance is the win of six mandates of fund managers who are above $100 million.

items.statement: Alternative investment funds count at 731 with 37.3% market share, approaching 40% including pipeline
items.quote: Our total consolidated count of the funds today is roughly around 731, and it occupies a share of about 37.3%. The wins that we have, which are yet to launch, if we add that, we believe that the market share will be closing in on 40%.

items.statement: Won 3 wealth management mandates in transition, targeting bank-based platform
items.quote: Very happy to inform you that we have won three mandates on this particular line of business, which are cur rently in the process of transition and deployment. items.statement: Signed tech deals worth ~INR 40 crore total top-line in Q1 FY27

items.statement: Large data lake deal worth INR 25 crore over 18 months signed with domestic entity
items.quote: have yielded us opportunity to bid and win a reasonably large investment management from a domestic-based entity’s big data solutioning mandate, which is over INR 25 crore turnover or the revenue to be booked into the next 18 months as the delivery will start

items.quote: The organization has, you know, we are to start our facility in Cayman Islands in terms of a substance requirement that has come through as a part of the regulatory requirements, which means that we are going to have feet on street in Cayman Islands as well.

items.statement: Yield declined 2% QoQ: ~30% from debt-to-liquid shift, ~70% from contract renewal provisions
items.quote: I think the debt-to-liquid is a substantive movement into the previous quarter. I think from a yield, the 2% impact that you have seen, about 30% of that impact is attributed to the movement from debt-to-liquid itself, okay, which then obviously means that it is about 1.7% is net of the asset class movement.

items.statement: Client discount provisions made but will negotiate hard due to infrastructure cost pressures
items.quote: See, we are now trying to balance in terms of high amount of cost being incurred on the infrastructure in terms of servers, routers, laptop. All of us know how the prices have gone up. items.statement: International fund split: ~1/3 each across hedge funds, private equity/venture, digital assets
items.quote: As is the case with the diversification geographically, it is the same in terms of the type of the funds as well. It is a near third equivalent splits between hedge funds, private equity, venture and the digital asset funds.

items.statement: NSE 500 market share at 50%, down from 52% due to market cap reduction
items.quote: Our market share on the NSE 500 company stands at 50%. There is a slight reduction in terms of the market cap reduction for some of the clients that we currently manage.

items.quote: Issuer solutions, we have added 670-odd clients into the previous quarter. Clearly, our intent of mini-SME IPOs beyond the main board IPOs is a slight detour in terms of our strategy into the previous year, where we wanted to drive for larger market share.

items.statement: Philippines BPI pension contract won last year, now pitching for large global pension RFPs
items.quote: Having won the BPI contract in the Philippines in the previous year, and also now pitching for large RFPs for pensions across the globe and not just within India.

items.statement: Philippines government contract identified as highest bidder but not yet awarded
items.quote: No, we have not announced any win. I mean, there was a media leak in terms of us being identified as the highest bidder in terms of both technical and commercials. So, to that extent, that is where it is right now. So, it is still under discussions with the client.

items.statement: Ascent revenue grew from $4.4M to $5.9M YoY (32% growth), $5.7M to $5.9M QoQ
items.quote: Ascent revenue increased on a dollar basis from US$5.7 billion in Q4 to US$5.9 million, and that was, as Sreekanth mentioned, more driven by the increase in corporate solutions and some new client wins that they have. items.quote: You have the presentation with you. We have shared. items.quote: We have a healthy cash and cash equivalents of INR 687 crores at the end of June. About INR 200 odd crores will get utilized towards payment of dividend, which has been declared by the board. And we still remain a cash accretive business where about 51% of the EBITDA gets converted into free cash flows.

items.statement: Dividend declared, ~INR 200 crore payout from cash reserves
items.quote: About INR 200 odd crores will get utilized towards payment of dividend, which has been declared by the board.

items.statement: Corporate actions tepid in Q2 due to IT services companies not declaring dividends, other sectors healthy
items.quote: I would even guide to slightly tepid corporate action movement into at least the next quarter, as you may have seen that several top-tier IT services companies have decided not to declare dividends, and that might change obviously within a quarter as well, but at this point in time, the visibility we have is that the corporate actions could be a little tepid into the Q2 based on the financial perf

items.statement: Digital asset fund AUM markdowns from crypto decline offset by new wins at Ascent
items.quote: As I said, the digital currency funds have seen a certain amount of write -downs, markdowns, because of the crypto value coming down quite a bit, as you might have tracked to it. obviously, that impacts the AUM and hence the overall revenue that you would get. items.statement: Cost of operations guidance: 25 bps reduction this year over 150 bps reduction since listing
items.quote: Cost of operations have been calibrated in a downward sloping curve and we continue our guidance of a 25-basis point reduction this year over the 150-basis point reduction we've delivered since listing.

items.statement: Spreads improved 39 bps to 9.4% driven by lower cost of borrowing and better asset pricing
items.quote: Capital allocation discipline helped us protect spreads, which improved by 39 bps at 9.4% driven by both a lower cost of borrowing and better pricing on the asset side.

items.statement: NIMs moved up by similar basis points as spreads to 10.6%
items.quote: NIMs moved up by a similar basis point as spreads and stood at 10.6% even as absolute borrowings increased, proof that growing the balance sheet and protecting the margin aren't mutually exclusive, just occasionally in tension.

items.statement: AUM grew 6% Q-o-Q and 27% Y-o-Y to INR 11,922 crores
items.quote: AUM grew 6% for the quarter at 27%-odd for the full year at INR 11,922 crores.

items.statement: MSME disbursements rose 3% Q-o-Q to INR 809 crores
items.quote: MSME disbursements rose 3% Q-o-Q to INR 809 crores.

items.statement: Co-origination mix reset to 10% following revised guidelines, expected to return to usual run rate from current quarter
items.quote: Following the revised guidelines, the co-origination mix reset to 10%. This has since stabilized and we expect a return to the usual run rate from this quarter onwards.

items.statement: Login to disbursal conversion moderated to 34% from 42% due to inflation denting disposable income
items.quote: We've seen this show up in our login to disbursal conversion which moderated to 34% from 42%.

items.statement: Sub-10 lakh segment showing signs of leveraged stress, average ticket size inching up due to shift from that segment
items.quote: The sub-10 lakh segment in particular is showing signs of leveraged stress and warrants close monitoring.

items.statement: Deliberate about pricing, walked away from some business to protect spreads
items.quote: We were deliberate about pricing through the quarter, which meant walking away from some business rather than chasing it at any cost.

items.statement: Added 5 branches in Q1, total 256 branches; plan 10-15 branches for FY27
items.quote: We added five branches during the quarter, bringing the total branch count to 256 as on June 2026.

items.statement: Opex at 4.29%, up 30 bps Y-o-Y but sequentially higher due to increments and branch costs; expect to reach 4% or below by year-end
items.quote: As the AUM grows on these set of branches, we will start to see the cost to average AUM coming down and we should be closer to 4% or below at the end of the year.

items.statement: 0+ DPD rose 70 bps in quarter, rollbacks better, expect stabilization this quarter and pullback in subsequent quarters
items.quote: On asset quality, 0+ rose by 70 bps during the quarter and that's our homework for the current quarter. The momentum on rollbacks is better and we should stabilize here for a quarter before a pullback in the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: GNPA improved 12 bps Y-o-Y to 2.66%, up 5 bps Q-o-Q; PCR at 42%
items.quote: NPAs improved 12 bps Y-o-Y to 2.66%, though up 5 bps sequentially.

items.statement: Stage 2 ECL increased to 16% from 6%, total provisioning at 1.91% of assets (2x regulatory minimum)
items.quote: As flagged in our last call, we took Stage 2 ECL up to 16% from 6%, bringing total provisioning to assets at 1.91% - The highest we've taken to date and roughly twice the regulatory requirement.

items.statement: Credit cost at 1.45%, expected to remain range-bound at 1.4-1.5% for next two quarters
items.quote: Our credit cost for the quarter is at 1.45%, we expect it to remain in this range in the short term.

items.statement: Cost of funds down 90 bps Y-o-Y to 8.42%; expect to stabilize at current levels
items.quote: Our cost of borrowing for the quarter is at 8.42% which has reduced 90 bps Y-o-Y and 10 bps Q-o-Q.

items.statement: Upfronted borrowing, closing liquidity INR 1,864 crores; intend to keep higher liquidity as AUM grows to INR 15,000 crores
items.quote: we have upfronted borrowing seeing the macro environment and thus have a closing liquidity of INR 1,864 crores. As we grow towards INR 15,000 crores, we intend to keep higher liquidity on the balance sheet.

items.statement: ROE at 14.7%, ROA at 4.53%; PAT INR 130 crores, up 6% Q-o-Q and 29% Y-o-Y
items.quote: PAT stood at INR 130 crores, up 6% Q-o-Q and 29% Y-o-Y, marginally outpacing book growth. That gap reflects the combined efficiency of risk-adjusted pricing, disciplined borrowing costs, and distribution, each working together. We close the quarter at 14.7% ROE

items.statement: New gold loan regulations effective April 1, 2026 reset eligibility norms, reducing loan amounts
items.quote: Second, gold prices were on a declining trend and with new regulations effective April 1st, 2026, resetting eligibility norms, the loan amount landing in customers' hands came down accordingly.

items.statement: RBI circular mandating banks not to accept collateral security for MSME customers within 20 lakh ticket size impacted co-origination (20% of disbursals/book)
items.quote: Third, the regulator's circular mandating banks not to accept collateral security for MSME customers within the 20 lakh ticket size had a direct bearing on our co-origination which accounts for roughly 20% of our disbursals and book.

items.statement: Competitors showing up with competitive pricing or generous loan amounts, adjusted footwork
items.quote: Lastly, a few birds strayed on the badminton court, by which I mean competitors showing up with competitive pricing or generous loan amounts which simply made us adjust our footwork.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM grew 11% Q-o-Q to INR 2,631 crores; gold yields contributed to yield improvement
items.quote: The loan against gold AUM is at INR 2,631 crores with a growth of 11% on Q-o-Q basis.

items.statement: Company yield range 17.50%-17.75%; Q1 yield 17.9% (up 29 bps Q-o-Q) due to gold portfolio performance
items.quote: That's our range where the yields generally stabilize. One good quarter of either product gives a 10-15 bps up and down. So, that's the range we will be at and which ensures that at say current cost of fund 10 bps up and down will give you a spread of more than 9

items.statement: Household DSR touching 14% (among highest globally); retail credit to GDP at 45%+; sub-10 lakh segment leveraged stress
items.quote: If you had seen the latest CLSA report, on the household DSR in India now almost touching 14%, and which is one of the highest in the world. So, while, people look at retail to GDP which also is now pushing 45% plus and is really high, but what is concerning is the DSR.

items.statement: Guidance unchanged on all fronts for coming quarter; preparing for unanticipated scenarios with anti-fragile approach
items.quote: Our guidance for the coming quarter remains unchanged on all fronts. No surprises there, birds on the badminton court notwithstanding.

items.statement: Employee cost increase due to increments and full-year impact of 20-25 branches opened in H2 FY26 plus 5 in Q1
items.quote: One obviously is the rollout of increment that has happened, that has one impact. The second is that the last quarter we opened close to 20-25 branches, again this quarter we've added five, so, all those employees that we've hired, full-blown cost has come in this quarter.

items.statement: Branches opened in last year need to become productive before further expansion; 60% of distribution from branches >67 crores AUM
items.quote: Now, these addition of branches have to actually start delivering the required returns before we add in any more branches.

items.statement: Top line expected to grow in line with stated guidance of mid-teens; FY27 EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY26
items.quote: Overall, we expect the top line to grow in line with the stated guidance of mid -teens. We will continue to invest behind our core brands, super-premium to luxury portfolio and organizational capabilities while maintaining FY27 EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY 26.

items.statement: Management reviewing mid-teens guidance upward to high teens and EBITDA margin of 18% over 2 years
items.quote: I would rather want to step it up from mid -teens, it may go even higher to high teens and an EBITDA margin of 18%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin expanded 277 bps to 46%; like-to-like gross margin 48.4% (up 522 bps) excluding supply chain impact
items.quote: Gross margin expanded by 277 basis points to 46%, supported by a favorable input cost environment and early benefits from backward integration despite the temporary impact of global supply chain disruptions.

items.statement: India-UK FTA expected to improve margins by 70-80 bps in FY27 and 130-140 bps in FY28
items.quote: We expect the benefit to flow in second half of the year and would lead to about 70 to 80 basis points improvement in current financial year. For FY28 on a full year basis, it would help us in improving margins by 130 to 140 basis points.

items.statement: Premiumization remains a structural trend; ABD outperformed industry in P&A (10.7% vs low single digits) and Mass Premium (2.3% vs stable)
items.quote: Importantly, ABD's volume performance was ahead of the industry where the P&A segment grew in the low single digits and Mass Premium and others remained broadly stable on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Prestige & Above segment contributed 48.2% of volumes and 59.3% of value in Q1 FY27 vs 46.2% and 55.8% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In Q1 FY '27, the Prestige & Above segment contributed 48.2% of volumes and 59.3% of value compared to 46.2% and 55.8% respectively in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: ICONiQ White grew 33.8% to 3.1 million cases in Q1 FY27; targeting ~15 million cases in FY27
items.quote: ICONiQ White continues to lead this momentum. The brand delivered 3.1 million cases in Q1 FY27 compared to 2.3 million cases in Q1 FY26 with a monthly average of 1 million plus cases resulting in a growth of 33.8% in the quarter on year -on-year basis.

items.statement: Launching deluxe vodka and premium whisky in H2 FY27 to fill white spaces
items.quote: There is a vodka market of 15 million to 18 million case s, where there is a brand leader which is unchallenged. It is a high contribution segment and now ABD can make foray into this space, this in H2 FY27. We will also come up with a premium Whisky in H2 FY 27 which will again be a uniquely packaged product with a new concept altogether.

items.statement: International footprint expanded to 39 countries in Q1 FY27 from 36 in Q4 FY26; exports asset-light with superior working capital efficiency
items.quote: ABD has expanded its footprint to 39 countries in Q1 FY 27 compared to 36 countries in Q4 FY 26, reinforcing our position as one of India's leading spirits exporters by volume.

items.statement: Telangana overdues ~₹400 crores; recent supplies paid on time, older overdues largely cleared, dialogue ongoing for price increase
items.quote: Overdue from Telangana government is approximate ₹400 crores. So right now, what's happening is Telangana is paying us well within agreed timeline for all recent supplies. Whereas for the overdue before 2024 has been paid up.

items.statement: Price increase dialogue ongoing with Telangana and 1-2 other states; guardrails built in case price hikes don't materialize

items.statement: Capex program to be funded through internal accruals and debt while maintaining leverage within defined framework
items.quote: Our capex program is planned to be funded through internal accruals and debt while maintaining leverage within our defined framework through the investment cycle.

items.statement: ABD Maestro FY26 revenue ~₹40 crores, expected to double in FY27; minimum 3-year gestation for luxury portfolio
items.quote: we clocked in FY 26 was top line of ~₹40 crores, which we expect to double in FY27. So that is an indication of how the business is moving forward. On the cost side, ABD Maestro being a luxury product vertical it is a minimum of a 3 -year gestation period when you will start seeing the fruits of labor

items.statement: Reiterated FY28 outlook of $400 million organic revenue and 40% EBITDA margins
items.quote: we really remain confident and are happy to reiterate our FY28 outlook of $400 million organic revenue as well as, EBITDA margins of 40%.

items.statement: US$100 million capex program 80% committed, mostly for drug device combination; biologics expansion later at significantly lower amount
items.quote: last year we mentioned we had taken about US$100 million capex to be invested across sites, most of it coming to drug device combination. As we sit today, almost 80% of that capex has been committed

items.statement: Order book visibility supports FY28 guidance across DDC, biologics, soft gel, and injectables with multiple new customers and markets
items.quote: the short answer to your question is yes. The little bit longer answer is that, we've got multiple pillars of that business, right? So yes, indeed drug device combination is going to be one of a very important contributor.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin improvement driven by mix shift to higher-margin drug device combination business and seasonal H2 weighting of base business
items.quote: it's basically the mix which is driving this. You know, the as you see there's a significant improvement in margins which primarily coming from higher contribution from the drug device combination business

items.statement: Demand for semaglutide generics significantly outpaces supply in Canada and India; customer forecasts remain robust
items.quote: The constraint in this market has been supply, not demand. In fact, the demand has been significantly outpacing supply both in the markets where the brand was present or was launching.

items.statement: Shift toward more commercial supply agreements (CSAs) vs MSAs as new DDC capacity comes online; first new GLP-1 customer added last quarter
items.quote: the lines are driven by the CSA. That's we have always said that the mix of the company is going to be driven by significantly more CSA.

items.statement: Injectable site shutdown in Q2 FY27 to add pre-filled syringe and lyophilization capacity; new capacity to contribute fully in FY28
items.quote: this first half itself, we will be taking a shutdown on our one of our sterile injectable sites basically to add this capacity. So, you will see, this addition will be a significant contributor to our FY28 numbers.

items.statement: EBITDA trajectory to continue upward beyond FY28 driven by biologics commercialization from FY29, Europe/US market entry, and capacity expansions
items.quote: One clear answer for you is that yes, our EBITDA trajectory will continue to go upward beyond FY28. And this is going to be dependent on all our modalities, which all our service offerings.

items.statement: Geopolitical issues increase freight time and cost but impact muted due to ex-works contracts; US tariff announcement seen as likely to follow pattern of changes and backdowns
items.quote: the geopolitics is in a flux, no doubt about that. Especially what is happening in the Middle East is in nobody's interest. So, for us also, typically it has impacted in terms of the freight challenges

items.statement: Biologics RFP funnel nearly 4x vs year ago across innovators, biosimilars, animal health; long-gestation but sticky business contributing beyond FY28
items.quote: our RFP funnel today is almost 4x of what it was just over a year ago. And this spans across innovators, biosimilars, as well as animal health companies.

items.statement: Biologics capacity expansion planned for both mammalian and microbial based on pipeline visibility; amount significantly lower than DDC capex
items.quote: we are also going to be taking some other capacity expansion because we see our current biologics capacity will require expansion. So, we are going to be expanding both the mammalian as well as microbial capacity.

items.statement: DDC lines fungible across customers/products; batch size increase from 200L to 500L possible in most geographies with quick regulatory timeline
items.quote: the lines what we have added, even when we had started this program of adding capacity, the idea was line, all lines should be able to cater to all our customers.

items.statement: DDC capacity fully utilized; injectables demand exceeds capacity; soft gel tech transfers underway to fill new capacity over 12-15 months
items.quote: the utilization of all our current capacity t here is complete. And similar function I can tell you for injectables because the reason we are adding so much lyophilization capacity is that, the demand today is higher than the capacity

items.quote: you will see this as a sequential quarter-on-quarter improvement in our revenue and in EBITDA.

items.statement: No anticipated supply impact from Dr. Reddy's temporary disruption due to diverse customer base and full capacity utilization; capacities sufficient for DRL resumption
items.quote: thanks to all these, we are able to actually pull demand into this quarter, therefore, which is what the timeline which Dr. Reddy's has shared publicly. And therefore, thanks to that we have had, we don't anticipate any impact on our supplies.

items.statement: 12 successful regulatory inspections and customer audits in Q1 including two surprise FDA audits across two sites
items.quote: We had 12 successful inspections this quarter across regulatory inspections and customer audits, including two surprise FDA audits across two of our sites.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 8% to 12% YoY for FY27

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR 140-160 crores for FY27
items.quote: On the capital expenditure side, we are on plan to use our IPO proceeds as per the stated objects therein, and we will probably maintain the range we have said earlier, about INR 140 crores to INR 160 crores per year of capital expenditure, even in this financial year.

items.statement: Won two multi-year PSU bank tenders worth INR 73 crores
items.quote: In this quarter, we won two multi-year tenders from leading PSU banks, which represent approximately INR 73 crores in revenue over the tender period.

items.statement: Gross margin moderated to 41.7% in Q1 FY27 from 44.5% in Q1 FY26 due to higher material costs
items.quote: Gross profit increased by 13.3% to INR 157 crores. Gross margin moderated to 41.7% in Q1 FY27 from 44.5% in Q1 FY26 as cost of materials consumed increased faster than revenue.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 135 bps YoY to 25.1% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter came in at INR 94 crores with an EBITDA margin of 25.1%, an increase of 135 bps Y-o-Y. Despite the pressure on gross margin, disciplined management of employee and other operating costs supported profitability.

items.statement: 40-45% of gross margin impact from currency, rest from war-driven commodity and logistics costs
items.quote: Now, right now probably the input costs that have impacted our cost of goods sold here in the first quarter are predominantly the entire war-related impact. Now, this has got probably two or three-fold impact. One is obviously the direct impact on the currency, and then there is an impact which is the outcome of the war in terms of the commodity pricing, the logistics, and the freight cost. So may

items.statement: Actively working with customers on price revisions to protect margins
items.quote: As of now, we operate in a challenging environment impacted by geopolitical uncertainties, currency fluctuations, and cost pressures. While these factors may create some near-term headwinds, we are actively working with customers on price revisions and taking steps to protect margins and maintain healthy profitability.

items.statement: Expect H2 FY27 stronger due to seasonal BFSI pickup and steady communication and IoT momentum
items.quote: Looking ahead, given the nature of our business, we expect H2 FY27 to be stronger driven by seasonal pickup in BFSI demand, and steady momentum in the communication and fulfillment businesses, and continued growth in the IoT segment.

items.statement: Bengaluru metal card facility expected operational by end of calendar year 2026
items.quote: We would like to update that our Nagpur and Bengaluru facilities are still under construction. We expect the Bengaluru facility to be operational by the end of the calendar year after the necessary regulatory approvals.

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization 65-70% on average, peaking at 85-90% during high demand periods
items.quote: Capacity utilization, typically for us, in our business currently is around 65% to 70%. Having said that, this also has a cyclical nature to it. So, typically, when customers have higher renewal cycle demands or there are month-end loads of customers, we also reach about 85% to 90% of our capacity utilization, but on average we tend to be in the 65% to 70% range.

items.statement: Order book stood at Rs 357.63 crore as of March 31, 2026, providing visibility beyond 24 months due to 3-5 year contract life cycles.
items.quote: As on 31st March 2026, our order books stood at Rs. 357.63 crores. Since our contracts are 3-5 years in life cycle, these order books provide visibility beyond 24 months.

items.statement: FY26 PAT margin improved to 10.5% from 7% in FY25; Q4 FY26 PAT margin improved to 15.1% from 8.7% in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: Profit after tax for the year stood at Rs. 24 crores, representing a robust 70% year-on-year growth, while PAT margin improved to 10.5% compared with 7% in previous financial year.

items.quote: I am also pleased to share that the Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of Rs. 0.5 per equity share for Financial Year 26, subject to shareholders' approval at the forthcoming Annual General Meeting.

items.statement: Strategy prioritizes continued investment in technology infrastructure, proprietary platforms, AI/ML capabilities, and skilled workforce for complex digital transformation programs.
items.quote: Looking ahead, our strategy remains focused on four key priorities: 1. Continue investing in strengthening our technology infrastructure and proprietary products and platforms. 2. Further enhance our capability in artificial intelligence and machine learning and other emerging technologies.

items.statement: One-time exceptional charge of Rs 2.7 crore recognized in FY26 for statutory impact of new Labor Codes.
items.quote: During the year, the company recognized a one-time exceptional charge of Rs. 2.7 crores towards the statutory impact of new Labor Codes. Excluding this one-time item, our profitability remained robust.
